title: Gurmukh, Equality, Sewa and the Sangat
subject: religious-studies-edexcel

cards.front: Name the five actions the lesson lists as marks of a gurmukh Sikh's life.
cards.answer: Regular Nam Japna / Sewa (selfless service) / Attending the gurdwara / Keeping Sikh discipline (Rahit) / Living in community (sangat)

cards.front: Name the three core duties of a Sikh given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Nam Japna (remembering God) / Sewa (service) / Kirat karni (honest work)

cards.front: According to Guru Granth Sahib 226, how is haumai overcome?
cards.answer: By contemplating the Guru's Shabad (word), which turns the soul toward God.

cards.front: How does the difference between Khalsa and non-Khalsa Sikhs affect their sewa and sangat?
cards.answer: Khalsa Sikhs practise sewa and sangat within the full discipline of the Rahit Maryada after initiation, while non-Khalsa follow the same core teachings without formal initiation, differing in commitment not spiritual worth.

cards.front: Name the five Jewish festivals described in the lesson.
cards.answer: Rosh Hashanah / Yom Kippur / Pesach / Shavuot / Sukkot

cards.front: Name the four stages of Jewish mourning described in the lesson.
cards.answer: Rapid community-organised funeral / Shiva / Avelut / Yahrzeit

cards.front: Why do many kosher kitchens keep two sets of pans and dishes?
cards.answer: Because Kashrut requires meat and dairy to be kept separate at all times.

cards.front: Why is an Orthodox Bat Mitzvah often marked differently to a Reform one?
cards.answer: Because Orthodox synagogues do not allow women to read the Torah during services, unlike Reform ones.

cards.front: Name the five key themes running through Silas Marner.
cards.answer: Community and belonging / Isolation and exclusion / Love versus money / Class and moral worth / Moral consequences

cards.front: What three fitting consequences does the lesson describe for Silas, Godfrey and Dunsey?
cards.answer: Silas rewarded with Eppie and community / Godfrey punished with childlessness and rejection / Dunsey dies in the stone-pit
items: Silas rewarded with Eppie and community
Godfrey punished with childlessness and rejection

cards.front: Why does Eliot use gold and Eppie as parallel symbols?
cards.answer: Both are golden and precious to Silas, but gold is dead metal that shrinks his world, while Eppie is alive and expands it.

cards.front: How does the stone-pit function as a symbol in Silas Marner?
cards.answer: It hides Dunsey's body and the stolen gold for sixteen years, showing that hidden wrongs always eventually surface.

cards.front: According to Genesis 1 and John 1 together, what three roles did the Trinity play in creation?
cards.answer: Father initiated creation / Son (the Word) was the agent through whom everything was made / Holy Spirit was present, hovering over the waters
items: Son (the Word) was the agent through whom everything was made
Holy Spirit was present, hovering over the waters

cards.front: After particular judgement, which three destinations can a soul be sent to?
cards.answer: Heaven / Hell / Purgatory (Catholic belief)

cards.front: Why do Christians believe resurrection is central to their faith?
cards.answer: Because Jesus himself was resurrected three days after his crucifixion, so without it their faith would be futile.

cards.front: How does belief in judgement affect how Christians live?
cards.answer: Because they believe God will judge them, they try to live morally, follow Jesus's teachings, help others and avoid sin.

cards.front: Name the five key computer specifications that affect DAW performance.
cards.answer: Operating system / RAM / Hard drives (SSD preferred) / Processor (CPU) / Display

cards.front: Name the five types of MIDI controller described in the lesson.
cards.answer: Keyboard controllers / Guitar controllers / Percussion controllers / Wind controllers / Control surfaces

cards.front: Why does more RAM improve performance when producing music in a DAW?
cards.answer: More RAM allows you to run more tracks, plug-ins and virtual instruments simultaneously.

cards.front: Why is a faster CPU important for DAW work?
cards.answer: A faster processor handles more real-time audio processing, effects and virtual instruments without stuttering.

cards.front: Name the six reflexive pronouns given in the lesson.
cards.answer: me (myself) / te (yourself) / se (himself/herself/oneself) / nous (ourselves) / vous (yourselves) / se (themselves)

cards.front: Name the four things the lesson lists under 'il ne faut pas' (you must not do) for health.
cards.answer: smoke cigarettes / vape / drink alcohol / eat too much fast food

cards.front: According to the lesson, how can smoking cigarettes affect a person's health?
cards.answer: Smoking cigarettes can cause illness or even death.

cards.front: According to the lesson, how can a bad diet affect a person?
cards.answer: A bad diet can cause a lack of energy.

title: Anglo-Saxon Resistance & the Harrying of the North
subject: history-edexcel

cards.front: Name the three underlying causes of resentment that remained in the north after the 1068 revolt.
cards.answer: Heavy taxation / Loss of land / Replacement of English lords with Normans
items: Replacement of English lords with Normans

cards.front: What were the four immediate impacts of the Harrying of the North?
cards.answer: Mass famine across the north / Refugees fled south or to Scotland / Centuries-old communities wiped out / Land values collapsed
items: Refugees fled south or to Scotland

cards.front: Why did William build castles at Warwick and Nottingham while marching north in 1068?
cards.answer: To demonstrate his power to Edwin, Morcar and the north as he advanced to crush their rebellion.

cards.front: How did William's forces finally get onto the Isle of Ely to end Hereward's rebellion?
cards.answer: After his causeway collapsed, the monks of Ely showed the Normans a secret path through the marshes.

title: Magnetism, Electromagnets and the Motor Effect
subject: separate-sciences-edexcel

cards.front: Name the four common magnetic materials given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Iron / Steel / Nickel / Cobalt

cards.front: Name the three ways to increase the strength of a solenoid's magnetic field.
cards.answer: Increase the current / Increase the number of turns per unit length / Insert an iron core
items: Increase the number of turns per unit length

cards.front: Why is an induced magnet always attracted to the permanent magnet that induced it, never repelled?
cards.answer: Because its poles align with the external magnetic field, so it is always pulled towards the magnet, not pushed away.

cards.front: Why are electromagnets, rather than permanent magnets, used in scrapyard cranes?
cards.answer: Switching off the current removes the magnetism, so the crane can pick up scrap metal then release it on demand.

cards.front: Name the six preterite forms of 'ir' (to go) in order (yo, tú, él/ella, nosotros, vosotros, ellos).
cards.answer: fui / fuiste / fue / fuimos / fuisteis / fueron

cards.front: What three tenses does the lesson say a strong holiday answer should combine?
cards.answer: present / preterite / conditional

cards.front: How can you tell if 'fue' means 'went' or 'was' in a Spanish sentence?
cards.answer: Context tells you which meaning is intended, since ir and ser share the same preterite forms.

cards.front: How do you form the conditional tense of a regular verb from its infinitive?
cards.answer: Add the endings -ía, -ías, -ía, -íamos, -íais, -ían to the infinitive.

title: Political and economic problems of the 1970s
subject: history-eduqas

cards.front: Name the four British industries the lesson says were losing competitiveness in the 1970s.
cards.answer: Steel / Shipbuilding / Textiles / Cars

cards.front: Name the three regions the lesson identifies as suffering long-term structural unemployment in the 1970s.
cards.answer: South Wales / North-east England / Clydeside in Scotland

cards.front: Why did the 1973 OPEC oil embargo hit Britain's economy so hard?
cards.answer: It quadrupled oil prices almost overnight, which was devastating for Britain as an oil-importing economy.

cards.front: Why was Callaghan's government forced to seek an IMF loan in 1976?
cards.answer: The pound had fallen sharply, forcing the government to borrow from the IMF and accept harsh conditions including spending cuts.

cards.front: According to the Duke, name the three ordinary pleasures the Duchess valued as much as his name.
cards.answer: A sunset / A cherry branch / A mule ride

cards.front: Name the three other poems the lesson compares 'My Last Duchess' with.
cards.answer: Ozymandias / Poppies / London

cards.front: Why does the Duke keep the painting of the Duchess behind a curtain?
cards.answer: It symbolises his control over who sees her, even in death, just as he controlled her in life.

cards.front: How does the poem's single, unbroken stanza reflect the Duke's character?
cards.answer: It shows the Duke monopolising the conversation, never letting the envoy interject, mirroring his desire to control everything.

cards.front: Name the four electronic instruments the lesson describes.
cards.answer: Electric guitar and electric bass / Synthesiser / Sampler / Drum machine

cards.front: Name the four types of DJ technology the lesson describes.
cards.answer: Turntables / CDJs / Mixer / DJ software

cards.front: Why do chromatic chord progressions sound surprising or tense compared to diatonic ones?
cards.answer: They include chords with notes from outside the key, creating surprise, tension or colour.

cards.front: How do dotted rhythms create a sense of energy and drive?
cards.answer: A dot after a note adds half its value, creating a long-short pattern.

title: The Milky Way and Other Galaxies
subject: astronomy-edexcel

cards.front: Name the four dominant galaxies of the Local Group other than the Milky Way.
cards.answer: Andromeda Galaxy (M31) / Large Magellanic Cloud / Small Magellanic Cloud / Triangulum Galaxy (M33)

cards.front: Name the three types of active galaxy described in the lesson.
cards.answer: Seyfert galaxies / Quasars / Blazars

cards.front: Why does the Milky Way band appear broader and brighter towards Sagittarius?
cards.answer: Because Sagittarius lies in the direction of the galactic centre, where the bulge concentrates far more stars.

cards.front: Why do blazars appear extremely bright and highly variable across all wavelengths?
cards.answer: Their relativistic jet points almost directly at Earth, so its emission is Doppler-boosted, making it appear far brighter.

title: Sustainable Energy: Renewables & a Local LIC Scheme
subject: geography-aqa

cards.front: Name the seven main renewable energy sources the lesson lists.
cards.answer: Biomass / Wind / Hydro / Tidal / Geothermal / Wave / Solar

cards.front: Name the three reasons the lesson gives for why fossil fuels still dominate energy use.
cards.answer: Very high energy density / Infrastructure already built / Reliable on demand

cards.front: Why does micro-hydro suit isolated mountain communities like those near Chambamontera?
cards.answer: Big national grids are too costly to build across mountains, so small local schemes are cheaper, easier to repair and fit the geography.

cards.front: Why did health improve in villages after the Chambamontera scheme was built?
cards.answer: Kerosene fumes, a major cause of respiratory illness, disappeared from homes once electricity replaced them.

title: Eschatology: Life After Death, Resurrection and Purgatory
subject: religious-studies-edexcel

cards.front: Name the four key elements of Catholic belief about what follows death.
cards.answer: Resurrection of the whole person / Judgment (particular and Last) / Heaven or Hell / Purgatory

cards.front: Name the two scriptural passages the lesson says anchor Catholic eschatology.
cards.answer: John 11:17–27 / 2 Corinthians 5:1–10

cards.front: Why do Catholics believe the whole person, body and soul, will be raised after death?
cards.answer: Because Jesus rose bodily from the dead, so Catholics believe all human beings will share in a resurrection of the body.

cards.front: Why do Catholics pray for the dead, such as at funerals and All Souls' Day?
cards.answer: Because it reflects the belief in purgatory, a state of purification after death for those who died in God's grace.

title: Research Methods: Questionnaires, Interviews and Observation
subject: sociology-aqa

cards.front: Name the five factors the lesson gives that shape a sociologist's choice of research method.
cards.answer: The research question / The population being studied / Practical constraints like time and cost / Ethical considerations / The theoretical perspective of the researcher
items: Practical constraints like time and cost
The theoretical perspective of the researcher

cards.front: Name the three types of interview by level of structure described in the lesson.
cards.answer: Structured interview / Unstructured interview / Semi-structured interview

cards.front: Why would a structured interview be inappropriate for researching women who left violent relationships?
cards.answer: Fixed questions might miss what matters most to participants, and the formal tone could feel clinical and discouraging when discussing trauma.

cards.front: Why do sociologists sometimes use semi-structured interviews as a compromise between structured and unstructured?
cards.answer: They use key themes for some comparability while still allowing the interviewer to probe and follow up for depth.

title: Practitioner Application: Brechtian Distance and Naturalistic Truth
subject: drama-aqa

cards.front: Name the three types of scene the lesson gives as candidates for Brechtian staging devices in Noughts and Crosses.
cards.answer: Interrogation scenes / School arrival scene / The execution scene

cards.front: Name the three scenes the lesson gives as candidates for Stanislavskian depth in Noughts and Crosses.
cards.answer: The beach scene / The hostage scene / The final letter

cards.front: Why did Brecht believe naturalistic theatre encouraged political passivity in audiences?
cards.answer: If audiences lose themselves in characters' emotions, he argued, they forget to think about the social structures producing those emotions.

cards.front: Why must the audience be kept slightly distanced from the world of Noughts and Crosses for its racial reversal to work?
cards.answer: Pure naturalistic immersion would make the reversed world feel alien, whereas Brechtian distance keeps the comparison to the audience's own world alive.

cards.front: Name the three things done to improve accuracy in the Hooke's Law investigation.
cards.answer: Take three readings and calculate the mean / Check for parallax by reading the ruler at eye level / Ensure the spring hangs freely without touching the stand
items: Take three readings and calculate the mean
Check for parallax by reading the ruler at eye level
Ensure the spring hangs freely without touching the stand

cards.front: List the four steps used to investigate Hooke's Law with a spring.
cards.answer: Clamp the spring vertically and measure original length / Add known masses one at a time, recording new length / Calculate the extension for each mass / Plot force against extension
items: Clamp the spring vertically and measure original length
Add known masses one at a time, recording new length
Calculate the extension for each mass

cards.front: Why is more than one force needed to stretch, bend or compress an object?
cards.answer: A single force would just make the object accelerate, so two opposing forces are needed to cause deformation.

cards.front: Why does carrying a box horizontally do no work against gravity?
cards.answer: Because the force (weight) acts downwards, perpendicular to the direction of motion, not along it.

cards.front: Name the four types of guidance a coach can use to communicate a skill.
cards.answer: Visual guidance / Verbal guidance / Manual guidance / Mechanical guidance

cards.front: Name the four types of feedback a performer can receive.
cards.answer: Intrinsic feedback / Extrinsic feedback / Concurrent feedback / Terminal feedback

cards.front: Why can visual guidance cause cognitive overload in beginners?
cards.answer: Showing too much visual information at once, like a full complex routine, is too much for a beginner to process.

cards.front: Why must mechanical guidance be phased out as a performer progresses?
cards.answer: The supported movement it creates is not identical to the natural, unsupported movement needed in real performance.

title: Edward's Inheritance: From Henry III to a New King
subject: history-aqa

cards.front: According to the lesson, what four problems were waiting for Edward I when he returned in 1274?
cards.answer: Corrupt local officials taking bribes and seizing land / Royal income too small for the king's ambitions / Magnates holding privileges that belonged to the crown / Llywelyn ap Gruffudd's unanswered challenge in Wales
items: Corrupt local officials taking bribes and seizing land
Royal income too small for the king's ambitions
Magnates holding privileges that belonged to the crown
Llywelyn ap Gruffudd's unanswered challenge in Wales

cards.front: What three things did the Provisions of Oxford (1258) impose on Henry III?
cards.answer: A council of fifteen barons to supervise the king / Regular parliaments / Reform of local government
items: A council of fifteen barons to supervise the king

cards.front: Why did the leading barons force Henry III to accept the Provisions of Oxford in 1258?
cards.answer: He had spent vast sums on foreign schemes like putting his son on the Sicilian throne and relied on unpopular foreign favourites.

cards.front: Why was Edward I confident no one would challenge his right to rule while he travelled slowly home in 1272–74?
cards.answer: He was already recognised as king from the moment his father died and returned as a famous crusader warrior, quietening thoughts of rebellion.

cards.front: Name the three things Godfrey offers Eppie when he tries to claim her as his daughter.
cards.answer: A fine house / An education / Social standing

cards.front: Name the three reasons Eppie gives for refusing Godfrey's offer.
cards.answer: She was raised in poverty / She loves her father (Silas) / She is engaged to Aaron Winthrop
items: She is engaged to Aaron Winthrop

cards.front: Why does the discovery of Dunsey's skeleton devastate Godfrey?
cards.answer: It is evidence of a crime tied to his own secrets, risking exposure of his hidden marriage and abandoned child.

cards.front: Why does Godfrey's concealment harm Nancy as well as Eppie?
cards.answer: It deprives both of the relationship they could have had, since Nancy would have raised Eppie if told the truth.

title: The Five Pillars, the Ten Obligatory Acts and Worship
subject: religious-studies-ocr

cards.front: Name the five acts that make up the Sunni Five Pillars.
cards.answer: Shahadah / Salat / Zakat / Sawm / Hajj

cards.front: Name the five daily prayers of Salah.
cards.answer: Fajr / Zuhr / Asr / Maghrib / Isha

cards.front: Why can everyday actions like eating or working count as acts of worship in Islam?
cards.answer: Because worship is defined by the sincere intention (niyyah) behind an act, so any action done with the right intention becomes worship.

cards.front: Why do businesses in Muslim-majority countries often close at midday on Fridays?
cards.answer: To allow Muslims to attend the obligatory Jummah congregational prayer held at midday on Fridays.

cards.front: Name the three forms of the possessive adjective 'my' in French, based on the noun's gender/number.
cards.answer: mon (masculine) / ma (feminine) / mes (plural)

cards.front: Name the four structures the lesson's model family paragraph combines to build a description.
cards.answer: avoir for hair and family members / être for personality and build / possessive adjectives (mon, ma) / the relative pronoun qui to add detail
items: avoir for hair and family members
the relative pronoun qui to add detail

cards.front: Why are 'his sister' and 'her sister' both translated as 'sa sœur' in French?
cards.answer: Possessive adjectives agree with the noun they describe, not the owner, and sœur is feminine, so both use sa.

cards.front: Why do you say 'mon amie' instead of 'ma amie' for 'my friend' (female)?
cards.answer: Before a feminine noun starting with a vowel, mon replaces ma for pronunciation reasons.

cards.front: Name the four reasons the lesson gives for why businesses promote.
cards.answer: Inform or remind customers about the product / Create or increase sales / Create or change the image of the product / Persuade customers to buy
items: Inform or remind customers about the product
Create or change the image of the product

cards.front: Name the five factors the lesson says shape a business's promotional mix.
cards.answer: Finance available / Competitor actions / Nature of the product or service / Nature of the market / Target market
items: Nature of the product or service

cards.front: Why do adverts shift towards persuasion during the growth stage of the product life cycle?
cards.answer: To show off the product's USP and convince customers to choose it as competition increases.

cards.front: Why is promotion usually cut back during the decline stage of the product life cycle?
cards.answer: To save cash, unless the firm is running an extension strategy.

title: Binary Numbers, Two's Complement and Hexadecimal
subject: computer-science-edexcel

cards.front: Name the three places the lesson gives where hexadecimal is used in computing.
cards.answer: Web colour codes / MAC addresses on network cards / Memory dump listings in diagnostic tools
items: Memory dump listings in diagnostic tools

cards.front: Why does binary suit the physical hardware inside a computer?
cards.answer: A transistor is either conducting electricity or not, and that two-state reality maps perfectly onto binary's two digits, 1 and 0.

cards.front: How do you convert an 8-bit two's complement binary pattern back to denary?
cards.answer: Treat the leftmost bit as -128, then add the place values of the remaining bits that are set to 1.

title: Electrolysis of Molten and Aqueous Compounds
subject: separate-sciences-ocr

cards.front: Name the three industrial uses given for the products of electrolysing brine.
cards.answer: Chlorine used to make bleach and PVC / Hydrogen used as a fuel / Sodium hydroxide used to make soap and paper
items: Chlorine used to make bleach and PVC
Sodium hydroxide used to make soap and paper

cards.front: Name the three components used when electroplating an object with copper.
cards.answer: Object as the cathode / Copper electrode as the anode / Copper sulfate solution as the electrolyte
items: Copper sulfate solution as the electrolyte

cards.front: Why can't a solid ionic compound be electrolysed?
cards.answer: Its ions are held in a fixed lattice and are not free to move, so it cannot conduct electricity.

cards.front: How does copper get deposited onto an object during copper electroplating?
cards.answer: Copper atoms at the anode dissolve into solution as ions, and the same mass of copper deposits on the cathode object.

title: Act 2: Mrs Birling and the Charity Committee
subject: english-literature-aqa

cards.front: Name the three tactics Mrs Birling uses to resist the Inspector's investigation.
cards.answer: Tries to pull rank / Dismisses the investigation as irrelevant / Deflects all blame

cards.front: Why does Priestley give Mrs Birling the register of a magistrate rather than a charity worker?
cards.answer: To reveal that she treats charity as a tool of social control rather than genuine compassion for Eva.

cards.front: Why is Mrs Birling seen as the most unsympathetic character in the play?
cards.answer: She shows no remorse even after learning her actions contributed to Eva's death.

title: Internal Energy, Specific Heat Capacity and Latent Heat
subject: separate-sciences

cards.front: Name the three things the amount of internal energy in a substance depends on.
cards.answer: Temperature / Mass / What material it's made from

cards.front: Name the four changes of state described by the particle model.
cards.answer: Melting (solid to liquid) / Boiling (liquid to gas) / Condensing (gas to liquid) / Freezing (liquid to solid)

cards.front: Why do gases take up much more space than liquids or solids?
cards.answer: Energy completely overcomes the forces between particles, so they move freely and far apart.

cards.front: Why do different substances have different melting and boiling points?
cards.answer: It depends on how strong the forces between their particles are.

title: Instrumental Music 1700–1820: Two Worlds, Two Set Works
subject: music-edexcel

cards.front: Name the three instruments that make up the concertino in Bach's Brandenburg Concerto No. 5.
cards.answer: Flute / Violin / Harpsichord

cards.front: Name the three musical eras that the period 1700–1820 spans.
cards.answer: Late Baroque / Classical / Early Romantic

cards.front: Why is the harpsichord's role in Bach's Brandenburg Concerto No. 5 considered progressive for 1721?
cards.answer: It is treated almost as a solo instrument, given genuinely virtuosic passagework, rather than merely providing continuo accompaniment.

cards.front: Why does the slow Grave material return later in the first movement of Beethoven's Pathétique Sonata?
cards.answer: It unexpectedly interrupts just before the development and near the movement's end, as if refusing to be left behind, going beyond standard sonata form.

title: The Nature of Allah and Core Muslim Beliefs
subject: religious-studies-edexcel

cards.front: Name the four holy books Allah revealed, according to the lesson.
cards.answer: Tawrat (Torah) / Zabur (Psalms) / Injil (Gospel) / Qur'an

cards.front: Name the five key divine attributes of Allah given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Omnipotence / Beneficence / Mercy / Transcendence / Immanence

cards.front: Why did Shi'a scholars replace al-Qadr with Adl in their framework of belief?
cards.answer: Because they were concerned predestination could undermine human accountability, so they preferred to emphasise Allah's justice instead.

cards.front: Why does Islamic art traditionally avoid depicting Allah or the Prophet?
cards.answer: Because Tawhid forbids associating anything with Allah, so artists use calligraphy and geometric patterns instead of images.

title: Jesus Christ: Incarnation, the Cross and Salvation
subject: religious-studies-ocr

cards.front: Name the four central events in Christian teaching about Jesus.
cards.answer: The incarnation / The crucifixion / The resurrection / The ascension

cards.front: Name the three different ways Christian denominations teach that salvation works.
cards.answer: Catholics: faith and the sacraments / Protestants: faith alone (sola fide) / Evangelicals: a personal decision to accept Jesus
items: Evangelicals: a personal decision to accept Jesus

cards.front: Why does the incarnation matter so much to Christians?
cards.answer: God did not stay distant from suffering but entered it, experiencing hunger, grief, temptation and death, becoming a compassionate intercessor.

cards.front: Why is it significant that the Temple curtain tore when Jesus died?
cards.answer: It was a sign that the barrier between God and humanity had been removed.

cards.front: Name the four poems the lesson compares with 'Envy' in the conflict cluster.
cards.answer: Songs for the People / Colonization in Reverse / We Lived Happily during the War / Thirteen
items: We Lived Happily during the War

cards.front: Name the three flowers the rose-tree in 'Envy' is said not to be made to bear.
cards.answer: Violet blue / Lily fair / Sweet mignionet

cards.front: Why would it be foolish for the rose-tree in 'Envy' to resent its limits?
cards.answer: Fretting over what it cannot grow would only prove it had forgotten the red rose and scent it already has.

cards.front: How does 'Envy' present envy as a self-inflicted form of damage?
cards.answer: Energy spent comparing yourself to others is energy not spent developing the talent you already possess.

title: Economy, society and the Nazi winners and losers
subject: history-ocr

cards.front: What were the three Ks that summed up the Nazi ideal for women?
cards.answer: Kinder (Children) / Küche (Kitchen) / Kirche (Church)

cards.front: Name the three groups the lesson identifies as losers under Nazi policy.
cards.answer: Workers / Women / The Mittelstand

cards.front: Why did female employment rise during the late 1930s despite Nazi propaganda about motherhood?
cards.answer: Rearmament absorbed male labour into the army, so women were increasingly needed in factories and farms despite ideology.

cards.front: Why were farmers' gains from Nazi policy limited despite the Reich Entailed Farm Law protecting their land?
cards.answer: Agricultural prices stayed low, labour was drawn to better-paid industry, and the Four-Year Plan demanded food self-sufficiency without adequate reward.

title: Managing Medical Conditions: Hypothermia, Heat Exhaustion & Dehydration
subject: cambridge-nationals-sport-science

cards.front: State the five symptoms of heat exhaustion.
cards.answer: Excessive sweating / Headache or dizziness / Being very thirsty / Feeling or being sick / Rapid pulse and/or rapid breathing

cards.front: State the four symptoms of dehydration.
cards.answer: Feeling thirsty / Fatigue / Dark yellow urine and infrequent urination / Dry mouth or lips
items: Dark yellow urine and infrequent urination

cards.front: Why must a hot bath, hot water bottle or rubbing never be used to treat hypothermia?
cards.answer: These cause rapid vasodilation, sending cold blood from the periphery to the core, which can cause cardiac complications.

cards.front: Why do hot, humid conditions increase the risk of heat exhaustion?
cards.answer: High humidity prevents sweat from evaporating effectively, so the body's main cooling mechanism fails to work properly.

cards.front: In Cope's '1st Date — She', what three things does she worry about?
cards.answer: Whether her outfit works / Whether she's talking too much / Whether he'll call again

cards.front: What three different methods do Cope, Cooper Clarke and Hadfield each use to reject Romantic conventions of love poetry?
cards.answer: Colloquial inner monologue (Cope) / Punk-influenced domestic imagery (Cooper Clarke) / Philosophical paradox (Hadfield)

cards.front: How does the refrain 'I wanna be yours' change in meaning through repetition in Cooper Clarke's poem?
cards.answer: Repetition shifts the refrain from comic to genuinely moving, turning what starts as a joke into an earnest declaration.

cards.front: Why does Hadfield's 'Love's Dog' refuse to present love as simply positive or negative?
cards.answer: It shows love as fundamentally paradoxical, where joy cannot exist without pain, making it psychologically honest and complex.

title: Injury Prevention, PARQ, RICE and PEDs
subject: physical-education-edexcel

cards.front: Name the seven banned categories of performance-enhancing drugs listed in the lesson.
cards.answer: Anabolic steroids / Beta blockers / Diuretics / Narcotic analgesics / Peptide hormones (EPO/growth hormone) / Stimulants / Blood doping

cards.front: What seven areas of health does the PARQ ask questions about?
cards.answer: Cardiovascular health / Recent illness / Known medical conditions / Bone or joint problems / Pregnancy / Prescription medication / Other reasons vigorous exercise may be unsuitable

cards.front: Why does increasing training load too quickly cause overuse injuries such as shin splints or stress fractures?
cards.answer: It violates progressive overload, so training volume/intensity rises faster than the body can adapt, damaging tissue.

cards.front: Why does doping create a coercive culture for young athletes even if they don't want to dope?
cards.answer: If some competitors dope and gain an advantage, non-doping athletes risk being left behind, forcing an unfair dilemma.

title: Catholic Beliefs about God, Creation and Jesus
subject: religious-studies-eduqas

cards.front: What are the four key attributes used to describe God's nature as Creator?
cards.answer: Omnipotence (all-power) / Omnibenevolence (all-goodness) / Omniscience (all-knowledge) / Omnipresence (present everywhere)

cards.front: What three events together make up the Paschal Mystery?
cards.answer: The crucifixion / The resurrection / The ascension

cards.front: Why do Catholics believe God is a sustainer as well as a Creator?
cards.answer: Because the universe depends on God's continued will for its ongoing existence, not just its original creation.

cards.front: How does the Incarnation show God entering human experience?
cards.answer: John 1:14 teaches that the Word (God) became flesh and lived among people, so God entered human experience completely.

cards.front: Name the three peaceful methods the NUWSS (Suffragists) used to campaign for the vote.
cards.answer: Petitions / Public meetings / Lobbying Parliament

cards.front: Name the four militant tactics the WSPU (Suffragettes) escalated to from 1908.
cards.answer: Smashing windows / Chaining themselves to railings / Setting fire to post boxes and empty buildings / Disrupting public meetings
items: Setting fire to post boxes and empty buildings

cards.front: Why do historians argue the Representation of the People Act 1918 did not show full acceptance of women's equality?
cards.answer: It excluded women under 30 and without property, deliberately leaving out young working-class women who had done most of the war work.

cards.front: How did women's work during the First World War weaken the argument against giving them the vote?
cards.answer: Women took on vital roles in munitions factories, as nurses, land army workers and in transport, making the claim they were unfit to vote hard to sustain.

cards.front: Name the five interlocking techniques that make up Stanislavski's system.
cards.answer: Emotion memory / Given circumstances / The magic if / Objectives and super-objectives / The method of physical actions

cards.front: Why did Stanislavski warn against 'emotional memory wallowing'?
cards.answer: Because losing yourself in the feeling means losing technical control; the actor must stay an artist shaping emotion for the audience.

cards.front: Why doesn't an actor need to feel real emotion at every single performance?
cards.answer: Rehearsal work internalises the emotional truth into the physical and vocal score, keeping the performance consistent even when tired or unwell.

cards.front: Why does the Ghost repeat Scrooge's own words about 'decreasing the surplus population'?
cards.answer: To force Scrooge to recognise that his cold phrase has a real human cost, since it could mean Tiny Tim's death.

cards.front: How does the Ghost's rapid ageing across Stave 3 work as a warning to Scrooge?
cards.answer: By ageing quickly until his hair turns grey, the temporal structure warns that time to act on suffering is always running out.

cards.front: Name the three additive manufacturing processes described in the lesson.
cards.answer: Fused deposition modelling (FDM) / Stereolithography (SLA) / Metal sintering (SLS/DMLS)

cards.front: Name the five differences the lesson gives between additive manufacturing and conventional mass production.
cards.answer: Tooling cost / Speed of iteration / Geometric freedom / Production volume / Material waste

cards.front: Why is metal sintering only used for high-value, low-volume parts?
cards.answer: The process is slow and the machines cost hundreds of thousands of pounds, making it uneconomical for large volumes.

cards.front: Why does additive manufacturing waste less material than subtractive machining?
cards.answer: Additive manufacturing adds material only where needed, while subtractive processes like milling can waste 90% of the starting billet.

cards.front: Name the four types of grievance that fed into the Pilgrimage of Grace.
cards.answer: Religious grievance over the dissolution / Economic anxiety over new taxes and bad harvests / Political resentment of Cromwell / Social unease over rising rents and enclosure
items: Economic anxiety over new taxes and bad harvests
Social unease over rising rents and enclosure

cards.front: What four demands did the Pilgrimage of Grace articles set out?
cards.answer: Restoration of the monasteries / Removal of Cromwell / Protection of the Catholic Church / A free Parliament held in the north
items: A free Parliament held in the north

cards.front: Why did closing the monasteries threaten more than just religion in northern villages?
cards.answer: Monasteries were the social and economic heart of villages, providing schools, almshouses, hospitality and employment, not just spiritual centres.

cards.front: Why is royal authority in this period described as 'performative', comparing 1381 and 1536?
cards.answer: Kings like Richard II and Henry VIII bargained with promises when too weak to fight, then broke them and punished ringleaders once safe.

title: Rhythms of the World: Samba and Calypso from Central and South America
subject: music-ocr

cards.front: Name the four instrument families that make up the bateria.
cards.answer: Surdo / Caixa / Agogo / Tamborim

cards.front: Name the three influences the lesson gives for samba's musical origins.
cards.answer: West and Central African drumming traditions / Portuguese influences / Indigenous influences
items: West and Central African drumming traditions

cards.front: Why does samba create constant rhythmic tension?
cards.answer: It is built on a two-beat pulse, but nearly every layer of the bateria plays syncopated patterns against that pulse.

cards.front: How does texture typically build during a bateria performance?
cards.answer: It starts with one or two instruments stating the pulse, then further layers of surdo, caixa, agogo and tamborim are added until the full ensemble plays together.

title: The Orchestra 1650-1910: How the Sound Changed
subject: music-aqa

cards.front: Name the three things you should identify when naming what you hear in an orchestral extract.
cards.answer: The forces (strings alone, full orchestra, or in between) / The texture (contrapuntal, homophonic chords, or melody with accompaniment) / The dynamics (sudden blocks, gradual build, or shock accent)
items: The forces (strings alone, full orchestra, or in between)
The texture (contrapuntal, homophonic chords, or melody with accompaniment)
The dynamics (sudden blocks, gradual build, or shock accent)

cards.front: What extra instruments did later Romantic composers add to grow the orchestra after Beethoven's time?
cards.answer: Extra horns / Valved brass / Tuba / Harp / A larger string section

cards.front: Why is the sudden loud chord in Haydn's Symphony No. 94 'Surprise' not the same as Baroque terraced dynamics?
cards.answer: It isn't caused by an instrument's limits — Haydn had a full dynamic range available and chose to spring the chord on the listener as a joke.

cards.front: How does Classical homophonic texture differ from Baroque homophonic texture?
cards.answer: Baroque homophony is blocks of chords moving together, while Classical homophony is melody-and-accompaniment, with one voice carrying the tune.

cards.front: Name the three classes of lever the lesson describes.
cards.answer: First-order lever / Second-order lever / Third-order lever

cards.front: Give three examples of a first-order lever named in the lesson.
cards.answer: Seesaw / Crowbar / Scissors

cards.front: Why does a second-order lever always multiply force?
cards.answer: Because the load sits between the fulcrum and the effort, so the effort moves further than the load.

cards.front: How does a crossed belt differ from a flat belt in a pulley system?
cards.answer: A flat belt makes pulleys rotate in the same direction, but a crossed belt reverses the direction of rotation.

cards.front: What charge do ions form for elements in Groups 1, 2, 6 and 7?
cards.answer: Group 1 lose 1 electron to form +1 ions / Group 2 lose 2 electrons to form +2 ions / Group 6 gain 2 electrons to form −2 ions / Group 7 gain 1 electron to form −1 ions
items: Group 1 lose 1 electron to form +1 ions
Group 2 lose 2 electrons to form +2 ions
Group 6 gain 2 electrons to form −2 ions
Group 7 gain 1 electron to form −1 ions

cards.front: Name the four positive ions the lesson lists you should know the formulae for.
cards.answer: Na+ / K+ / Mg2+ / Ca2+

cards.front: How does dissolving an ionic compound allow it to conduct electricity?
cards.answer: Dissolving breaks apart the lattice, freeing ions to move towards oppositely charged electrodes and carry the current.

cards.front: Why does magnesium chloride have the formula MgCl2?
cards.answer: Mg2+ has a +2 charge, so two Cl− ions are needed to balance the charge to zero.

title: Structures You Must Recognise: Binary, Ternary, Rondo, Variations and Sonata Form
subject: music-aqa

cards.front: Name the five standard structures covered in this lesson for organising a classical or romantic movement.
cards.answer: Binary form / Ternary form / Rondo form / Theme and variations / Sonata form

cards.front: Name the five elements composers can vary between repeats in theme and variations form.
cards.answer: Ornamentation / Dynamics / Instrumentation / Harmony / Rhythm

cards.front: Why is the development section of a sonata-form movement the most unpredictable part?
cards.answer: It takes fragments of the exposition's themes and works them through unstable, quickly-changing keys, with shifting textures and motifs passed between instruments.

cards.front: How does the recapitulation in sonata form resolve the tension built up in the development?
cards.answer: It restates both the first and second subjects, but now both stay in the tonic key instead of separating.

cards.front: Name the five scientists (in order) whose work changed the atomic model, from Dalton to Chadwick.
cards.answer: Dalton - solid sphere model / Thomson - plum pudding model / Rutherford - nuclear model (alpha-scattering) / Bohr - fixed energy levels / Chadwick - discovered the neutron

cards.front: Name the three subatomic particles found in an atom.
cards.answer: Protons / Neutrons / Electrons

cards.front: How do you calculate the number of neutrons in an atom?
cards.answer: Subtract the atomic number from the mass number.

cards.front: Why does a neutral atom have no overall electrical charge?
cards.answer: It has equal numbers of protons (+1) and electrons (-1), so their charges cancel out.

cards.front: Name the four protein alternatives for vegetarian and vegan diets given in the lesson.
cards.answer: TVP (textured vegetable protein) / Soya / Mycoprotein (Quorn) / Tofu

cards.front: Name the three structural forms of carbohydrates described in the lesson.
cards.answer: Monosaccharides / Disaccharides / Polysaccharides

cards.front: Why does eating too much protein put extra strain on the kidneys?
cards.answer: Excess protein isn't stored; its nitrogen is excreted as urea, which the kidneys have to process.

cards.front: Why can a lack of carbohydrate lead to ketoacidosis?
cards.answer: Without enough carbohydrate the body switches to using fat then protein for fuel, producing ketone bodies which build up.

cards.front: What are the five stages of Rostow's modernisation theory?
cards.answer: Traditional society / Preconditions for take-off / Take-off / Drive to maturity / High mass consumption

cards.front: What five types of causes does the lesson give for global inequality?
cards.answer: Historical / Environmental / Economic / Political / Social
items: Political (corruption, conflict, weak rule of law)

cards.front: Why does Cuba have a life expectancy similar to the UK despite having roughly a tenth of its GDP per capita?
cards.answer: Because Cuba has a strong public health system, showing income alone doesn't determine health outcomes.

cards.front: Why does GDP per capita fail to capture the true state of a country's economy?
cards.answer: It hides the informal economy, such as street trading and subsistence farming, which isn't officially recorded.

title: Film Posters: The Man with the Golden Gun and No Time to Die
subject: media-studies-eduqas

cards.front: Name the three characters on the No Time to Die poster who look directly at the camera, giving a personal mode of address.
cards.answer: Safin, the villain / Q / Swann

cards.front: What three real-world contexts influenced the representation of women and race on the No Time to Die poster?
cards.answer: The 2016 #OscarsSoWhite campaign / The 2020 killing of George Floyd / Decades of feminist critique of Bond Girls
items: Decades of feminist critique of Bond Girls

cards.front: Why does only showing the shooter's hand on The Man with the Golden Gun poster create an enigma code?
cards.answer: Because the assassin's identity is hidden, making the audience want to find out who is trying to kill Bond.

cards.front: How does the No Time to Die poster's design create nostalgia for fans?
cards.answer: It uses an intertextuality montage that layers separate images referencing earlier Bond films to create nostalgia.

cards.front: What three reasons does the lesson give for why people obey authority figures?
cards.answer: Authority figures are seen as legitimate / Refusing to obey can carry real consequences / Symbols of authority increase how much a person is obeyed
items: Authority figures are seen as legitimate
Refusing to obey can carry real consequences
Symbols of authority increase how much a person is obeyed

cards.front: Name the four examples of authority figures given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Police officer / Teacher / Doctor / Employer

cards.front: Why can symbols of authority such as a uniform or badge increase obedience?
cards.answer: They act as a visible reminder of someone's position and power, making people more likely to obey.

cards.front: Why can crowds produce both pro-social and anti-social behaviour?
cards.answer: The same features - numbers, unity and shared emotion - that enable cooperation can also cause serious harm.

cards.front: Name the three key facts about 1980s Liverpool given in the lesson to explain the play's setting.
cards.answer: Deindustrialisation destroyed traditional industries like shipping and coal / Council estates rehoused families with poor facilities and high crime / North-South divide harmed the industrial north while the south flourished
items: Deindustrialisation destroyed traditional industries like shipping and coal
Council estates rehoused families with poor facilities and high crime
North-South divide harmed the industrial north while the south flourished

cards.front: Why does Russell use the nature versus nurture argument as the play's core device?
cards.answer: Because the twins share identical DNA, so their completely different lives must be caused by nurture — environment, wealth, and class.

cards.front: How does Mrs Johnstone giving up one twin support Russell's argument that poverty is not a personal failing?
cards.answer: She gives him up not because she is a bad mother but because she literally cannot feed another mouth, showing structural causes.

cards.front: Name the three purposes that blaming Snowball serves for Napoleon after the windmill collapses.
cards.answer: Deflects blame from his own failures / Maintains an external enemy / Justifies increased control over the animals
items: Deflects blame from his own failures
Justifies increased control over the animals

cards.front: Why does the harder Boxer works actually make his exploitation worse?
cards.answer: The harder he works, the more the pigs benefit from his labour, and the faster he is used up.

cards.front: How does the pigs' eventual use of the windmill mirror the Soviet system Orwell is criticising?
cards.answer: It mirrors how Soviet industrial output benefited the state apparatus rather than the workers who produced it.

title: The Divine: Brahman, the Deities and the Avatars
subject: religious-studies-ocr

cards.front: Name the three goddesses of the Tridevi and the male deity each is associated with.
cards.answer: Saraswati - wisdom and arts, associated with Brahma / Lakshmi - prosperity and devotion, associated with Vishnu / Parvati/Durga - power and transformation, associated with Shiva
items: Saraswati - wisdom and arts, associated with Brahma
Lakshmi - prosperity and devotion, associated with Vishnu
Parvati/Durga - power and transformation, associated with Shiva

cards.front: What four things do worshippers offer a murti during puja?
cards.answer: Flowers / Food / Incense / Water

cards.front: Why does Vishnu descend to earth as an avatar, according to the Bhagavad Gita?
cards.answer: Whenever righteousness declines and evil increases, Vishnu descends to restore the cosmic order.

cards.front: Why did the Arya Samaj reform movement reject murti worship?
cards.answer: It argued Brahman cannot be contained in physical form and that the Vedas do not sanction image worship.

cards.front: Name the three aspects of housing identified in the lesson.
cards.answer: Housing needs / Housing conditions / Housing location

cards.front: Name the three types of pollution identified in the lesson.
cards.answer: Air pollution / Noise pollution / Light pollution

cards.front: Why can living in a rural area negatively affect a person's wellbeing?
cards.answer: Long distances to hospitals, shops, and schools can lead to social isolation.

cards.front: How does noise pollution particularly affect emotional and intellectual wellbeing?
cards.answer: Prolonged exposure causes stress, anxiety, irritability, and difficulty concentrating.

cards.front: Name the seven family forms in the UK identified in the lesson.
cards.answer: Nuclear family / Extended family / Reconstituted family / Lone parent family / Single sex family / Cohabiting family / Beanpole family

cards.front: What three sociological consequences did China's one-child policy have, according to the lesson?
cards.answer: 4-2-1 family structure / demographic imbalances (more boys than girls) / financial pressure on only children to support elderly parents
items: financial pressure on only children to support elderly parents

cards.front: Why did Parsons argue the nuclear family is the most efficient form for modern industrial society?
cards.answer: Because it is geographically mobile and suited to the demands of the labour market.

cards.front: Why has the beanpole family structure emerged in the UK?
cards.answer: Declining birth rates mean fewer children per generation while increased life expectancy means more generations are alive at once.

cards.front: Name the five data types the lesson says you must know.
cards.answer: Integer / Real / Boolean / Character / String

cards.front: Name the three programming constructs that every program is built from.
cards.answer: Sequence / Selection / Iteration

cards.front: Why does "5" + "3" give "53" instead of 8?
cards.answer: Because the values are stored as strings, so + joins (concatenates) them as text instead of adding them as numbers.

cards.front: Why must a program convert user input before performing arithmetic on it?
cards.answer: User input arrives as a string by default, so it must be converted to an integer or real to do arithmetic instead of concatenation.

cards.front: Name the four non-experimental methods used in psychology when experiments aren't possible.
cards.answer: Interviews / Questionnaires / Case studies / Observation studies

cards.front: What three types of relationship can a correlation show between two variables?
cards.answer: Positive correlation / Negative correlation / No correlation

cards.front: Why might participants behave differently when they know they are being watched in an observation study?
cards.answer: Knowing they are being observed changes their natural behaviour, known as the Hawthorne effect.

cards.front: Why are ice cream sales and drowning rates correlated even though ice cream doesn't cause drowning?
cards.answer: Hot weather is the unmeasured third variable that increases both ice cream sales and drowning rates.

cards.front: Name the five worship traditions the lesson identifies, in order.
cards.answer: Anglican Communion service (liturgical) / Roman Catholic mass (liturgical) / Greek Orthodox service (liturgical) / Methodist Sunday morning worship (informal) / Quaker meeting (silent, Spirit-led)

cards.front: Name the five types of prayer recognised in Christian tradition, according to the lesson.
cards.answer: Adoration / Confession / Thanksgiving / Intercessions / Supplication

cards.front: Why do liturgical Christian traditions use set prayers from authorised books alongside extempore prayer?
cards.answer: Set prayers give theological precision and prevent heresy creeping into public worship.

cards.front: Why do Quakers sit in silence during their meetings for worship?
cards.answer: Because they believe God can speak directly to every individual, so they wait silently until someone feels moved by the Spirit to speak.

cards.front: Name the five main pollutants produced by burning fossil fuels, as given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Carbon dioxide / Carbon monoxide / Soot/particulates / Sulfur dioxide / Nitrogen oxides

cards.front: Name the four alternative approaches to reducing pollution mentioned in the lesson.
cards.answer: Switching to renewable energy sources / Using electric or hydrogen-powered vehicles / Improving fuel efficiency / Developing carbon capture and storage technologies
items: Developing carbon capture and storage technologies

cards.front: How does soot contribute to global dimming?
cards.answer: Soot particles released into the atmosphere block sunlight, causing global dimming.

cards.front: What useful product does flue gas desulfurisation make, and what can it be used for?
cards.answer: It produces calcium sulfate, which can be used to make plaster.

cards.front: Name the four things a coach must consider when designing a circuit training session.
cards.answer: Space and equipment available / Number of stations / Work:rest ratio at each station / Type of exercise at each station
items: Type of exercise at each station

cards.front: In the basketball player's pre-season example, name the three training methods her coach combines.
cards.answer: Fartlek training / Plyometric training / Static stretching

cards.front: Why would continuous training alone be insufficient for a basketball player's pre-season programme?
cards.answer: It would not develop the anaerobic power that basketball demands.

cards.front: Why must the back remain straight during deadlifts and squats?
cards.answer: To protect the lumbar vertebrae from injury.

title: John's Accession and the Murder of Prince Arthur
subject: history-edexcel

cards.front: Name the three character traits the lesson says show up again and again in John's behaviour.
cards.answer: Suspicious / Vindictive / Personally repellent

cards.front: Name the three figures who persuaded England and Normandy to accept John as king in 1199.
cards.answer: Eleanor of Aquitaine / William Marshal / Hubert Walter

cards.front: How did John show administrative competence as king?
cards.answer: He toured England in person hearing pleas, checking accounts and badgering sheriffs, keeping ever-thicker pipe-roll records.

cards.front: Why did Philip II declare John's French fiefs forfeit in 1202?
cards.answer: The Lusignans appealed to Philip over Isabella's seizure, and when John refused to attend Paris as Duke of Aquitaine, Philip declared his fiefs forfeit.

cards.front: Name the four factors the lesson gives that combined to discredit the Tsarist regime by 1917.
cards.answer: Huge losses of 1914–16 (around five million casualties) / Food shortages in the cities / Tsar taking personal command of the army in 1915 / Chaotic influence of Rasputin at home
items: Huge losses of 1914–16 (around five million casualties)
Tsar taking personal command of the army in 1915
Chaotic influence of Rasputin at home

cards.front: Name the three reasons the lesson gives for why the USA had stayed neutral before 1917.
cards.answer: Long tradition of avoiding European conflicts / Strong German-American minority / Economy doing well selling food and munitions to both sides
items: Long tradition of avoiding European conflicts
Economy doing well selling food and munitions to both sides

cards.front: Why did Ludendorff launch the German Spring Offensive in March 1918?
cards.answer: Russia's exit freed German troops, giving Germany a temporary manpower advantage before American forces could arrive in mass strength.

cards.front: How did the Provisional Government's decision to continue the war help the Bolsheviks seize power?
cards.answer: Its summer 1917 offensive collapsed, soldiers deserted in tens of thousands, and Lenin's peace promise gained support since the government refused to make peace.

cards.front: Name the six network hardware devices covered in this lesson.
cards.answer: Router / Switch / Hub / Bridge / Wireless access point (WAP) / Network interface card (NIC)

cards.front: Give three drawbacks of wireless connections mentioned in the lesson.
cards.answer: Signals blocked by walls / Interfered with by other devices on same frequency / Intercepted more easily than wired
items: Interfered with by other devices on same frequency

cards.front: Why is fibre-optic cable used despite being more expensive to install than copper?
cards.answer: It uses pulses of light to offer much higher bandwidth over longer distances than copper.

cards.front: How does a bridge reduce unnecessary traffic crossing between two network segments?
cards.answer: It checks the destination MAC address and only forwards frames meant for the other segment, dropping same-segment traffic.

cards.front: Name the three 3D drawing systems the lesson describes for communicating design ideas.
cards.answer: Isometric drawing / Oblique drawing / Perspective drawing

cards.front: Name the four things CAD software lets a designer do before anything is physically made.
cards.answer: Build an accurate digital model / Rotate it to check every angle / Apply realistic colours and materials / Run simple simulations
items: Rotate it to check every angle

cards.front: Why is isometric drawing chosen to show a client how big a product will actually be?
cards.answer: Because isometric drawing keeps every measurement to scale, giving accurate proportions.

cards.front: How does sending CAD files straight to CAM equipment help the design process?
cards.answer: It speeds up the move from idea to prototype and reduces wasted material from mistakes made on paper.

title: Cortes as Governor and the Spanish Base at Panama
subject: history-edexcel

cards.front: Name the four accusations Cortes's rivals made against him at the Spanish court.
cards.answer: Corruption / Withholding the king's share of treasure / Executing Cuauhtemoc in 1525 / Behaving like an independent prince
items: Withholding the king's share of treasure

cards.front: Name the four ways Indigenous Mexico survived in the long term after the conquest.
cards.answer: Nahuatl continued to be spoken and written / Codex-painting adapted to Catholic subjects / Cabildos preserved Indigenous self-government / Virgin of Guadalupe absorbed Indigenous symbolism
items: Nahuatl continued to be spoken and written
Virgin of Guadalupe absorbed Indigenous symbolism

cards.front: Why is the encomienda described as the old Aztec tribute economy with new owners, not a new economy?
cards.answer: The same Nahua communities kept paying maize, cotton and labour, but it now went to Spanish encomenderos instead of Tenochtitlan.

cards.front: How did Cortes's Honduras expedition of 1524–26 contribute to his downfall?
cards.answer: His nearly two-year absence from the capital let rivals at court build accusations of corruption and acting like an independent prince.

cards.front: Name the five key themes the lesson says every Animal Farm exam question connects to.
cards.answer: Power and corruption / Propaganda and language / Class and inequality / Revolution and its failure / Education and ignorance

cards.front: What four factors does Orwell identify for why revolutions fail?
cards.answer: Power concentrated in a small elite / Lack of education among the masses / The effectiveness of propaganda / The powerful's willingness to use force
items: Power concentrated in a small elite
Lack of education among the masses
The powerful's willingness to use force

cards.front: How should a student structure paragraphs for the comparison task pairing Animal Farm with an unseen modern prose extract?
cards.answer: Structure every paragraph as a comparison using linking phrases like 'similarly'/'in contrast', analysing language and linking to context throughout.

cards.front: Why is memorising 8-10 short quotations important given Animal Farm is a closed-text exam?
cards.answer: Because the novella cannot be brought into the exam, memorised quotations let you respond to any question asked.

title: Sources of Bias, Designing and Interpreting Investigations
subject: psychology-ocr

cards.front: The 'design an investigation' task requires five elements applied to a scenario. Name them.
cards.answer: A hypothesis / Identifying variables / An experimental design / A sampling method / How ethical guidelines would be followed
items: How ethical guidelines would be followed

cards.front: How does the observer effect differ from demand characteristics as a source of bias?
cards.answer: The observer effect happens simply because participants know they are being watched, not because they have guessed the study's aim.

cards.front: In the worked example, why does telling participants the study's aim beforehand threaten the validity of the results?
cards.answer: Knowing the aim could lead participants to try harder to remember, or deliberately underperform, changing their behaviour to match or disrupt it.

title: Wounded Knee, the Dawes Act and the End of the Frontier
subject: history-edexcel

cards.front: Name the three connected pressures that destroyed the buffalo herds by 1890.
cards.answer: Railroads selling hunting seats and clearing track / Eastern leather demand paying for hides / US Army strategy endorsed by General Sheridan
items: Railroads selling hunting seats and clearing track
Eastern leather demand paying for hides
US Army strategy endorsed by General Sheridan

cards.front: According to Wovoka's 1889 vision, what three things would happen if Indigenous peoples danced the Ghost Dance and lived peacefully?
cards.answer: The buffalo would return / The dead would rise / Settlers would be swept from the land
items: Settlers would be swept from the land

cards.front: Why did Custer's forces lose at the Battle of the Little Bighorn?
cards.answer: He ignored scout warnings that the village was the largest ever seen on the Plains and split his command into three, weakening each part.

cards.front: How did the Dawes Act lead to Indigenous families losing most of their land?
cards.answer: It allotted 160 acres per family, declared remaining reservation land 'surplus', and sold that surplus to white settlers.

cards.front: Why does raising the temperature of a gas at constant volume increase its pressure?
cards.answer: Particles gain kinetic energy, move faster, and collide with the walls more forcefully and more frequently.

cards.front: Why does an object sink in a fluid?
cards.answer: Because its weight exceeds the upthrust acting on it.

cards.front: Name the three quantities needed to calculate pressure at depth in a liquid using P = ρgh. (Higher tier)
cards.answer: Density of the liquid / Gravitational field strength / Depth

cards.front: Name the six material categories in AQA D&T.
cards.answer: Papers & boards / Timber / Metals / Polymers / Textiles / Electronic & mechanical systems

cards.front: Name the four metals given as property-matched examples for commercial products in this lesson.
cards.answer: Stainless steel / Aluminium / Copper / Mild steel

cards.front: Why does repeated cold forming cause a metal to crack if further forming is attempted?
cards.answer: Repeated cold forming introduces internal stresses (work-hardening) that make the metal crack if further forming is attempted.

cards.front: Why is Gore-Tex used in outdoor sports clothing?
cards.answer: Its expanded PTFE membrane makes it simultaneously waterproof and breathable, a critical property combination for outdoor sports clothing.

cards.front: Name the six classical conditions Islamic jurisprudence lists before lesser jihad is permissible.
cards.answer: Legitimate cause (self-defence or defending the oppressed) / All peaceful alternatives exhausted first / Declared by a legitimate authority, not individuals / Non-combatants must be protected / Destruction of crops and buildings prohibited / Must cease when enemy stops fighting or offers peace
items: Legitimate cause (self-defence or defending the oppressed)
Declared by a legitimate authority, not individuals
Destruction of crops and buildings prohibited
Must cease when enemy stops fighting or offers peace

cards.front: Name the four Islamic festivals covered in this lesson.
cards.answer: Id-ul-Fitr / Id-ul-Adha / Ashura / Id-ul-Ghadeer

cards.front: Why is describing jihad simply as 'holy war' considered a misrepresentation of Islamic teaching?
cards.answer: It ignores greater jihad, seen as the more important form, and strips lesser jihad of its strict conditions, making it sound like unlimited violence which the Qur'an prohibits.

cards.front: Why did the Prophet Muhammad encourage fasting on Ashura, according to the hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari?
cards.answer: He observed Jews fasting to mark Moses being saved from Pharaoh and said he had a stronger connection to Moses.

title: Feeding the Human Race: Selective Breeding and GM
subject: separate-sciences-ocr

cards.front: Name the five threats to food security given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Population growth / Climate change / Rising costs / Conflict / Water scarcity

cards.front: Name the four traits GM crops have been engineered for.
cards.answer: Resistant to insect pests / Resistant to herbicides / Tolerant to drought / Greater yields

cards.front: Why does tissue culture make a whole crop vulnerable to the same disease?
cards.answer: All the plants produced are genetically identical clones, so if a disease emerges that one can't resist, none of them can either.

cards.front: How does integrated pest management minimise chemical use while still protecting crop yields?
cards.answer: It uses pesticides only when pest numbers exceed a threshold and relies on natural predators where possible, reducing environmental impact.

title: Popularity of Sport in the UK & Emerging Sports
subject: cambridge-nationals-sport-studies

cards.front: Name the eight factors the lesson gives that affect the popularity of a sport in the UK.
cards.answer: Number of people participating / Provision of facilities / Environment and climate / Live spectator opportunities / Media coverage and range / High-level success of national teams or athletes / Positive role models / Social acceptability
items: High-level success of national teams or athletes

cards.front: Give the reasons the lesson gives for why emerging sports sometimes fail to grow.
cards.answer: Require expensive specialist equipment / Cannot be played in existing facilities / Rules are hard to explain quickly / No official governing body / Social media interest fades without in-person participation
items: Cannot be played in existing facilities
Rules are hard to explain quickly
Social media interest fades without in-person participation

cards.front: Why did the closure of public swimming pools in the 2010s reduce adult swimming participation?
cards.answer: With no pool within reach, people in those areas had less facility provision, so fewer of them swam.

cards.front: Why is pickleball particularly popular with retired people and older adults?
cards.answer: Its court is smaller, the pace is lower than tennis, and rallies last longer, suiting older players.

cards.front: Name the three practical uses of static electricity described in the lesson.
cards.answer: Electrostatic paint/crop sprayers / Photocopiers and laser printers / Electrostatic precipitators in chimneys

cards.front: Name the three dangerous situations involving static electricity given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Refuelling aircraft or fuel tankers / Sparks near oxygen or anaesthetics in hospitals / Electrostatic discharge damaging electronic components
items: Sparks near oxygen or anaesthetics in hospitals

cards.front: Why is the force on a charge the same everywhere between two parallel charged plates?
cards.answer: Because the field lines between the plates are parallel and equally spaced, making the field uniform.

cards.front: How does doubling the distance between two charges affect the force between them?
cards.answer: Doubling the distance between charges significantly reduces the force between them.

cards.front: Name the four characteristics the lesson says recur in successful entrepreneurs.
cards.answer: Hard working / Innovative / Well organised / Willing to take a calculated risk
items: Willing to take a calculated risk

cards.front: Name the four things the lesson gives as causing a constantly shifting business environment.
cards.answer: Technology / The economy / Legislation / Environmental expectations

cards.front: Why has the tertiary sector become the biggest part of the UK economy?
cards.answer: Cheaper labour abroad pulled most factory work overseas, while digital technology created new service businesses like Deliveroo and Monzo.

cards.front: Why should an explanation of opportunity cost name the specific alternative given up?
cards.answer: Strong answers must state exactly what was sacrificed, such as the money going to X, rather than just saying there was an opportunity cost.

cards.front: Name the three types of business situation the lesson says JIT stock management suits.
cards.answer: Reliable, nearby suppliers / Predictable demand / Products where parts are expensive to store
items: Products where parts are expensive to store

cards.front: What are the three concrete benefits of strong supplier relationships given in the lesson?
cards.answer: Processes run smoothly / Business secures best value, not just lowest price / Waste is stripped out so lead times fall
items: Business secures best value, not just lowest price
Waste is stripped out so lead times fall

cards.front: Why might a supermarket chain choose a JIC stock strategy rather than JIT?
cards.answer: Running out of stock would be disastrous for customers, so buffer stock stops delivery hiccups from emptying the shelves.

cards.front: Why have post-Brexit border delays hit fresh food exporters especially hard?
cards.answer: Their goods are perishable, so long waits at ports mean the produce spoils before it can reach customers.

cards.front: Name the four things you must label on a reaction profile diagram.
cards.answer: Reactants energy level / Products energy level / Activation energy (arrow up to peak) / Overall energy change (arrow reactants to products)
items: Overall energy change (arrow reactants to products)

cards.front: In a calorimetry experiment, what three temperature-related values do you record?
cards.answer: Starting temperature / Maximum or minimum temperature reached / Calculated temperature change (ΔT)

cards.front: How does a catalyst manage to lower the activation energy of a reaction?
cards.answer: It provides an alternative reaction pathway with a lower energy barrier.

cards.front: [Higher] Why is the reaction H2 + Cl2 → 2HCl exothermic based on bond energy calculations?
cards.answer: Because forming H–Cl bonds releases 862 kJ/mol, more than the 678 kJ/mol needed to break H–H and Cl–Cl bonds, giving a negative energy change.

cards.front: Name the six main renewable energy sources covered in this course.
cards.answer: Solar / Wind / Hydroelectric / Geothermal / Biomass / Wave/tidal

cards.front: Name the three main energy storage methods used for products mentioned in the lesson.
cards.answer: Batteries / Mains electricity / Wind-up mechanisms

cards.front: Why is geothermal energy less practical in the UK than in a place like Iceland?
cards.answer: Geothermal energy uses heat from the Earth's crust, which is only practically available in regions with volcanic activity.

cards.front: Why does surface area matter when designing a product with PV cells?
cards.answer: PV cells must be exposed to light to generate electricity, so surface area affects the product's form and orientation.

title: War: Just War, Holy War & Pacifism
subject: religious-studies-aqa

cards.front: Name the three main reasons for war studied in GCSE Religious Studies.
cards.answer: Greed / Self-defence / Retaliation

cards.front: Name the four conditions for a holy war to be legitimate in Islam.
cards.answer: Declared by a recognised religious authority / Fought in self-defence, not aggression / Uses proportionate force / Does not target civilians, elderly, women or children
items: Declared by a recognised religious authority
Does not target civilians, elderly, women or children

cards.front: Why do religious believers warn against retaliation as a reason for going to war?
cards.answer: Because although it can deter future aggression, retaliation often creates a cycle of violence.

cards.front: Why is there tension within Christianity over whether war can be justified?
cards.answer: Because Jesus taught peace and non-violence, yet the Church accepts war may sometimes be necessary to prevent greater suffering.

cards.front: Name the three factors the lesson says decide how fast a river or coastal landform changes.
cards.answer: Geology / Climate / Human activity

cards.front: Name the three types of coastal defence the lesson mentions that are designed to slow erosion.
cards.answer: Sea walls / Groynes / Rock armour

cards.front: Why does straightening a river channel (channelisation) speed up erosion downstream?
cards.answer: It makes water flow more quickly, so erosion accelerates further down the river.

cards.front: Why do dams and reservoirs reduce deposition on floodplains downstream?
cards.answer: They trap sediment behind them, starving floodplains of new alluvium.

cards.front: Name the three key functions functionalists argue education performs for society.
cards.answer: Serving the needs of the economy / Facilitating social mobility / Fostering social cohesion
items: Serving the needs of the economy

cards.front: Name the four perspectives compared in the lesson on education's functions.
cards.answer: Functionalist / Marxist / Feminist / Interactionist

cards.front: How does the hidden curriculum work according to Marxists?
cards.answer: It teaches working-class children unwritten lessons about conformity, obedience and hierarchy, preparing them for routine employment.

cards.front: How does the interactionist approach to education differ from functionalism and Marxism?
cards.answer: It focuses on small-scale teacher expectations, labelling and pupil interactions shaping individual outcomes, rather than macro-level functions.

title: Respiration and Synthesis of Biological Molecules
subject: separate-sciences-ocr

cards.front: During exercise, what three ways does the body respond to meet muscles' increased energy demand?
cards.answer: Increasing heart rate / Increasing breathing rate and depth / Breaking down glycogen into glucose

cards.front: What four things are proteins essential for, according to the lesson?
cards.answer: Enzymes / Structural components (collagen, keratin) / Hormones (insulin) / Antibodies

cards.front: Why does aerobic respiration produce a much larger yield of ATP than anaerobic respiration?
cards.answer: Aerobic respiration completely breaks down glucose, transferring all its energy, while anaerobic respiration only partially breaks it down.

cards.front: Why do muscles switch to anaerobic respiration during intense exercise?
cards.answer: Because blood cannot deliver oxygen to the muscles fast enough to meet their increased energy demand.

cards.front: (Higher tier) Name the four factors the lesson gives that affect the size or direction of an induced potential difference.
cards.answer: Speed of movement / Strength of the magnetic field / Number of turns on the coil / Direction of movement or field change
items: Number of turns on the coil
Direction of movement or field change

cards.front: (Higher tier) Why is there no force on a current-carrying conductor when the current is parallel to the magnetic field?
cards.answer: The motor effect only occurs when current and field are not parallel, so a parallel current produces zero force.

cards.front: (Higher tier) Why must a step-up transformer reduce the current if it increases the voltage?
cards.answer: Since power input equals power output (VpIp = VsIs), increasing voltage means current must decrease by the same factor to conserve power.

cards.front: Name the six things on the mother's list of 'Friends'.
cards.answer: God / Our dog / Auntie Madge / The Novels of Charlotte Brontë / Slug pellets / Jeanette, at first

cards.front: Name the four physical, vivid elements of the church services described in the early chapters.
cards.answer: Speaking in tongues / Exorcisms / Laying on of hands / Passionate preaching

cards.front: Why is Jeanette completely unprepared and bewildered when she finally starts school?
cards.answer: She has been educated exclusively through the Bible with no experience of children outside the church, so the secular world does not share her mother's categories.

cards.front: How do the school scenes establish a recurring pattern in Jeanette's life?
cards.answer: They show Jeanette as an outsider wherever she goes: in the secular world because of her upbringing, and later in church because of her sexuality.

cards.front: Name the six comparison operators described in the lesson.
cards.answer: equal to == / not equal to != / less than / greater than or equal to >=

cards.front: Name the three Boolean operators covered in the lesson.
cards.answer: AND / OR / NOT

cards.front: Why does '=' not mean 'equals' in programming, unlike in maths?
cards.answer: It is an instruction to store the value on the right into the variable on the left, not a test of equality.

cards.front: Why must the registration example use AND rather than OR for age and agreeing to terms?
cards.answer: Both conditions must be true to register; using OR would let someone register by meeting just one.

title: The Berlin Wall & the Cuban Missile Crisis
subject: history-edexcel

cards.front: Name the three summit meetings between 1959 and 1961 that tried to resolve the Berlin crisis.
cards.answer: Camp David summit (1959) / Paris summit (1960) / Vienna summit (1961)

cards.front: What four options did Kennedy's ExComm advisers consider after discovering the missiles in Cuba?
cards.answer: Naval blockade / Air strike / Invasion of Cuba / Diplomacy

cards.front: Why did the Paris summit of 1960 collapse?
cards.answer: The USSR shot down an American U-2 spy plane over Soviet territory, Eisenhower refused to apologise, so Khrushchev walked out.

cards.front: Why was the Berlin refugee crisis humiliating for Khrushchev?
