cards.answer: Railroad sport-hunters / Hide hunters supplying Eastern leather factories / Encouragement by military commanders like Sheridan
items: Hide hunters supplying Eastern leather factories
Encouragement by military commanders like Sheridan

cards.front: Why did the Great Sioux War of 1876-77 break out?
cards.answer: Miners rushed into the Black Hills for gold breaking the Fort Laramie Treaty; the government failed to remove them and Lakota leaders refused to sell.

cards.front: How did the Ghost Dance movement lead directly to the Wounded Knee Massacre?
cards.answer: Alarmed reservation agents called in troops; Sitting Bull was killed by police, then the Seventh Cavalry intercepted Spotted Elk's band days later.

cards.front: Name the three things vipassana meditation systematically observes arising and passing away, according to the lesson.
cards.answer: Physical sensations / Emotions / Thoughts and perceptions

cards.front: Name the three practices that often accompany visualisation meditation in Tibetan Buddhism.
cards.answer: Mantra recitation / Mudras (hand gestures) / Contemplation of thangka paintings

cards.front: How does zazen differ in method from both samatha and vipassana?
cards.answer: Zazen doesn't focus on one object like samatha or analyse experience like vipassana, but maintains alert, open awareness while simply sitting.

cards.front: Why do Buddhists visualise a Buddha or Bodhisattva such as Avalokiteshvara?
cards.answer: Not to summon an external being, but to cultivate within themselves the qualities that figure embodies, such as compassion or wisdom.

cards.front: What three things happen in the original ending Dickens wrote before revising it?
cards.answer: Pip encounters Estella briefly in London / She has remarried after Drummle's death / They part as strangers
items: Pip encounters Estella briefly in London
She has remarried after Drummle's death

cards.front: How does the Thames function structurally during Magwitch's escape attempt?
cards.answer: It is both a physical escape route and a symbolic journey of Pip breaking free from the class prejudice oppressing his moral development.

cards.front: Why is the original bleak ending arguably more consistent with the novel's themes than the revised one?
cards.answer: Because Pip's expectations were always misguided, and a fairy-tale union with Estella would undermine that message.

title: Gas Pressure and Pressure in Fluids
subject: science-aqa

cards.front: Name the three everyday examples the lesson gives of pressure differences causing fluid to flow.
cards.answer: Drinking through a straw / Suction cups sticking to surfaces / Hydraulic systems transmitting force

cards.front: Name the three devices the lesson gives as uses of the hydraulic principle.
cards.answer: Hydraulic brakes / Car jacks / Industrial presses

cards.front: Why do aerosol cans carry warnings not to heat them?
cards.answer: Heating raises particle kinetic energy, increasing collisions in the fixed volume until pressure builds enough to cause an explosion.

cards.front: Why does a steel ship float even though steel is denser than water?
cards.answer: Its hollow shape displaces a large volume of water, creating enough upthrust to support its weight.

cards.front: Name the four types of primary storage.
cards.answer: RAM / ROM / Cache / Registers

cards.front: What three things does secondary storage provide that primary storage cannot?
cards.answer: Persistence / Capacity / Portability

cards.front: Why is unsaved work lost during a power cut?
cards.answer: Unsaved work exists only in volatile RAM, which is erased when the power supply is cut.

cards.front: How does having more RAM let more programs run at once without slowing down?
cards.answer: More RAM holds more data in quick-access memory, reducing the need to fetch data from slower secondary storage.

cards.front: Name the five factors the lesson gives that increase reaction time.
cards.answer: Tiredness / Alcohol / Drugs / Distractions / Age

cards.front: Name the four factors the lesson gives that increase braking distance.
cards.answer: Wet or icy roads / Worn tyres / Worn brakes / Higher speed

cards.front: Why does an object moving in a circle at constant speed have a changing velocity?
cards.answer: Velocity includes direction, and the object's direction is constantly changing even though its speed stays the same.

cards.front: Why does a fully loaded lorry take much longer to stop than an empty car at the same speed?
cards.answer: Its greater mass and greater kinetic energy both increase the braking distance needed to stop.

cards.front: Name the three components whose I-V characteristics are studied in the lesson.
cards.answer: Fixed resistor (ohmic conductor) / Filament lamp / Diode

cards.front: Name the three uses of an NTC thermistor given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Thermostats / Fire alarms / Engine management systems

cards.front: Why does static charge build up on insulators but not on conductors?
cards.answer: Insulators stop electrons flowing away, so charge builds up, but on conductors excess charge spreads out immediately.

cards.front: Why is the current the same at every point in a series circuit?
cards.answer: Because charge is not used up as it flows around the circuit.

cards.front: Name the four financial aims and objectives the lesson lists for a business.
cards.answer: Survival / Profit / Market share / Financial security

cards.front: Name the four non-financial aims and objectives the lesson describes for business owners.
cards.answer: Social objectives / Personal satisfaction / Challenge / Independence and control

cards.front: Why can a profitable business still run out of cash?
cards.answer: Profit is not the same as cash — customers may pay late or stock can build up, draining cash even while profit is positive.

cards.front: Why does trying to gain market share often reduce a business's short-term profit?
cards.answer: Gaining market share often requires spending more on marketing or lowering prices, which cuts short-term profit even as it builds position.

cards.front: Name the five renewable energy sources named in this topic.
cards.answer: Wind / Solar / Tidal / Hydro-electrical / Biomass

cards.front: Name the five factors a designer must balance when choosing an energy source for a product.
cards.answer: Portability / Environmental impact / Power output / Circuit/system connections / Cost

cards.front: Why does burning fossil fuels contribute to climate change?
cards.answer: Burning fossil fuels releases carbon dioxide, which contributes to climate change.

cards.front: Why are biofuels often considered more sustainable than fossil fuels?
cards.answer: The plants used to make biofuels absorb carbon dioxide as they grow.

cards.front: Name the three specific design approaches a modern director could use to address the colonial gaze in the Indian marketplace scene.
cards.answer: Soundscape using authentic Indian musical textures like tabla and raga / Costume with specific, researched cultural elements / Performance giving Indian characters the same specificity as the Reform Club gentlemen
items: Soundscape using authentic Indian musical textures like tabla and raga
Costume with specific, researched cultural elements
Performance giving Indian characters the same specificity as the Reform Club gentlemen

cards.front: Give the three examples the lesson uses to show Verne's novel is a product of the imperial imagination.
cards.answer: Indian characters are largely incidental / Aouda is defined initially by needing rescue / Native American railroad attack is a thrilling obstacle not resistance
items: Aouda is defined initially by needing rescue
Native American railroad attack is a thrilling obstacle not resistance

cards.front: Why is Fogg's obsession with the schedule linked to the theme of the British Empire?
cards.answer: Fogg's schedule obsession reflects the Victorian industrial precision of steam, rail and telegraph that made British imperialism possible.

cards.front: Why is simply staging the play as a critique of Fogg or Verne considered too simple an approach?
cards.answer: Turning the comedy into a lecture about imperialism loses the joy and energy that make the adventure work, losing the audience.

title: Genetics: DNA, Inheritance and Punnett Squares
subject: separate-sciences-edexcel

cards.front: Name the four nitrogenous bases found in DNA nucleotides.
cards.answer: Adenine / Thymine / Cytosine / Guanine

cards.front: Name the four ABO blood groups described by the codominance system.
cards.answer: Blood group A / Blood group B / Blood group AB / Blood group O

cards.front: Why was Mendel's work largely ignored during his lifetime?
cards.answer: Because he lacked a mechanism to explain his results, as chromosomes and genes weren't discovered until after his death.

cards.front: How can a mutation affect the protein a gene produces?
cards.answer: A mutation changes the DNA base sequence, altering the mRNA and amino acid sequence, which may change the protein's shape so it stops working.

cards.front: Name the three forms of human warmth Scrooge rejects in Stave 1.
cards.answer: Fred's dinner invitation / The charity collectors' appeal / Adequate coal/comfort for his clerk

cards.front: Name the three stages of Scrooge's past life shown in Stave 2.
cards.answer: A lonely, vulnerable child / A joyful apprentice under Fezziwig / A young man in love with Belle
items: A young man in love with Belle

cards.front: Why does Scrooge's transformation happen gradually across Staves 2 to 4 rather than all at once?
cards.answer: Stave 2 unlocks his emotions, Stave 3 confronts him with consequences like Tiny Tim, and Stave 4 terrifies him with his own death, cumulatively breaking his defences.

cards.front: Why does Dickens use Bob Cratchit's grief for Tiny Tim to build sympathy rather than anger?
cards.answer: Bob's simple, dignified words show helpless love without blaming Scrooge or society, making the reader feel preventing such deaths should be society's priority.

title: Work Done, Elasticity and Hooke's Law
subject: separate-sciences

cards.front: Name the four main steps in the required practical for investigating Hooke's law.
cards.answer: Hang spring from clamp stand / Measure the original length / Add masses and record new length / Calculate the extension / Plot a force-extension graph
items: Add masses and record new length

cards.front: Why does a spring not return to its original length once it passes the limit of proportionality?
cards.answer: It has been permanently deformed (inelastic deformation), so it no longer obeys Hooke's law.

cards.front: Why is a ruler with a pointer (set square) used when measuring spring length in the Hooke's law practical?
cards.answer: To reduce parallax error when measuring the length.

cards.front: What three themes does Hill use the predatory marsh landscape to embody in The Woman in Black?
cards.answer: Deception (solid ground hides quicksand) / The inescapable past (buried secrets that drag you down) / Isolation (the tide cuts off all escape)
items: The inescapable past (buried secrets that drag you down)
Isolation (the tide cuts off all escape)

cards.front: What four supernatural events does Hill use to escalate suspense, from least to most terrifying?
cards.answer: First sighting of the Woman in Black / Sound of the pony and trap / Discovery of the rocking chair / Spider's near-death in the marsh
items: First sighting of the Woman in Black
Sound of the pony and trap

cards.front: How does fog work as a technique to create uncertainty in the novel?
cards.answer: Fog obscures Kipps's vision, creating physical danger since he cannot see where he is going and uncertainty since he cannot understand what is happening.

cards.front: How does the frame narrative foreshadow the novel's tragic ending?
cards.answer: The older Kipps's inability to join in the Christmas ghost stories tells the reader that his own story ended in genuine horror.

cards.front: Name the five time expressions for the past given in the lesson.
cards.answer: letztes Jahr (last year) / letzten Sommer (last summer) / vor zwei Wochen (two weeks ago) / gestern (yesterday) / letztes Wochenende (last weekend)

cards.front: Name the five time expressions for the future given in the lesson.
cards.answer: nächstes Jahr (next year) / nächsten Sommer (next summer) / in den Sommerferien (in the summer holidays) / morgen (tomorrow) / nächstes Wochenende (next weekend)
items: in den Sommerferien (in the summer holidays)

cards.front: Why does German use 'in die' or 'in den' instead of 'nach' for countries like Switzerland, Turkey and the USA?
cards.answer: Because countries with an article use in die/in den (e.g. in die Schweiz, in die Türkei, in den USA), not nach.

cards.front: Why does 'Ich bin geschwommen' use sein instead of haben in the perfect tense?
cards.answer: Because verbs of movement, like swimming, flying and travelling, form the perfect tense with sein rather than haben.

title: The Second World War and civil rights
subject: history-ocr

cards.front: Name the ways the US government expanded its power during wartime mobilisation in the Second World War.
cards.answer: War Production Board coordinated industrial output / Federal workforce grew enormously / Taxation rose sharply to fund the war / Selective Service conscripted around 10 million / Government controlled prices, wages and rationing
items: War Production Board coordinated industrial output
Taxation rose sharply to fund the war
Government controlled prices, wages and rationing

cards.front: Why did the Fair Employment Practices Committee fail to stop discrimination in war industries?
cards.answer: It was underfunded and had no enforcement powers, so discrimination continued and the military stayed segregated.

cards.front: Why did Truman sign Executive Order 9981 to desegregate the armed forces in 1948?
cards.answer: He was influenced by reports that returning Black veterans were beaten or even killed for wearing their uniforms in the South.

title: Creating Audio with a DAW & Health and Safety
subject: music-technology

cards.front: Name the six methods the lesson gives for capturing audio and MIDI into a DAW project.
cards.answer: Recording audio tracks / Importing audio files / Recording via the interface with correct gain / Importing MIDI files / MIDI controller input (real-time performance) / MIDI programming (drawing notes on the grid)
items: Recording via the interface with correct gain
MIDI programming (drawing notes on the grid)

cards.front: Name the four main studio hazards identified in the lesson.
cards.answer: Noise / Displays and workstations / Slip, trip and fall hazards / Electrical hazards

cards.front: Why must gain be set carefully when recording audio via an interface?
cards.answer: So the signal is strong but not distorting, avoiding clipping.

cards.front: Why do studios use RCDs (residual current devices) as an electrical control measure?
cards.answer: They protect against electrocution, burns or fire caused by faulty wiring or damaged cables.

title: Planetary Geology: Earth and Its Neighbours
subject: geology-eduqas

cards.front: Name the four bodies most directly compared in planetary geology.
cards.answer: Earth / Moon / Mars / Venus

cards.front: What three pieces of evidence show Mars had past liquid water?
cards.answer: Ancient river valleys / Delta deposits at crater rims / Clay minerals that only form in liquid water
items: Clay minerals that only form in liquid water

cards.front: Why does a hot spot on Earth create a chain of volcanoes rather than one giant volcano?
cards.answer: The Pacific Plate moves over the stationary hot spot, so each new eruption forms a separate volcano in a chain.

cards.front: Why does Mars have a much thinner atmosphere than Earth today?
cards.answer: Mars lost much of its internal heat early in its history, losing its magnetic field and volcanic resupply of atmospheric gases.

cards.front: Name the four key ways Kelly uses language in DNA.
cards.answer: Phil's silence as control / Leah's verbal desperation as failed conscience / Euphemism as moral distancing / Fragmented dialogue as naturalism and urgency
items: Leah's verbal desperation as failed conscience
Fragmented dialogue as naturalism and urgency

cards.front: Why are sentences left incomplete throughout DNA?
cards.answer: Because moral reality is too uncomfortable to articulate, so language itself breaks down to represent the unsayable.

cards.front: How does Leah's rambling speech function as 'verbal filling' against Phil's silence?
cards.answer: She compulsively talks to fill the uncomfortable silence and provoke an emotional response, but every attempt fails.

cards.front: The lesson names three signature devices used in Submarine's aesthetic. What are they?
cards.answer: Saturated 1980s-throwback colour palette / Symmetrical framing and iris transitions / Super-8 inserts and voice-over narration

cards.front: Name the three named sequences the lesson analyses as worked examples in Submarine.
cards.answer: Bullying-of-Zoe playground scene / Cliff-side argument with the mother / Closing return-to-the-beach sequence

cards.front: Why is Oliver's voice-over narration in Submarine described as unreliable?
cards.answer: He is unreliable not because he lies, but because he edits and aestheticises events as he retells them.

cards.front: Why does the cliff-side argument scene use a wide shot instead of close-ups?
cards.answer: The wide shot and dwarfing coastline insist on the smallness of the drama, showing family tension observed rather than dramatised.

cards.front: Name the five hazards identified in the worked example for drilling a hole with a pillar drill.
cards.answer: Rotating drill bit / Workpiece snagging and spinning / Metal swarf ejected from the hole / Loose clothing or hair drawn into spindle / Noise from machine operation
items: Metal swarf ejected from the hole
Loose clothing or hair drawn into spindle

cards.front: Name the five levels of the hierarchy of control measures, in order from most to least effective.
cards.answer: Elimination / Substitution / Engineering controls / Administrative controls / Personal protective equipment (PPE)

cards.front: Why must a workpiece be clamped in a machine vice before drilling?
cards.answer: It reduces the risk of the workpiece spinning if the drill bit snags.

cards.front: Why should hot workpieces from brazing be left to cool before handling with bare hands?
cards.answer: Because hot metal looks the same as cold metal, so touching it could cause burns.

cards.front: Name the four industries the lesson gives for extracting raw materials used in construction.
cards.answer: Oil and gas industry / Forestry industry / Quarrying / Mining

cards.front: Name the three methods of demolition described in the lesson.
cards.answer: Explosives (controlled implosion) / Hand demolition (manual tools) / Machine demolition (excavators/robots)

cards.front: How does the hydration process make concrete hard and strong?
cards.answer: Cement reacts chemically with water, binding the aggregate particles together to form a hard, strong material as it cures.

cards.front: Why is sending demolition waste to landfill seen as the least sustainable disposal option?
cards.answer: It fails to preserve resources and carries a significant financial cost through landfill tax, unlike reuse or recycling.

title: Authority at the end of the reign and Essex's rebellion (1601)
subject: history-aqa

cards.front: Name the five things the lesson gives for why Elizabeth's authority held into the 1590s.
cards.answer: The patronage system of lands, monopolies and offices / The cult of Gloriana image / The legacy of the 1588 Armada victory / Robert Cecil's growing administrative role / The queen remaining the source of final decisions
items: The patronage system of lands, monopolies and offices
The legacy of the 1588 Armada victory
The queen remaining the source of final decisions

cards.front: Name the five crises the lesson says struck England in the 1590s.
cards.answer: War with Spain after 1588 / Tyrone's rebellion in Ireland / Four bad harvests, 1594–1597 / Outbreaks of plague / The deaths of Walsingham and Burghley
items: The deaths of Walsingham and Burghley

cards.front: Why did losing the sweet wines monopoly cause Essex's finances to collapse?
cards.answer: The monopoly let him charge a fee on every cask of imported sweet wine, and this income funded his household, agents, soldiers and followers.

cards.front: Why did Essex's followers have nowhere to go but rebellion once his patronage was withdrawn?
cards.answer: Patronage was the glue holding the elite to the Crown, so followers promised offices and rewards through Essex lost their only route to advancement.

cards.front: Name the three perspectives the lesson says should be presented when discussing stratification.
cards.answer: Functionalist – meritocratic necessity (Davis and Moore) / Marxist – serves ruling-class interests, perpetuates exploitation / Feminist – reflects patriarchy, not just merit
items: Marxist – serves ruling-class interests, perpetuates exploitation
Feminist – reflects patriarchy, not just merit

cards.front: Why does the UK class system show elements of both open and closed systems, according to the lesson?
cards.answer: Qualifications and hard work can improve life chances, but social class background remains a strong predictor of outcomes.

cards.front: Why might high earners' success not simply reflect merit, according to the sociological critique?
cards.answer: Ascribed status from family wealth or privilege still shapes access to elite positions, shown by the over-representation of privately educated people.

title: Cosmology: Redshift, Hubble's Law and the Big Bang
subject: astronomy-edexcel

cards.front: Name the three pieces of observational evidence the lesson gives for the Big Bang theory.
cards.answer: Galaxy redshifts and Hubble's law / Cosmic microwave background at 2.7 K / Quasar distribution at high redshift

cards.front: Name the three possible fates of the universe described in the lesson.
cards.answer: Big Freeze / Big Crunch / Big Rip

cards.front: How does Hubble's law imply that the universe had a beginning?
cards.answer: Running the expansion backwards shows galaxies converge to a single origin point about 13.8 billion years ago.

cards.front: Why can't dark matter be detected directly using telescopes?
cards.answer: Dark matter does not emit, absorb or reflect electromagnetic radiation, so it cannot be seen electromagnetically.

cards.front: Name the three details in The Sign of Four that show the British Empire shaping the plot.
cards.answer: The Agra treasure comes from India / Jonathan Small lost his leg to a crocodile serving in India / Tonga is brought to England from the Andaman Islands
items: The Agra treasure comes from India
Jonathan Small lost his leg to a crocodile serving in India
Tonga is brought to England from the Andaman Islands

cards.front: Name the three groups of characters Doyle uses to show London's class divide.
cards.answer: Mary Morstan, an educated but poor governess / Thaddeus Sholto, living in gaudy luxury / Dockworkers and street children (the Baker Street Irregulars)
items: Mary Morstan, an educated but poor governess
Thaddeus Sholto, living in gaudy luxury
Dockworkers and street children (the Baker Street Irregulars)

cards.front: How does Doyle use fog as more than just setting in The Sign of Four?
cards.answer: The fog represents moral confusion and hidden truths, showing the characters cannot yet see the solution to the mystery.

cards.front: Why does Holmes seem superior to the police detective Athelney Jones?
cards.answer: It reflects the popular Victorian view that official institutions were often slow and incompetent compared to brilliant individuals.

cards.front: According to the lesson's Key Fact, Viola's genuine love contrasts with three other characters' flawed attitudes to love. Name them.
cards.answer: Orsino's self-indulgence / Olivia's impulsive infatuation / Malvolio's self-serving ambition

cards.front: The lesson gives three descriptions of Malvolio's personality. What are they?
cards.answer: A killjoy who interrupts festivities / A social climber who fantasises about marrying his employer / A pompous man who takes himself too seriously
items: A social climber who fantasises about marrying his employer
A pompous man who takes himself too seriously

cards.front: Why does the lesson say Twelfth Night's comic resolution is 'incomplete' for Sir Toby?
cards.answer: He marries Maria, who designed the cruellest prank, and never reforms, unlike traditional misrule where order is restored.

cards.front: Why does the lesson suggest Orsino's connection with Cesario is more genuine than his love for Olivia?
cards.answer: He is more intimate, honest and emotionally open with Cesario, showing real love grows through companionship, not distant worship.

cards.front: Name the three levels of automation described in the lesson.
cards.answer: Manual control / CAM processes (software toolpaths on CNC) / Fully automated robotic control

cards.front: Name the four work-holding and shaping devices described for achieving consistency in production.
cards.answer: Jig / Fixture / Template / Mould

cards.front: Why is a jig unsuitable for true one-off production?
cards.answer: A jig is costly to design and becomes useless once the design changes, but one-off items are never repeated.

cards.front: Why is manual control still suitable for one-off work despite being slower?
cards.answer: It is flexible with low capital cost, and relies on the operator's judgement, which suits unique, non-repeated jobs.

cards.front: Name the five elements of the PALMW method used for describing a photo in the speaking exam.
cards.answer: Person(en) / Aktion / Location/Ort / Meinung (opinion) / Wetter (weather)

cards.front: What are the two main structures for describing physical appearance in German?
cards.answer: sein + adjective / haben + noun phrase

cards.front: How do adjective endings change after 'einen' in the masculine accusative case?
cards.answer: The adjective takes the ending -en, for example 'einen schwarzen Bart'.

cards.front: How does word order change when a German sentence starts with a time or location phrase?
cards.answer: The verb still comes second (V2 rule), so the subject moves after the verb, e.g. 'Im Vordergrund sehe ich einen Mann.'

cards.front: Name the six Hindu festivals specifically required for study.
cards.answer: Holi / Navaratri / Diwali / Maha Shivaratri / Ganesh Chaturthi / Raksha Bandhan

cards.front: Why is harming the natural world seen as a spiritual concern in Hinduism, not just a practical one?
cards.answer: Because Brahman pervades all of creation, so harming nature is harming something sacred.

cards.front: Why is Ganesh worshipped at the beginning of any new enterprise?
cards.answer: Because he is the remover of obstacles (Vighnaharta) and the patron of beginnings.

cards.front: The lesson names four types of fan production that digital networks have made accessible to millions. What are they?
cards.answer: Fan fiction / Fan videos / Commentary channels / Cosplay documentation

cards.front: Name the three negative dynamics of stan culture the lesson describes.
cards.answer: Harassment of critics / Extreme parasocial attachment / Fans turning on creators when disappointed
items: Fans turning on creators when disappointed

cards.front: How does Gauntlett's view of the audience differ from the passive-audience or hypodermic model?
cards.answer: He argued audiences are always active readers who pick and choose what resonates, not passive absorbers of media values.

cards.front: How does second-screen viewing turn watching television into an active social practice?
cards.answer: Audiences simultaneously tweet reactions, look up background information, read others' responses and join live comment threads while watching.

cards.front: Name the three types of sewa identified in Sikh teaching.
cards.answer: Tan – physical service using the body / Man – mental service using the mind / Dhan – material service using resources
items: Tan – physical service using the body
Man – mental service using the mind

cards.front: How does the sangat support Sikhs during times of difficulty such as bereavement or illness?
cards.answer: It supports members practically and emotionally, expressing Sikh teaching on the equality and interdependence of all people.

cards.front: Why do amritdhari Sikhs have a deeper formal commitment to sewa than sahajdhari Sikhs?
cards.answer: Amritdhari Sikhs are initiated members of the Khalsa, so sewa is a dimension of the vows they have taken.

title: Who Makes a Play: Roles in Professional Theatre
subject: drama-aqa

cards.front: Name the four things the theatre manager is responsible for regarding the audience's experience of the building.
cards.answer: Box office / Front-of-house staff / Venue licensing / Marketing

cards.front: Name the four main design roles the lesson describes in a quick overview.
cards.answer: Set designer / Lighting designer / Sound designer / Costume designer

cards.front: Why can two professional productions of the same play look and feel completely different?
cards.answer: Once a playwright hands over the script they have no further creative authority, so each director interprets the text as they see fit.

cards.front: Why must an understudy be ready to perform without a full rehearsal?
cards.answer: If the lead performer is ill or injured, the understudy must step in so the production runs seamlessly for the audience.

cards.front: Name the three main areas of UK legislation the lesson says affect businesses directly.
cards.answer: Employment law / Health and safety law / Consumer law

cards.front: Name the five risks the lesson lists that every business faces.
cards.answer: New rivals arriving / Laws changing / Costs rising / Customers changing taste / Economies tipping into recession

cards.front: Why does the lesson describe legislation as a 'floor' for business behaviour?
cards.answer: Because it sets the minimum standard of behaviour businesses must meet, not an ideal to aim for.

cards.front: Why do the costs of following legislation hit a small café harder than a large retailer?
cards.answer: Because the same costs bite proportionally harder on a small business than on a large one.

cards.front: Name the three people who remain with Hero after the men leave the church.
cards.answer: Beatrice / Benedick / Friar Francis

cards.front: Why does Beatrice demand that Benedick 'kill Claudio'?
cards.answer: It forces Benedick to choose between male solidarity with Claudio and his love for her, testing if his love is genuine.

cards.front: How does Hero's faked death give her power in the play?
cards.answer: Her 'death' gives her power only through absence, showing that in Messina's patriarchy a woman's removal is more effective than her presence.

cards.front: Name the four marriages Austen uses for her structural comparison on the theme of marriage.
cards.answer: Elizabeth and Darcy / Jane and Bingley / Charlotte and Collins / Lydia and Wickham

cards.front: Why does Darcy insist on keeping his rescue of Lydia a secret?
cards.answer: He acts out of genuine care rather than wanting credit, proving his moral transformation is real, not performative.

cards.front: How does Austen show that Darcy's pride is redirected rather than destroyed by the novel's end?
cards.answer: He remains proud, but his pride now expresses itself through principled, generous action rather than social condescension.

cards.front: Name the four abstract nouns Browning piles up to describe the moment in 'Now'.
cards.answer: Thought / Feeling / Soul / Sense

cards.front: Name the four other anthology poems the lesson links to 'Now' for comparison.
cards.answer: Looking at Your Hands (Martin Carter) / Poem for My Love (June Jordan) / Flirtation (Rita Dove) / The Perseverance (Raymond Antrobus)

cards.front: Why does the speaker ask the lover to ignore the past and future in 'Now'?
cards.answer: So the speaker can 'make perfect the present', letting one moment stand in for a whole life.

cards.front: How does the constant use of dashes and enjambment in 'Now' support its meaning?
cards.answer: They make the sense spill from line to line, creating a voice too excited to stop, fitting a poem about refusing to let a moment end.

title: The Endocrine System and Blood Glucose Control
subject: separate-sciences

cards.front: Name the five hormones the lesson says the pituitary gland produces.
cards.answer: Growth hormone / FSH / LH / ADH / TSH

cards.front: Name the six endocrine glands described in the lesson.
cards.answer: Pituitary gland / Thyroid gland / Pancreas / Adrenal glands / Ovaries / Testes

cards.front: (Higher tier) Why is the insulin and glucagon system described as negative feedback?
cards.answer: Because insulin lowers blood glucose and glucagon raises it, so together they cancel out changes and return glucose to normal.

cards.front: How do the nervous and endocrine systems work together to coordinate the body?
cards.answer: The hypothalamus in the brain links the two systems so they work together to coordinate body functions.

cards.front: Name the three reasons the lesson gives for why the ferrous/non-ferrous classification matters in engineering.
cards.answer: Ferrous metals are generally magnetic (useful for sorting/recycling) / Ferrous metals corrode through rusting / The two families have different density and conductivity profiles
items: Ferrous metals are generally magnetic (useful for sorting/recycling)
The two families have different density and conductivity profiles

cards.front: Name the four ways the lesson says engineers can prevent rusting.
cards.answer: Painting / Galvanising with zinc / Applying plastic coatings / Choosing a different material like stainless steel or aluminium
items: Choosing a different material like stainless steel or aluminium

cards.front: Why does rust keep weakening a mild steel component instead of protecting it?
cards.answer: Rust is porous, so it keeps allowing oxygen and water through to attack the metal beneath, unlike a protective oxide layer.

cards.front: How does galvanising protect steel from rusting?
cards.answer: It coats the steel with zinc, which corrodes preferentially, protecting the steel underneath from rusting.

title: Advertising, Sales Promotion and Public Relations
subject: cambridge-nationals-enterprise-and-marketing

cards.front: Name the seven digital advertising mediums given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Social media / Social networks / Websites / Online banners / SMS (text messages) / Podcasts / Vlogs

cards.front: How does sales promotion differ from advertising in what it aims to achieve?
cards.answer: Sales promotion uses time-limited tactics to get customers to buy now, while advertising builds awareness over time.

cards.front: Why can using discounts too often harm a start-up trying to build a premium image?
cards.answer: It may train customers to wait for a deal rather than paying full price for the product.

cards.front: What three rules did M.R. James set out for writing ghost stories, which Hill follows?
cards.answer: The setting should be recognisably real / The ghost should be malevolent / The story should build gradually from normality to horror
items: The setting should be recognisably real
The story should build gradually from normality to horror

cards.front: Name the three ghost story writers whose techniques Hill combines in The Woman in Black.
cards.answer: M.R. James / Charles Dickens / Henry James

cards.front: How does M.R. James's typical ghost story plot pattern relate to Arthur Kipps' journey in The Woman in Black?
cards.answer: An educated, rational man travels to an isolated place connected to the past, disturbs something, and is punished, as Kipps is at Eel Marsh House.

cards.front: Why does Arthur's inability to tell a ghost story on Christmas Eve matter for how we read his account?
cards.answer: When pressed to contribute he cannot, signalling his story is not mere entertainment but something that has genuinely damaged him.

cards.front: Name the three dimensions of development the lesson describes.
cards.answer: Economic development (wealth and jobs) / Social development (health, education, quality of life) / Environmental development (sustainability for the future)
items: Social development (health, education, quality of life)

cards.front: Which three countries top the HDI rankings, according to the lesson?
cards.answer: Iceland / Norway / Switzerland

cards.front: Why does climate change widen the development gap between LIDCs and richer countries?
cards.answer: LIDCs contribute least to global emissions but suffer the worst effects from droughts, floods and food-supply shocks.

cards.front: Why is the cycle of underdevelopment hard for unequal countries to break?
cards.answer: Unequal countries struggle to attract investment, and without investment they struggle to develop further.

cards.front: Name the four Catholic elements of worship that Puritans wanted removed from Church of England services.
cards.answer: Vestments / Crucifixes / Kneeling at Communion / The sign of the cross at baptism
items: The sign of the cross at baptism

cards.front: Why did the Marprelate Tracts (1588–89) harden Elizabeth's government's stance towards Puritans?
cards.answer: Their savage, scurrilous attacks on bishops shocked even Puritan sympathisers, making Elizabeth less willing to tolerate even moderate Puritan demands.

cards.front: How does the revisionist view (Peter Lake) of the Puritan threat differ from the traditional view?
cards.answer: It argues most Puritans were loyal 'church Puritans' working within the Church, so Elizabeth's firm response was overkill, unlike the traditional view of serious danger.

cards.front: Name the three relationships that Act 1 of A Taste of Honey establishes.
cards.answer: Jo and Helen / Jo and the Boy / Helen and Peter

cards.front: Name the three consequences that Act 2 of A Taste of Honey shows.
cards.answer: Jo's pregnancy / Geof's care for Jo / Helen's return

cards.front: How does the jazz music work in A Taste of Honey's scenes between Jo and the Boy?
cards.answer: It is associated with the Boy and adds a sensual, dreamlike quality to Jo's brief period of happiness.

cards.front: Why is the published text of A Taste of Honey seen as a collaborative work, not just Delaney's writing?
cards.answer: Littlewood reshaped the script through improvisational rehearsals, adding the jazz, comic timing and music hall elements.

title: Simon de Montfort and the Birth of Parliament, 1258-1265
subject: history-aqa

cards.front: What three things did the Provisions of Oxford (1258) set up to control Henry III?
cards.answer: 15-member council of barons supervising the king / Parliament to meet three times a year / Royal sheriffs answerable to local communities, not just the king
items: 15-member council of barons supervising the king
Parliament to meet three times a year
Royal sheriffs answerable to local communities, not just the king

cards.front: What three outcomes followed the Battle of Evesham in 1265?
cards.answer: De Montfort was killed and mutilated / The reform movement collapsed / Henry III was restored to full power and de Montfort's lands were confiscated
items: De Montfort was killed and mutilated
Henry III was restored to full power and de Montfort's lands were confiscated

cards.front: Why did the barons refuse to pay for the Sicilian Business?
cards.answer: They saw it as a foreign vanity project funded from English pockets, on top of their existing anger at Henry's foreign favourites.

cards.front: How did the Provisions of Oxford build on the principle set by Magna Carta?
cards.answer: Magna Carta said the king must take counsel before raising taxes; the Provisions turned that into a permanent supervisory baronial council.

cards.front: Name the five stages considered in a full lifecycle assessment (LCA) of a paper or board product.
cards.answer: Raw material extraction / Manufacturing / Distribution / Use phase / End of life

cards.front: In the FSDU case study, name the three board materials used and what each is for.
cards.answer: Corrugated double-wall board base for structural rigidity / Laminated duplex board graphics panels for grease resistance and colour / Solid white board header card with UV spot varnish for visibility
items: Corrugated double-wall board base for structural rigidity
Laminated duplex board graphics panels for grease resistance and colour
Solid white board header card with UV spot varnish for visibility

cards.front: Why does a paper mill run as a continuous 24-hour process rather than stopping and starting?
cards.answer: It runs constantly to justify the energy cost of maintaining the operating temperatures needed for the process.

cards.front: How does NFC paper let a smartphone read product information without any visible electronics?
cards.answer: A thin conductive antenna and chip are embedded within the paper sheet, letting a phone read data simply by tapping the packaging.

title: The Magisterium, Sacred Art and Catholic Funeral Rites
subject: religious-studies-eduqas

cards.front: Name the three principal rites that make up the Catholic Order of Christian Funerals in Britain.
cards.answer: The vigil (prayer service the evening before) / The funeral Mass / The rite of committal at the graveside or crematorium
items: The vigil (prayer service the evening before)
The rite of committal at the graveside or crematorium

cards.front: What five key symbols are used in the Catholic funeral rite?
cards.answer: The Paschal Candle / Sprinkling the coffin with holy water / A white pall over the coffin / A copy of the Gospels or a cross on the coffin / The use of incense
items: Sprinkling the coffin with holy water
A white pall over the coffin
A copy of the Gospels or a cross on the coffin

cards.front: Why is the Paschal Candle used at both baptisms and funerals?
cards.answer: Baptism begins a person's share in Christ's paschal mystery, which death completes, so the same candle marks both stages of passing from death to life.

cards.front: How did Vatican II's Sacrosanctum Concilium reform the celebration of the Mass?
cards.answer: It permitted the Mass to be celebrated in vernacular languages instead of Latin and emphasised the active participation of all the faithful.

cards.front: What four qualities did the gods each give to Pandora, according to Hesiod?
cards.answer: Beauty / Charm / Cunning / Deceit

cards.front: In the Iliad's 'viewing from the walls' scene, which four Greek leaders does Helen identify to Priam?
cards.answer: Agamemnon / Odysseus / Ajax / Idomeneus

cards.front: Why did Zeus send Pandora to humanity?
cards.answer: Zeus was angry that Prometheus had stolen fire for humanity, so he sent Pandora as punishment.

cards.front: Why did Medea kill her own children?
cards.answer: To punish Jason as deeply as possible for abandoning her to marry a Greek princess.

title: Search and Destroy, My Lai and Protest
subject: history-aqa

cards.front: Name the three structural problems that caused search-and-destroy to fail.
cards.answer: Vietcong chose when and where to fight (80% of engagements enemy-initiated) / Cleared ground was simply re-occupied once US units left / Body-count metric corrupted reporting
items: Vietcong chose when and where to fight (80% of engagements enemy-initiated)
Cleared ground was simply re-occupied once US units left

cards.front: What three things does the lesson give for why US public opinion turned so hard against the war?
cards.answer: Nightly TV footage of the 'living-room war' / The Tet Offensive contradicting official optimism / The 1971 Pentagon Papers revealing government lies
items: Nightly TV footage of the 'living-room war'
The Tet Offensive contradicting official optimism
The 1971 Pentagon Papers revealing government lies

cards.front: How did the draft make the Vietnam War personal for many young Americans?
cards.answer: Young men were called up, disproportionately working-class and African American, while wealthier students could defer through college.

cards.front: Why is Vietnam described as the first 'living-room war'?
cards.answer: TV crews followed combat units and networks broadcast nightly footage of body bags, burning villages and wounded marines into American homes.

title: Time Series, Trends and Rates of Change
subject: statistics-aqa

cards.front: Name the four steps the lesson gives for interpreting a time series graph.
cards.answer: State the overall trend / Identify any seasonal pattern / Note any unusual features / Quantify where possible

cards.front: Name the four specific rate measures the lesson says are used in real UK contexts.
cards.answer: Birth rate / Death rate / House price change / Unemployment rate

cards.front: Why doesn't a rise in the number of deaths necessarily mean mortality is getting worse?
cards.answer: The population may have grown or aged, so the death rate is needed to put the change in proportion.

cards.front: How does a cyclic trend differ from a seasonal trend?
cards.answer: A cyclic trend rises and falls over a longer, less regular timescale, unlike a seasonal trend which repeats at a fixed calendar point.

title: Fats, Fruit & Vegetables and Raising Agents
subject: food-preparation-and-nutrition-aqa

cards.front: Name the four functional properties of fats and oils identified in the lesson.
cards.answer: Shortening / Aeration / Plasticity / Emulsification

cards.front: Name the four types of raising agent covered in the lesson.
cards.answer: Chemical / Mechanical / Steam / Biological

cards.front: Why must water only be added after the fat has been rubbed into the flour when making shortcrust pastry?
cards.answer: If water is added before the fat coats the flour, gluten begins developing immediately, making the pastry tough instead of short.

cards.front: Why is butter at room temperature (around 18–20°C) ideal for creaming?
cards.answer: Cold butter cannot trap air efficiently, while very warm butter releases the trapped air before the cake sets.

title: Homesteaders, Railroads and the Closing Frontier
subject: history-aqa

cards.front: Name the four big farming problems the lesson gives for settlers on the Great Plains.
cards.answer: Lack of timber / Lack of water / Tough sod / Crop failure from drought or pests
items: Crop failure from drought or pests

cards.front: Name the four big solutions the lesson gives to the Plains farming problems.
cards.answer: Sod homes / Windmill-pumped wells / John Deere's steel plough / Dry farming with drought-resistant wheat

cards.front: Why did railroad companies advertise the West and run cheap emigrant trains for settlers?
cards.answer: They calculated that filled-up land along the line meant freight to ship in both directions, and they profited from selling land to settlers.

cards.front: How did barbed wire bring about the end of the open range cattle system?
cards.answer: Cheap, mass-producible barbed wire let homesteaders fence their fields, enclosing the once-unfenced grassland from the mid-1870s onward.

cards.front: Name the five Ks that Khalsa Sikhs commit to wearing.
cards.answer: kesh (uncut hair) / kangha (small comb) / kara (steel bracelet) / kaccha (modest undergarment) / kirpan (small sword)

cards.front: Name the three practical expressions of equality in Sikh life given in the lesson.
cards.answer: sangat (equal congregation) / langar (community kitchen) / sewa (selfless service)

cards.front: Why is the Guru Granth Sahib treated as if it were a living being in the gurdwara?
cards.answer: Because it holds the eternal authority of a living Guru, so it is honoured like royalty: bowed to, fanned, and ceremonially put to rest at night.

cards.front: Why are Sikhs cremated rather than buried after death?
cards.answer: Cremation symbolises the soul's release from the cycle of rebirth, as the body returns to the elements while the soul journeys toward liberation.

cards.front: Name the three economic forces the lesson says influence almost every business decision.
cards.answer: Interest rates / Level of employment / Consumer spending

cards.front: Name the three examples of automation firms use to cut wage costs given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Self-checkout tills at Tesco / Order-at-table apps at Wetherspoon / AI chatbots for customer service

cards.front: How can rising interest rates end up reducing employment and incomes?
cards.answer: Rising rates slow spending, which reduces demand, which can reduce employment, weakening incomes and cutting spending further.

cards.front: Why might a business automate jobs when it is struggling to recruit staff?
cards.answer: Automation replaces some jobs, saving on rising wage costs while filling gaps left by hard-to-recruit vacancies.

cards.front: Name the four fields where nanoparticles are applied, according to the lesson.
cards.answer: Sunscreen / Medicine / Electronics / Catalysis

cards.front: Name the three example alloys given in the lesson, with their components.
cards.answer: Steel (iron + carbon) / Brass (copper + zinc) / Bronze (copper + tin)

cards.front: In the worked example, why does splitting a large cube into smaller cubes increase the surface area to volume ratio?
cards.answer: Cutting into smaller cubes increases total surface area while total volume stays the same.

cards.front: How does a composite material achieve properties that neither of its components has alone?
cards.answer: It combines materials so each contributes its best property, exploiting the stiffness of the fibres and toughness of the polymer matrix.

cards.front: How does Orwell contrast the setting with Clover's feelings after the executions?
cards.answer: He sets her silent despair against a clear spring evening and a farm that has never looked more desirable, heightening the tragedy.

cards.front: Why does Squealer say 'Beasts of England' must be banned?
cards.answer: He claims the song is no longer necessary because the Rebellion is complete and the better society it promised has been achieved.

title: Interpreting Data on Health and Participation
subject: physical-education-edexcel

cards.front: Name the five common errors the lesson identifies in data interpretation questions.
cards.answer: Describing a trend without quoting figures / Quoting figures without interpretation / Making claims beyond the data / Forgetting units on calculations / Confusing percentage point with percentage change
items: Describing a trend without quoting figures
Confusing percentage point with percentage change

cards.front: Why does the worked example suggest sport participation declines as socio-economic status decreases?
cards.answer: Higher costs like club fees, equipment and transport, plus less flexible working hours for lower-income groups, act as barriers.

cards.front: Why can't you claim a policy caused a change in participation just because the data shows a trend?
cards.answer: Data can show trends and suggest explanations, but you cannot state a cause definitively unless the data explicitly shows it.

title: Theme for English B — Langston Hughes
subject: english-literature-ocr

cards.front: Name the three short quotations from 'Theme for English B' worth memorising for part b) analysis.
cards.answer: "true" / "instructor" / "I hear New York too"

cards.front: Which four other anthology poems does the lesson suggest comparing with 'Theme for English B'?
cards.answer: 'Holy Thursday' / 'Cold Knap Lake' / 'Tea With Our Grandmothers' / 'Venus's-flytraps'

cards.front: Why does Hughes use alliteration in the phrase 'Bessie, bop, or Bach'?
cards.answer: It links a blues singer, jazz and classical music through their shared 'b' sound, showing his tastes can't be sorted into racial categories.

cards.front: How does the poem's free verse form reflect the speaker's writing process?
cards.answer: Lines of very different lengths capture the drifting, thinking voice of someone composing the assignment aloud.

cards.front: The lesson names three types of characters Delaney included that were rarely seen on stage before. What are they?
cards.answer: a single mother / a mixed-race relationship / a gay man

cards.front: According to the lesson, what three options did women like Helen have in 1950s Britain?
cards.answer: marriage / factory work / dependence on men

cards.front: How does Helen's reliance on men throughout the play reflect the lesson's context on 1950s women?
cards.answer: It reflects the limited options available to working-class women in the 1950s, who could rely only on marriage, factory work, or dependence on men.

cards.front: Why is Jo's line 'I'm not just talented, I'm geniused' significant in terms of context?
cards.answer: It represents a new generation of women refusing to accept the limited options available to working-class women in the 1950s.

cards.front: Name the four advantages of technology given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Communicate easily with people worldwide / Useful for homework research / Stay in touch with family and friends / A good way to have fun
items: Stay in touch with family and friends
A good way to have fun

cards.front: Name the four disadvantages of technology given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Too much time in front of the screen / Cyberbullying is a serious problem / Bad for health, not enough exercise / Risk of addiction
items: Too much time in front of the screen
Bad for health, not enough exercise

cards.front: Why does French use both 'pour' and 'afin de' when giving purpose sentences in French exams?
cards.answer: Both mean 'in order to' and take an infinitive, but using both shows you can vary your language.

cards.front: Why can the French word 'portable' cause confusion, and how do you make its meaning clear?
cards.answer: 'Portable' alone can mean phone or laptop; 'mon portable' usually means phone, while 'un ordinateur portable' specifically means laptop.

cards.front: Name the three models of atomic structure the lesson describes in order of development.
cards.answer: Thomson's plum pudding model / Rutherford's nuclear model (dense positive nucleus) / Bohr's model (electrons in fixed energy levels/shells)
items: Bohr's model (electrons in fixed energy levels/shells)

cards.front: Name the three sources of error in density experiments given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Reading the measuring cylinder at an angle (parallax error) / Not drying the object before measuring mass / Air bubbles clinging to the object during displacement
items: Reading the measuring cylinder at an angle (parallax error)
Not drying the object before measuring mass
Air bubbles clinging to the object during displacement

cards.front: Why did the alpha particle scattering experiment cause the plum pudding model to be abandoned?
cards.answer: Most alpha particles passed straight through but some deflected or bounced back, showing atoms have a tiny, dense, positively charged nucleus, which plum pudding couldn't explain.

cards.front: Why does density drop dramatically when water boils to steam?
cards.answer: Mass stays the same but the volume increases enormously as particles spread far apart, so the density decreases greatly.

title: Visual Illusions and Gregory's Constructivist Theory
subject: psychology-aqa

cards.front: Name the six illusions the lesson uses as evidence for Gregory's constructivist theory.
cards.answer: Ponzo illusion / Müller-Lyer illusion / Rubin's vase / Necker cube / Kanizsa triangle / Ames Room

cards.front: Why does perception flip between two interpretations in Rubin's vase and the Necker cube?
cards.answer: The brain cannot settle on one best-guess for figure and ground (or which face is front), so it alternates between equally plausible interpretations.

cards.front: Why is top-down processing harder to study scientifically than bottom-up processing?
cards.answer: It is difficult to isolate the effect of prior knowledge because everyone's past experience differs.

cards.front: Name the three components whose I-V characteristics you need to investigate.
cards.answer: Fixed resistors / Filament lamps / Diodes

cards.front: What equipment do you connect to investigate a component's I-V characteristics?
cards.answer: Variable resistor / Ammeter / Power supply / Voltmeter (in parallel across the component)

cards.front: Why does total resistance decrease when more resistors are added in parallel?
cards.answer: Because adding more resistors in parallel gives the current more paths to flow through.

cards.front: Why does the total current from the battery increase when more resistors are added in parallel?
cards.answer: Adding resistors in parallel decreases total resistance, which increases the total current from the supply.

cards.front: Name the four key terms studied in social influence.
cards.answer: Obedience / Conformity / Deindividuation / Bystander effect

cards.front: Name the five ways the lesson suggests blind obedience can be reduced.
cards.answer: Exposure to a disobedient role model / Education about situational pressures / Encouraging personal responsibility / Removing anonymity / Allowing time for reflection
items: Exposure to a disobedient role model

cards.front: How does having to answer publicly rather than privately affect conformity?
cards.answer: Giving an answer publicly increases conformity because people fear standing out or being judged if they disagree with the majority.

cards.front: How does feeling anonymous in a crowd lead to deindividuation?
cards.answer: Wearing similar clothing or a mask, or being in darkness or noise, makes people feel anonymous, reducing their sense of personal accountability.

title: Religion and race: the Bible Belt and the KKK
subject: history-eduqas

cards.front: Name the five groups the lesson says the 1920s Klan targeted.
cards.answer: Black Americans / Catholics / Jews / Immigrants / Trade unionists

cards.front: Name the five areas of public life the lesson says Jim Crow laws segregated.
cards.answer: Schools / Transport / Restaurants / Hospitals / Courtrooms

cards.front: Why did the Scopes Trial embarrass William Jennings Bryan and fundamentalism?
cards.answer: The trial was broadcast live on radio, letting millions hear Darrow cross-examine Bryan, who struggled to answer questions about the age of the Earth.

cards.front: Why did the 1920s Klan attract millions of members across the North, Midwest and South?
cards.answer: It appealed to working-class white Protestants who felt threatened by immigration, urbanisation and social change.

cards.front: Name the three main ways the lesson says humans modify UK ecosystems.
cards.answer: Mechanised farming and fishing for food / Wind farms and fracking for energy / Reservoirs and water transfer schemes for water
items: Mechanised farming and fishing for food
Wind farms and fracking for energy
Reservoirs and water transfer schemes for water

cards.front: Name the four factors that govern where UK wind farms are located.
cards.answer: Physical geography (wind, seabed, upland exposure) / Planning policy (excludes areas of outstanding natural beauty) / Grid connection (proximity to high-voltage cables) / Public acceptance
items: Planning policy (excludes areas of outstanding natural beauty)

cards.front: Why was fracking at Preston New Road paused in the UK?
cards.answer: It caused small earthquakes up to 2.9 magnitude and faced intense local opposition.

cards.front: Why did building reservoirs like Kielder Water and the Lake District reservoirs harm the environment?
cards.answer: They flooded valleys, displaced communities and altered downstream river flow.

cards.front: Name the five central themes this lesson identifies in Much Ado About Nothing.
cards.answer: Deception and Noting / Honour and Shame / Love and Gender / Wit and Language / Appearance versus Reality

cards.front: What are the three steps for structuring a theme-based Shakespeare essay?
cards.answer: Extract analysis / Whole-play links / Evaluate

cards.front: Why is Benedick's challenge to Claudio described as the play's most significant act?
cards.answer: He chooses Hero's word over male loyalty, breaking the honour code and redefining honour as moral courage rather than reputation.

cards.front: Why is Claudio and Hero's love fragile compared to Beatrice and Benedick's?
cards.answer: It is based on visual attraction and convention, so a false appearance created by Don John's trick can destroy it.

cards.front: Name the five types of home given in the lesson, with their French words.
cards.answer: une maison (individuelle) - detached house / un appartement - flat/apartment / une maison jumelée - semi-detached house / une maison mitoyenne - terraced house / une ferme - farm/farmhouse

cards.front: Name the four forms of 'il y a' given in the lesson for different tenses/negatives.
cards.answer: il y a - there is/are / il y avait - there was/were / il y aura - there will be / il n'y a pas de - there is no/isn't any
items: il y aura - there will be
il n'y a pas de - there is no/isn't any

cards.front: Why do adjectives like grand, petit, beau, joli and vieux come before the noun in French, unlike most adjectives?
cards.answer: They are common adjectives that the lesson states come before the noun, while most other adjectives come after it.

cards.front: Why is 'une grande cuisine' spelled with 'grande' but 'un petit jardin' spelled with 'petit'?
cards.answer: Adjectives must agree with the noun's gender, so they change form for feminine nouns like cuisine and masculine nouns like jardin.

title: Ethics in Sport: Sportsmanship, Gamesmanship and Deviance
subject: physical-education-ocr

cards.front: Name the four examples of deviant behaviour given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Using performance-enhancing drugs / Deliberately injuring an opponent / Match-fixing / Persistent verbal abuse of officials

cards.front: Name three golf etiquette customs the lesson describes.
cards.answer: Repair divots / Rake bunkers / Maintain silence when others are playing
items: Maintain silence when others are playing

cards.front: Why does a win-at-all-costs culture lead to deviant behaviour in sport?
cards.answer: Because winning is prioritised above all other values by athletes, coaches, clubs or the media, gradually eroding ethical boundaries.

cards.front: How do financial incentives amplify a win-at-all-costs culture in elite sport?
cards.answer: Prize money, sponsorship and status attached to winning create intense pressure on performers to succeed at any cost.

cards.front: Name the five aspects of Elizabethan society the lesson says you must understand as context for Romeo and Juliet.
cards.answer: Attitudes to love / Marriage / Family honour / Gender roles / Religion

cards.front: What three things does Juliet's refusal to marry Paris challenge at once, according to the lesson?
cards.answer: Patriarchal authority / Religious expectations / Family honour

cards.front: Why is Romeo's love for Rosaline described as performative rather than genuine?
cards.answer: He speaks in contradictory oxymorons like 'loving hate', showing he is performing the role of a lover rather than truly feeling love.

cards.front: Why does Romeo and Juliet's secret marriage act as a trap as well as a bond?
cards.answer: Marriage was a sacred, unbreakable sacrament, so once secretly married Juliet was already wed before God and could not marry Paris.

title: Circuit Symbols, Voltage and Current Rules
subject: electronics-eduqas

cards.front: Name the four test instruments the lesson says you need to know how to connect and use.
cards.answer: Voltmeter / Ammeter / Logic probe / Oscilloscope

cards.front: Name the three types of waveform a signal generator produces.
cards.answer: Sine wave / Square wave / Triangular wave

cards.front: Why does a voltmeter have very high input resistance?
cards.answer: So it draws negligible current, meaning it doesn't affect the circuit it's measuring.

cards.front: Why can setting a multimeter to the wrong mode damage it?
cards.answer: On the current setting it has almost zero resistance, so connecting it in parallel across a supply can damage it.

cards.front: Name the four potential benefits of autonomous vehicles given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Reduced road accidents caused by human error / Improved mobility for people who cannot drive / Smoother traffic flow / Reduced need for parking in cities
items: Reduced road accidents caused by human error
Improved mobility for people who cannot drive
Reduced need for parking in cities

cards.front: Name the three main categories of environmental impact of digital technology.
cards.answer: Manufacturing / Energy consumption in use / Disposal

cards.front: Why is hacking a serious risk for autonomous vehicles?
cards.answer: Because the vehicle is essentially a computer on wheels, hacking could let someone manipulate it remotely, creating a physical safety risk.

cards.front: How does manufacturing electronic devices harm the environment?
cards.answer: Mining metals like lithium and cobalt for devices causes habitat destruction, water pollution and carbon emissions, even before use.

title: Act 3: Eric, the Speech & the Twist
subject: english-literature-ocr

cards.front: Name the three people or things Mrs Birling deflects blame onto in Act 3.
cards.answer: Eva Smith ('she had only herself to blame') / Eric ('I didn't know — I didn't understand') / The Inspector (calling his manner 'rude and assertive')
items: Eva Smith ('she had only herself to blame')
Eric ('I didn't know — I didn't understand')
The Inspector (calling his manner 'rude and assertive')

cards.front: Name the three steps the older generation take to prove Inspector Goole wasn't real.
cards.answer: Gerald meets a police sergeant who knows no such inspector / Birling rings the chief constable to confirm it / Gerald rings the infirmary and no girl has died
items: Gerald meets a police sergeant who knows no such inspector
Birling rings the chief constable to confirm it
Gerald rings the infirmary and no girl has died

cards.front: Why does the lesson describe Eric's alcoholism as 'a product of privilege'?
cards.answer: He drinks because he can afford to, nobody in the family holds him accountable, and his father's emotional distance leaves him without guidance.

cards.front: Why does the Inspector's phrase 'millions and millions of Eva Smiths and John Smiths' matter?
cards.answer: It elevates Eva Smith from an individual victim into a symbol representing all working-class people.

cards.front: Name the stages of Mickey's decline that Russell shows across the play.
cards.answer: Energetic teenager / Factory worker / Unemployed man / Criminal / Prisoner / Medicated shell of himself

cards.front: Why does Russell shift from upbeat songs to sombre ones as the play moves into adolescence and adulthood?
cards.answer: The musical form compresses emotion in ways dialogue cannot, and the darkening songs mirror the play's darkening tone.

cards.front: Why does Mickey's childhood admiration for Eddie turn into toxic resentment in adulthood?
cards.answer: Class inequality destroys Mickey's self-esteem, friendships and mental health, curdling his harmless admiration into resentment.

cards.front: Name the three things self-management programmes help individuals do.
cards.answer: Identify triggers for substance use / Develop coping strategies / Set goals for reducing or stopping use
items: Set goals for reducing or stopping use

cards.front: Name the two types of therapy for addiction described in the lesson.
cards.answer: Aversion therapy / Self-management programmes

cards.front: How does social learning theory explain why people imitate peers who use substances?
cards.answer: Observing peers use substances and seeing them rewarded socially or through pleasure increases the likelihood of imitation.

cards.front: Why might combining aversion therapy with self-management programmes be more effective than using either alone?
cards.answer: Aversion therapy works quickly but may not stop relapse, while self-management is more comprehensive, so combining both improves outcomes.

title: Identity and Diversity in the UK
subject: citizenship-aqa

cards.front: What four levels does the lesson say shape a person's identity?
cards.answer: Individual level / Group level / National level / Global level

cards.front: Which religions does the lesson name as practised in the UK, alongside a growing group with no religion?
cards.answer: Christianity / Islam / Hinduism / Sikhism / Judaism / Buddhism

cards.front: Why does the lesson say identity is not fixed?
cards.answer: It shifts over time as a person's circumstances, relationships and experiences change.

cards.front: Why does having multiple identities not mean someone is disloyal to the UK?
cards.answer: Because these identities reinforce rather than compete with one another in most people's experience.

cards.front: Name the four monosyllabic adjectives given in the lesson that gain an umlaut in the comparative.
cards.answer: warm → wärmer / kalt → kälter / gesund → gesünder / scharf → schärfer

cards.front: Name the five key past participles for food verbs given in the lesson.
cards.answer: essen → gegessen / trinken → getrunken / bestellen → bestellt / kochen → gekocht / finden → gefunden

cards.front: Why does the conjugated verb move to the end of the clause when you use weil or obwohl?
cards.answer: Because weil and obwohl are subordinating conjunctions, and both send the conjugated verb to the end of their clause.

cards.front: How does the word order work when you combine a comparative with weil, e.g. 'weil es süßer als Brot ist'?
cards.answer: The verb still moves to the end of the clause, even when there is a comparative plus als phrase before it.

cards.front: Name the three things monasteries provided for the poor, according to the lesson.
cards.answer: Food at the gate / Beds in the guesthouse / Prayers for the dead

cards.front: Name the four reasons the lesson gives for why some people supported the dissolution.
cards.answer: Gentry buying cheap monastic land / Protestants saw monasteries as superstitious and wasteful / Towns repurposed buildings as schools or civic halls / Lollard communities in Kent and Essex welcomed removal of idolatry
items: Protestants saw monasteries as superstitious and wasteful
Towns repurposed buildings as schools or civic halls
Lollard communities in Kent and Essex welcomed removal of idolatry

cards.front: Why did the Pilgrimage of Grace fail despite having 30,000-40,000 supporters?
cards.answer: It lacked a noble military commander willing to take the field, as the northern earls were reluctant to commit to treason.

cards.front: Why could Mary I not restore the monasteries during her Catholic restoration of 1554-1555?
cards.answer: The monastic land had already been sold to new owners, who refused to give it back.

title: Measuring Development: GNI, HDI & the DTM
subject: geography-aqa

cards.front: Name the five social indicators of development given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Infant mortality / Life expectancy / Literacy rates / Doctors per 1,000 people / Access to safe water

cards.front: Name the five stages of the Demographic Transition Model in order.
cards.answer: High fluctuating / Early expanding / Late expanding / Low fluctuating / Decline

cards.front: Why is HDI more useful than GNI per head alone for measuring development?
cards.answer: HDI shows whether a country's wealth is actually being turned into better health and education, not just income.

cards.front: Why does Stage 5 of the DTM create a problem for a country?
cards.answer: Birth rate falls below death rate, so the population shrinks and ages, leaving fewer workers to support many pensioners.

title: Revelation, Visions and Miracles in Islam
subject: religious-studies-edexcel

cards.front: What three grounds do Atheists and Humanists give for challenging Islamic claims about the Qur'an and visions?
cards.answer: Beauty or complexity isn't evidence of divine authorship / All religions claim unique authority, so claims cancel out / Visions may have natural psychological explanations
items: Beauty or complexity isn't evidence of divine authorship
All religions claim unique authority, so claims cancel out
Visions may have natural psychological explanations

cards.front: What three responses do Muslims give to atheist and humanist challenges about the Qur'an?
cards.answer: The inimitability challenge has stood 1,400 years unanswered / Its consistency and preservation are themselves remarkable / The transformation it produces in believers is evidence of a real source
items: The inimitability challenge has stood 1,400 years unanswered
Its consistency and preservation are themselves remarkable
The transformation it produces in believers is evidence of a real source

cards.front: Why is the Islamic understanding of the Qur'an fundamentally different from most Christian understandings of the Bible?
cards.answer: Muslims believe the Qur'an is the direct speech of Allah himself, not a book written about God by humans.

cards.front: Why don't Muslims automatically accept every claimed vision or true dream as genuine divine communication?
cards.answer: Scholarly tradition requires such experiences to be consistent with the Qur'an and Sunnah before they are accepted as real.

cards.front: Name the nine criteria Aitchison uses to judge whether a communication system is a language.
cards.answer: Semanticity / Displacement / Arbitrariness / Productivity / Cultural transmission / Spontaneous usage / Turn-taking / Duality / Structure dependence

cards.front: Name the three animal communication examples the lesson uses to show shared function with human language.
cards.answer: Vervet monkeys' alarm calls for different predators / Bees' dance movements showing food source location / Bird song to attract mates or defend territory
items: Vervet monkeys' alarm calls for different predators
Bees' dance movements showing food source location
Bird song to attract mates or defend territory

cards.front: Why do most animal communication systems lack duality and structure dependence?
cards.answer: Animal signals function as a single whole rather than being built from smaller meaningless units combined by grammar rules.

cards.front: Why is cultural transmission limited in most animal communication systems?
cards.answer: Animal calls are largely instinctive and consistent across the species rather than learned from a particular community.

title: The English Revolution: Civil War, Regicide and Republic, 1642-1660
subject: history-aqa

cards.front: Name the four interlocking causes of the English Revolution given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Ideas: Divine Right vs Parliament's consent / Religion: Laudian reforms vs Puritan reformers / Money: ship money and the Personal Rule / Political crisis: Grand Remonstrance and failed arrest of Five Members
items: Ideas: Divine Right vs Parliament's consent
Religion: Laudian reforms vs Puritan reformers
Money: ship money and the Personal Rule
Political crisis: Grand Remonstrance and failed arrest of Five Members

cards.front: Name the four demands set out in the Levellers' 1647 Agreement of the People.
cards.answer: Manhood suffrage (excluding servants and beggars) / Regular elections / Religious liberty / Equality before the law

cards.front: Why did the New Model Army become a political force after the First Civil War ended in 1646?
cards.answer: Soldiers were owed back pay and many were Puritans with strong religious convictions, leading to radical movements like the Levellers.

cards.front: Why did the army decide Charles I could not be trusted alive in 1648?
cards.answer: Charles started a Second Civil War from his prison at Carisbrooke by plotting with the Scots, angering the army.

cards.front: What four steps does the lesson recommend when reading a graph or chart in a business question?
cards.answer: Read the title and axis labels / Check the units on each axis / Identify the trend before stating values / Note any anomalies and their possible cause
items: Read the title and axis labels
Check the units on each axis
Identify the trend before stating values
Note any anomalies and their possible cause

cards.front: Name the four main categories of data a business uses to understand performance, according to the lesson.
cards.answer: Financial data / Marketing data / Market data / Data from graphs and charts

cards.front: Why can having access to more data actually lead to worse or slower business decisions?
cards.answer: Too much data without the ability to filter and interpret it causes 'analysis paralysis', delaying decisions while more information is gathered.

cards.front: How can national market data mislead a business about its own position?
cards.answer: National market size figures may not accurately represent the specific niche or region the business actually operates in.

cards.front: What are the three types of plate boundary described in the lesson?
cards.answer: Convergent boundary / Divergent boundary / Conservative boundary

cards.front: Name the five volcanic hazards the lesson lists.
cards.answer: Lava flows / Ash falls / Pyroclastic flows / Lahars / Toxic gases

cards.front: Why are shallow earthquakes usually more damaging than deep ones?
cards.answer: Because they occur under 70 km deep, so their energy reaches the surface concentrated rather than spread out.

cards.front: Why is basaltic volcanic activity rarely deadly compared to andesitic eruptions?
cards.answer: Basaltic magma is fluid and produces gentle lava flows, while andesitic magma is sticky, trapping gas that builds up into explosive eruptions.

title: The Grand Alliance & the Origins of the Cold War
subject: history-edexcel

cards.front: What four things did the 'Big Three' agree at the Yalta Conference in February 1945?
cards.answer: Divide Germany into four zones of occupation / Hold free elections in liberated countries / Set up the United Nations / Allow the USSR to enter the war against Japan
items: Divide Germany into four zones of occupation
Hold free elections in liberated countries
Allow the USSR to enter the war against Japan

cards.front: According to the lesson, in what three ways did the atomic bomb transform superpower relations?
cards.answer: Gave the USA a nuclear monopoly / Truman used it for atomic diplomacy / Stalin accelerated the Soviet nuclear programme
items: Gave the USA a nuclear monopoly
Truman used it for atomic diplomacy
Stalin accelerated the Soviet nuclear programme

cards.front: Why did the Grand Alliance break down once Nazi Germany was defeated?
cards.answer: The shared enemy holding the alliance together disappeared, letting the deep ideological differences between capitalism and communism resurface and drive the powers apart.

cards.front: Why did Stalin want a buffer zone of friendly states in Eastern Europe?
cards.answer: Because the USSR had suffered around 27 million deaths in the war and Stalin wanted to prevent any future invasion.

cards.front: Name the four individual responses the lesson gives for reducing a consumer's ecological footprint.
cards.answer: Choosing seasonal local food / Eating less meat / Repairing rather than replacing electronics / Reducing fast-fashion buys

cards.front: Name the four government responses the lesson gives for tackling consumer environmental impact.
