cards.front: Why do longitudinal waves have areas of compression and rarefaction?
cards.answer: Because the oscillations are parallel to the direction of energy transfer, squashing particles together or spreading them apart.

cards.front: Name the four 'special areas' designated by the Special Areas Act of 1934 for government investment.
cards.answer: South Wales / North-east England / West Cumberland / Central Scotland

cards.front: What four reasons does the lesson give for new consumer industries preferring the Midlands and south-east over the north?
cards.answer: Closer to the largest consumer markets / Land was cheaper / Better road and rail links to the south / No entrenched union culture from staple industries
items: Closer to the largest consumer markets
Better road and rail links to the south
No entrenched union culture from staple industries

cards.front: Why was the National Insurance scheme unable to cope with unemployment in the 1930s?
cards.answer: It had been designed before the First World War, not for long-term mass unemployment, so by 1931 the fund was bankrupt.

cards.front: Why did the Jarrow Crusade organisers deliberately keep the march disciplined and non-violent?
cards.answer: To distance themselves from the communist-led Hunger Marches of the same period and win public sympathy.

title: Act 1: The Engagement and the Inspector Arrives
subject: english-literature-aqa

cards.front: How does Mr Birling react when the Inspector reveals he sacked Eva Smith?
cards.answer: He shows no remorse, calling it a 'perfectly straightforward case' and insisting he 'can't accept any responsibility.'

cards.front: Why does Priestley time the Inspector's arrival to interrupt Birling's speech to Gerald and Eric?
cards.answer: It cuts off Birling's capitalist philosophy mid-sentence, positioning the Inspector as its direct answer.

title: Act 3: Eric’s Confession and the Inspector’s Speech
subject: english-literature-aqa

cards.front: Name the three techniques the lesson identifies in the Inspector's final speech.
cards.answer: Repetition / Tricolon / Direct address

cards.front: Why is Eric's treatment of Eva considered the most serious wrongdoing in the play?
cards.answer: He used her sexually, got her pregnant, and tried to buy her off with stolen money.

cards.front: Why does Priestley use Eric's drinking problem as a device in the play?
cards.answer: To show that the Birling family's obsession with appearances blinded them to real problems in their own household.

title: Tropical Storm Effects & Management: Hurricane Ida
subject: geography-aqa

cards.front: Name the four tools the lesson gives for reducing tropical storm risk.
cards.answer: Monitoring / Prediction / Protection / Planning

cards.front: Why did Hurricane Ida intensify so rapidly from Category 1 to Category 4?
cards.answer: It passed over Caribbean waters around 30°C, well above the 26.5°C threshold needed for hurricanes to strengthen.

cards.front: Why can a slow-moving Category 1 hurricane still be as deadly as a Category 4?
cards.answer: The Saffir-Simpson scale only predicts wind damage, not storm surge or rainfall flooding, which is often the biggest killer.

cards.front: What three tests had Rochester posed before, all now answered by the time Jane returns to him?
cards.answer: Money / Mistress / Manipulation

cards.front: Why does Jane refuse to marry St John even though she considers his offer seriously?
cards.answer: Marrying without love would mean losing her private inner self, described as a kind of enslavement or bondage.

cards.front: Why does Brontë use Morton to show Jane's growing independence?
cards.answer: It proves Jane is now fully self-supporting, living out materially the independence her refusal at Thornfield began.

cards.front: Name the five key themes this lesson covers in A Christmas Carol.
cards.answer: Redemption / Social responsibility / Poverty / Christmas / Isolation

cards.front: What are the three stages of Scrooge's redemption journey?
cards.answer: Confronting the past (regret) / Witnessing the present (empathy) / Facing the future (terror)

cards.front: Why did Dickens choose the novella form for A Christmas Carol rather than a novel or short story?
cards.answer: A full novel would have diluted the emotional intensity while a short story lacked space for Scrooge's gradual transformation, so the novella's compactness creates urgency.

cards.front: How does the simile 'solitary as an oyster' show Scrooge's isolation in Stave 1?
cards.answer: It compares Scrooge to a creature sealed inside a hard shell, suggesting he has deliberately shut himself off from the world.

cards.front: Name the four factors of production an entrepreneur combines.
cards.answer: Land / Labour / Capital / Enterprise

cards.front: What four things do customers want that a business must understand to meet their needs?
cards.answer: Price / Quality / Choice / Convenience

cards.front: Why must an entrepreneur's three core functions all happen at the same time?
cards.answer: Missing any one causes failure: poor decisions ruin good organising and risk-taking, and refusing risk means nothing new is built.

cards.front: How does quality add value to a product?
cards.answer: A product that lasts longer, performs better or feels more premium justifies charging a higher price than a mass-produced alternative.

title: Medieval Warfare: Cavalry, Castles and Crossbows
subject: history-aqa

cards.front: Name the four main groups that made up Edward I's armies.
cards.answer: Heavy cavalry of knights and men-at-arms / Mass infantry of foot-soldiers / Longbow archers / Crossbowmen
items: Heavy cavalry of knights and men-at-arms

cards.front: Name the three ways a medieval siege could end.
cards.answer: Defenders ran out of food / Defenders surrendered to spare their lives / A breach was forced
items: Defenders surrendered to spare their lives

cards.front: Why did Edward send his archers forward before the cavalry charged at Falkirk in 1298?
cards.answer: The Scottish schiltrons resisted cavalry, so volleys of arrows were used to break up the static formations before the cavalry charged home.

cards.front: Why did Edward build ring after ring of stone castles in Wales instead of fighting repeated field campaigns?
cards.answer: Long sieges cost heavily in money, men and time, so castles aimed to make Welsh resistance impossible without repeated battles.

cards.front: Name the five other anthology poems the lesson says 'Prayer' connects well to for comparison.
cards.answer: Baby Song / Holy Thursday / Cold Knap Lake / Equilibrium / Tea With Our Grandmothers

cards.front: What features of form and structure does the lesson say 'Prayer' uses to mimic struggling speech?
cards.answer: short lines / short sentences / frequent caesura / shifts in tense

cards.front: Why does Kunial use short lines and frequent caesura in 'Prayer'?
cards.answer: They mimic a person struggling to get words out under pressure, forcing the reader to pause where the speaker pauses for breath.

cards.front: Why does Kunial place the Arabic phrase 'Allah hu Akbar' inside an English poem?
cards.answer: It places his father's Muslim inheritance directly inside the English poem, holding two languages of faith together like his own dual identity.

title: Inequality in Contemporary UK: Class, Gender, Ethnicity
subject: sociology-eduqas

cards.front: The lesson identifies seven domains where inequality is documented in the contemporary UK. Name them.
cards.answer: Income and wealth / Education / Crime / Health / Family / Work / Media representation

cards.front: Which three earlier laws did the Equality Act 2010 consolidate into a single framework?
cards.answer: Equal Pay Act / Sex Discrimination Act / Race Relations Act

cards.front: Why do sociologists say official crime statistics can exaggerate offending by certain ethnic minority groups?
cards.answer: Because the statistics reflect policing and prosecution patterns as much as actual offending, amplified by media labelling and moral panics.

cards.front: Why does the gender pay gap persist in the UK workplace despite formal equality laws?
cards.answer: Women are over-represented in part-time, lower-paid feminised jobs and face the glass ceiling restricting access to senior roles.

cards.front: Name the five comparative structures the lesson gives for comparing types of transport in Spanish.
cards.answer: más … que / menos … que / tan … como / mejor … que / peor … que

cards.front: Name the three connectives the lesson gives for justifying transport choices.
cards.answer: porque es / dado que es / ya que es
items: dado que es (given that it is)

cards.front: How does the lesson say you form 'by [vehicle]' phrases in Spanish, and what are the two exceptions?
cards.answer: You use 'en' plus the vehicle (e.g. en coche, en tren), except a pie (on foot) and a caballo (on horseback), which use 'a'.

cards.front: According to the lesson's example sentences, why might someone prefer to travel by bike?
cards.answer: Because going by bike is better for the environment and better for your health, as shown using 'mejor'.

cards.front: What three phases did Kohl's Ten-Point Plan envisage for reunification?
cards.answer: Expanded cooperation between the two Germanies / A confederal arrangement / Eventually full unification
items: Expanded cooperation between the two Germanies

cards.front: What four things did the Two Plus Four Treaty settle about reunified Germany?
cards.answer: Germany's existing borders were confirmed / Occupation rights of the four powers ended / Germany agreed not to develop weapons of mass destruction / NATO's jurisdiction would not extend to former GDR territory
items: Occupation rights of the four powers ended
Germany agreed not to develop weapons of mass destruction
NATO's jurisdiction would not extend to former GDR territory

cards.front: How did losing Soviet military backing make the SED regime vulnerable in 1989?
cards.answer: Without Soviet tanks as a guarantor, the SED could no longer rely on force to crush popular opposition as it had in 1953.

cards.front: Why did the SED become increasingly isolated in the late 1980s?
cards.answer: Honecker rejected Gorbachev's reforms and blocked reform-minded material, leaving the SED committed to a hard-line course even the USSR was abandoning.

cards.front: Name the three desperate tactics Leah uses to try to get Phil's attention in the field.
cards.answer: Mentions killing her pet / Threatens to harm herself / Talks about death

cards.front: Name the three minor group members who show discomfort but still comply with Phil's instructions.
cards.answer: Danny / Brian / Lou

cards.front: Why is John Tate instantly sidelined once Phil offers a plan?
cards.answer: He offers no resistance because, deep down, he knows he has nothing useful to contribute.

cards.front: Why does Cathy's behaviour support Kelly's idea that group pressure liberates rather than creates cruelty?
cards.answer: Cathy does not become cruel because of the group; it gives her permission to express cruelty she already possessed.

cards.front: According to Jacobean belief, name the three powers witches were thought to have.
cards.answer: Predict the future / Control the weather / Cause disease

cards.front: Name the three unnatural events that occur in nature after Duncan's murder.
cards.answer: Horses eat each other / The sky darkens / An owl kills a falcon

cards.front: Why does nature descend into chaos after Duncan's murder?
cards.answer: The murder ruptures the divinely ordained order of the Great Chain of Being, so the natural world reacts with unnatural chaos.

cards.front: Why is it ambiguous whether the witches cause Macbeth's downfall or simply reveal ambitions he already has?
cards.answer: The witches prophesy he will become king but never tell him to murder anyone; Macbeth and Lady Macbeth choose to act on the prophecies themselves.

title: Case Study: York under the Vikings
subject: history-edexcel

cards.front: Name the five craft goods produced in the Coppergate workshops that archaeologists have found.
cards.answer: Amber jewellery / Glass beads / Leather shoes / Ironwork / Bone combs

cards.front: Name the four goods York's Viking-age merchants exported in return for imported luxuries.
cards.answer: Wool / Cloth / Leather / Fine craftwork

cards.front: Why did Jorvik become such a strong magnet for migrants in the Viking period?
cards.answer: Because work and wealth were readily available there, pulling in a growing population through economic opportunity.

cards.front: How did the Church in York respond to Viking settlement rather than being destroyed by it?
cards.answer: Religious institutions adapted, blending Norse and Christian styles, and became a route by which Norse migrants were absorbed into English society.

cards.front: What three stages mark Jordan's drift into gang life, according to the lesson?
cards.answer: Expelled from school / Steals for the Crew for cigarettes and protection / Carries a knife
items: Steals for the Crew for cigarettes and protection

cards.front: What three things does the lesson say boys like Jordan lack, making the gang their only option?
cards.answer: No jobs / No prospects / No safe spaces

cards.front: How does the Dell Farm Crew fill a void in the estate, according to Kelman?
cards.answer: It provides structure, identity, and belonging where schools, police, and social services fail.

cards.front: Why does Lydia's own situation leave her unable to protect Harri?
cards.answer: She is fighting her own battles against peer pressure, estate life, and expectations on immigrant women, leaving her unavailable.

title: The impact of the Spanish conquest
subject: history-eduqas

cards.front: Name the three types of Spanish missionary friars who established missions across Mexico.
cards.answer: Franciscan / Dominican / Augustinian

cards.front: What six things does the lesson say passed from Europe to the Americas in the Columbian Exchange?
cards.answer: Wheat / Cattle / Horses / Sugar cane / Diseases / Enslaved Africans

cards.front: Why was working in the silver mines of Potosí especially deadly for indigenous labourers?
cards.answer: Men worked in near-darkness inhaling toxic mercury vapour, with minimal food and no safety equipment, drastically shortening life expectancy.

cards.front: Why did Spain's silver wealth paradoxically weaken its own economy?
cards.answer: Easy silver money reduced incentives for domestic industry, so Spain used it to pay for imports instead of building its own manufacturing base.

cards.front: Name the five aims of criminal sentencing given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Retribution / Deterrence / Public protection / Rehabilitation / Reparation

cards.front: Name the five types of civil disputes the lesson gives as examples.
cards.answer: Breach of contract / Negligence / Defamation / Employment disputes / Family law matters

cards.front: Why is the standard of proof set so high (beyond reasonable doubt) in criminal cases?
cards.answer: Because criminal punishment is severe, this high standard protects defendants from being wrongly convicted.

cards.front: Why can the same harmful act sometimes lead to both a criminal prosecution and a civil claim?
cards.answer: Because criminal and civil law are separate systems, an act like an unsafe building can breach safety law and cause harm, triggering both as separate processes.

title: Theatre, stage and screen: medieval to Victorian
subject: history-eduqas

cards.front: Name the three things Charles II brought back to English theatre after the Restoration.
cards.answer: Painted scenery / Indoor candlelit theatres / Professional women actors

cards.front: Name the five types of performers the lesson says appeared in rotation at Victorian music halls.
cards.answer: Comic singers / Acrobats / Jugglers / Magicians / Sentimental balladeers

cards.front: Why did Elizabethan theatre rely on spoken language, costume and convention rather than scenery?
cards.answer: Because the open-air stage had no ability to change lighting, so scenery could not be used effectively.

cards.front: Why were early commercial theatres built in the suburbs of London rather than inside the city?
cards.answer: Because they were outside the jurisdiction of city authorities, who disapproved of theatre as immoral and disruptive.

cards.front: Name the four types of proteins the lesson gives as examples.
cards.answer: Enzymes / Structural proteins (collagen and keratin) / Hormones (insulin) / Antibodies

cards.front: Name the four factors affecting enzyme activity described in the lesson.
cards.answer: Temperature / pH / Substrate concentration / Enzyme concentration

cards.front: Why does increasing substrate concentration eventually stop increasing the rate of an enzyme reaction?
cards.answer: All the active sites become occupied at once (the enzyme is saturated), so adding more substrate has no further effect.

cards.front: Why does raising the temperature increase the rate of an enzyme-controlled reaction up to the optimum?
cards.answer: Molecules move faster and collide more frequently with the enzyme, increasing the rate of reaction.

title: The Structure and Process of Memory
subject: psychology-edexcel

cards.front: Name the three processes that turn raw input into a usable memory.
cards.answer: Encoding / Storage / Retrieval

cards.front: What four things might someone with retrograde amnesia fail to recall from before their injury?
cards.answer: Family members they knew / Events they experienced / Skills they had learned / Facts they had learned

cards.front: Why can a fact feel like it's 'on the tip of your tongue'?
cards.answer: It has been encoded and stored successfully, but retrieval temporarily fails to bring it back out.

cards.front: How can someone with severe anterograde amnesia still hold a normal conversation?
cards.answer: Information can pass briefly through short-term memory, but fails to transfer into long-term storage.

cards.front: Name the four purposes of marriage given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Lifelong companionship / A stable environment for children / Sexual intimacy within a committed relationship / Following God's plan (for religious believers)
items: Sexual intimacy within a committed relationship

cards.front: Name the five common reasons for divorce in Britain given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Adultery / Unreasonable behaviour / Growing apart / Financial problems / Domestic abuse

cards.front: Why is there an ethical tension around divorce according to the lesson?
cards.answer: Because marriage is seen as sacred and permanent, yet compassion says it is cruel to force people to stay in harmful or loveless marriages.

cards.front: Why does the Church of England permit divorce while the Catholic Church does not?
cards.answer: Catholics see marriage as an unbreakable sacrament, while the Church of England allows divorce as a last resort out of compassion.

cards.front: Name the three roots of Enid's controlling behaviour, as the lesson identifies them.
cards.answer: Her abusive marriage — won't let daughters experience the same / Her mother's death and their estrangement — can't bear losing daughters that way / Her experience of racism as a Windrush immigrant — believes assimilation is protection
items: Her abusive marriage — won't let daughters experience the same
Her mother's death and their estrangement — can't bear losing daughters that way
Her experience of racism as a Windrush immigrant — believes assimilation is protection

cards.front: Why did Enid's husband become abusive towards her?
cards.answer: His cruelty was rooted in the racism and humiliation he suffered at work, which he inflicted on Enid.

cards.front: Why does Viv walk out of one of her exams?
cards.answer: It is an act of defiance against a Eurocentric curriculum that she feels has no place for her.

title: Piaget in Education: Conservation and Egocentrism
subject: psychology-aqa

cards.front: Name the three features of primary classrooms that reflect Piaget's insight about concrete operational learning.
cards.answer: Hands-on materials / Practical activities / Discovery learning

cards.front: Why do pre-operational children fail standard conservation tasks like the tall thin glass vs short wide glass?
cards.answer: They focus on the height of the water, what they can see, rather than reasoning about the actual quantity.

cards.front: How did children's responses in Piaget's Three Mountains Task demonstrate egocentrism?
cards.answer: Pre-operational children consistently described what they themselves could see, not what the doll's position would show.

title: Legacy of the Black Death: labour, wages and the Statute of Labourers
subject: history-eduqas

cards.front: What were the three aims of the Statute of Labourers (1351)?
cards.answer: Fix wages at pre-Black Death levels / Forbid labourers leaving for higher pay elsewhere / Fine employers who paid above the legal rate
items: Fix wages at pre-Black Death levels
Forbid labourers leaving for higher pay elsewhere
Fine employers who paid above the legal rate

cards.front: Name the three long-term effects of the sustained population decrease after the Black Death, according to the lesson.
cards.answer: Marginal land converted to sheep pasture / The wool trade benefited / Gradual emergence of a mobile wage-labour economy
items: Marginal land converted to sheep pasture
Gradual emergence of a mobile wage-labour economy

cards.front: Why did some marginal farmland get converted to sheep pasture after the Black Death?
cards.answer: There were fewer workers available, and sheep pasture required much less labour than farming the land.

cards.front: How did some physicians' observations after the Black Death hint at contagion theory, even though miasma theory still dominated?
cards.answer: They noticed people who had close contact with the sick were more likely to fall ill themselves.

title: Act 2: Geof, Helen's Return & the Ending
subject: english-literature-eduqas

cards.front: Name the six practical things Geof does to care for Jo during her pregnancy.
cards.answer: Cooks / Cleans / Buys baby clothes / Prepares for the birth / Asks practical questions about the baby / Encourages her to see a doctor
items: Asks practical questions about the baby
Encourages her to see a doctor

cards.front: What three things happen in the play's final unresolved scene?
cards.answer: Helen discovers the baby's father was Black and reacts with racist horror / Helen goes out for a drink / Jo is left alone on stage as the birth approaches
items: Helen discovers the baby's father was Black and reacts with racist horror
Helen goes out for a drink
Jo is left alone on stage as the birth approaches

cards.front: Why was Geof thrown out of his lodgings before moving in with Jo?
cards.answer: Likely because his landlady discovered his sexuality.

cards.front: How does the relationship between Jo and Geof challenge conventional ideas of family?
cards.answer: Helen, Jo's biological mother, fails at maternal duty, while Geof, with no blood tie, provides real care, showing family is defined by actions not blood.

cards.front: Name the four job roles the lesson says an organisational structure sets out, from top to bottom.
cards.answer: Directors set strategy / Managers plan / Supervisors organise / Operatives carry out the work

cards.front: Name the three types of communication the lesson describes within an organisation.
cards.answer: Vertical (up or down the chain) / Horizontal (between colleagues at the same level) / Diagonal (across departments)
items: Horizontal (between colleagues at the same level)

cards.front: Why do flat structures give a business lower management costs?
cards.answer: Because there are fewer layers of management, meaning fewer managers need to be employed and paid.

cards.front: Why does a wide span of control usually push a business towards horizontal communication?
cards.answer: Because a manager cannot brief every worker in person, so staff communicate directly with colleagues at the same level.

cards.front: Name the five thermosetting polymers given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Epoxy resin / Polyester resin / Melamine / Polyurethane / Vulcanised rubber

cards.front: Name the four factors that the lesson says determine the properties of a composite.
cards.answer: Type of reinforcement / Direction of the fibres / Volume fraction of fibres / Type of matrix

cards.front: How does cross-graining in plywood overcome timber's natural weakness across the grain?
cards.answer: Alternating the grain direction of each glued veneer layer makes the panel strong and stiff in both directions and resistant to splitting.

cards.front: How does prestressing improve concrete's resistance to tensile loads?
cards.answer: Tensioned steel tendons put the concrete into permanent pre-compression, allowing it to resist higher tensile loads before cracking.

cards.front: Name the five towns where anti-Jewish riots broke out in 1190.
cards.answer: King's Lynn / Norwich / Stamford / Lincoln / Bury St Edmunds

cards.front: What three types of institutions did medieval Jewish communities in England maintain?
cards.answer: Synagogues / Schools / Charitable networks

cards.front: Why were Jewish financiers essential to the Crown, Church and nobility in medieval England?
cards.answer: Canon law forbade Christians from lending money at interest, so Jews filled this role and became indispensable to royal and noble finance.

cards.front: How did the 1218 requirement for Jews to wear a badge increase their vulnerability?
cards.answer: It visually marked Jews as different, an early form of state-enforced exclusion that made physical attacks against them easier.

cards.front: Name the four groups of people the lesson describes as economically inactive.
cards.answer: Retired people / Full-time students / People caring for family members / People who have stopped looking for work
items: People who have stopped looking for work

cards.front: Name the three criteria the Labour Force Survey uses to count someone as unemployed.
cards.answer: Without a job / Available to start within two weeks / Actively seeking work in the past four weeks
items: Available to start within two weeks
Actively seeking work in the past four weeks

cards.front: How does rising unemployment cause lost output for the economy as a whole?
cards.answer: Idle workers mean the goods and services they could have produced are not made, so output falls below productive potential.

cards.front: Why does a long spell of unemployment make it harder for an individual to find a new job?
cards.answer: Their skills become outdated and gaps appear in their CV, which employers notice.

cards.front: Name the five uses of glucose produced by photosynthesis in a plant.
cards.answer: Respiration to release energy / Converted to starch for storage / Converted to cellulose for cell walls / Combined with nitrates to make amino acids/proteins / Converted to lipids for storage in seeds
items: Converted to cellulose for cell walls
Combined with nitrates to make amino acids/proteins
Converted to lipids for storage in seeds

cards.front: What are the four steps of the iodine test for starch in a leaf?
cards.answer: Boil the leaf in water / Boil the leaf in ethanol to remove chlorophyll / Rinse the leaf in water / Add iodine solution
items: Boil the leaf in ethanol to remove chlorophyll

cards.front: Why does the rate of photosynthesis increase as light intensity increases (before it plateaus)?
cards.answer: More light energy is available for the light-dependent stage, so more water can be split and more glucose produced.

cards.front: Why does the rate of photosynthesis drop below the optimum temperature?
cards.answer: Molecules have less kinetic energy so they collide less frequently with enzyme active sites, slowing the reaction.

cards.front: Name the three ways the lesson says Othello's suicide can be read.
cards.answer: Justice / Repentance / Hubris

cards.front: Name the three interpretations the lesson gives for Desdemona's 'Nobody; I myself' line.
cards.answer: Proof of saintly forgiveness / Ultimate expression of victim's conditioning under patriarchy / Both simultaneously
items: Ultimate expression of victim's conditioning under patriarchy

cards.front: Why does the lesson say Emilia's murder by Iago mirrors Othello's murder of Desdemona?
cards.answer: Both men kill women who threaten their control, showing a repeated pattern of male violence in the play.

cards.front: Why does the lesson describe the play's ending as 'hollow' despite Iago facing punishment?
cards.answer: Desdemona and Emilia are dead, Othello has destroyed himself, and Iago's silence leaves his true motivation unknown.

title: Uses and Dangers of Radiation, Fission and Fusion
subject: separate-sciences-edexcel

cards.front: Name the six precautions given for reducing radiation dose when handling sources.
cards.answer: Lead-lined containers / Tongs or remote handling / Minimising time near source / Maximising distance from source / Dosimetry badges / Minimum dose necessary for patients

cards.front: What are the three main engineering challenges to achieving fusion power?
cards.answer: Reaching and sustaining required temperature / Confining the plasma without touching walls / Achieving net energy gain
items: Confining the plasma without touching walls

cards.front: Why is beta radiation used for thickness gauging rather than alpha or gamma?
cards.answer: Alpha would be completely blocked by the material, while gamma would pass through unaffected by small thickness changes; beta partially penetrates, making it sensitive to thickness.

cards.front: Why is alpha contamination especially dangerous even though alpha can't penetrate skin from outside?
cards.answer: If inhaled or ingested, alpha particles are absorbed by internal organs at very short range, causing intense damage close to living cells.

cards.front: Name the three acts that show Ralph is capable of guilt and violence despite being the novel's hero.
cards.answer: Betrays Piggy's nickname / Participates in the mock hunt / Present at Simon's murder

cards.front: Name the three stages of Roger's arc across the novel's chapters.
cards.answer: Chapter 4: throws stones but deliberately misses / Chapter 11: murders Piggy with calculated precision / Chapter 12: sharpens a stick for Ralph's head
items: Chapter 4: throws stones but deliberately misses
Chapter 11: murders Piggy with calculated precision
Chapter 12: sharpens a stick for Ralph's head

cards.front: Why does Golding show Ralph committing acts of complicity and violence?
cards.answer: To prove that the darkness of man's heart exists even in the most civilised, most sympathetic character.

cards.front: Why is Roger presented as more dangerous than Jack?
cards.answer: Jack wants power and adulation, whereas Roger simply enjoys causing pain for its own sake.

cards.front: Name the three weaknesses of top-down strategies that the lesson gives for Mumbai.
cards.answer: Communities evicted with little notice or fair compensation / Slum-rehabilitation towers break up tight-knit migrant communities / Mega-projects overrun on cost and time (e.g. bullet train)
items: Communities evicted with little notice or fair compensation
Slum-rehabilitation towers break up tight-knit migrant communities
Mega-projects overrun on cost and time (e.g. bullet train)

cards.front: Name the three strengths of top-down strategies that the lesson gives for Mumbai.
cards.answer: Can shift millions of people quickly / Attract foreign investment and World Bank funding / National prestige projects give visible, politically useful results
items: Can shift millions of people quickly
Attract foreign investment and World Bank funding
National prestige projects give visible, politically useful results

cards.front: Why did Mumbai's first elevated coastal road cut journey times so much?
cards.answer: It bypassed the choked road system, turning a one-hour drive into 20 minutes and easing pressure off roads and rail.

cards.front: How does the Slum Rehabilitation Scheme get funded without costing the city money?
cards.answer: Private developers build rehousing blocks for slum dwellers in return for rights to build profitable luxury towers on the cleared land.

cards.front: Name the three main types of board used in GCSE D&T.
cards.answer: Corrugated board / Folding boxboard (FBB) / Mounting board

cards.front: Besides laminating, name the three other finishing techniques mentioned for papers and boards.
cards.answer: Spot UV varnish / Embossing / Foil blocking

cards.front: Why does mechanical pulp paper yellow over time?
cards.answer: Because lignin remains in the fibres, unlike chemically produced pulp which has lignin removed.

cards.front: Why does recycled paper lose strength over successive recycling cycles?
cards.answer: Because each recycling cycle shortens the paper fibres slightly, weakening the sheet.

cards.front: Name the three main schemes the lesson gives for reducing unemployment under the Nazis.
cards.answer: RAD labour service / Autobahn road-building programme / Rapid rearmament from 1935

cards.front: Name the four school subjects/areas the lesson says were changed under Nazi education.
cards.answer: History / Biology / Physical education / Girls' education

cards.front: Why was the official unemployment figure of under one million by 1938 misleading?
cards.answer: Because women and Jewish workers were excluded from the count, so the true unemployment figure was higher.

cards.front: Why did Nazi policy towards women become contradictory by the late 1930s?
cards.answer: Rearmament expanded and the economy increasingly needed female labour, so women were quietly encouraged back into work despite the official domestic ideal.

cards.front: Why does Ralph feel a moment of existential dread when looking at the ocean in Chapter 7?
cards.answer: He realises the sea is 'the divider, the barrier', making him grasp for the first time that rescue may never come.

cards.front: How does the storm act symbolically after Simon's murder?
cards.answer: It breaks the parachutist's body free and blows it out to sea, symbolically removing the 'beast', though the evil is already done.

cards.front: Name the three things the Good Friday Agreement (1998) established.
cards.answer: A power-sharing executive of unionist and nationalist parties / A North-South Ministerial Council / Commitments to human rights and decommissioning of weapons
items: A power-sharing executive of unionist and nationalist parties
Commitments to human rights and decommissioning of weapons

cards.front: Name the four areas of power given to the Scottish Parliament when it opened in 1999.
cards.answer: Health / Education / Justice / Local government

cards.front: Why was the 1979 Scottish devolution referendum result invalidated even though more people voted Yes than No?
cards.answer: A rule required 40% of the total electorate to vote Yes, and this threshold was not reached.

cards.front: Why did the 2010 general election lead to a coalition government?
cards.answer: No party won an overall majority, producing a hung Parliament, so the Conservatives and Liberal Democrats negotiated a coalition agreement.

cards.front: Name the three anthology poems the lesson pairs with 'Sonnet 29' for comparison.
cards.answer: 'Dusting the Phone' by Jackie Kay / 'Origin Story' by Eve L. Ewing / 'Catrin' by Gillian Clarke

cards.front: What three things should you focus on if 'Sonnet 29' is your specified poem?
cards.answer: the vine-and-tree conceit / the early volta / the closing paradox

cards.front: Why does the early volta in 'Sonnet 29' matter for understanding the speaker?
cards.answer: It shows the speaker correcting herself almost as soon as she notices the problem, not waiting for the form to catch up with her feelings.

cards.front: Why does the speaker stop thinking of her lover once he is truly present in 'Sonnet 29'?
cards.answer: Thinking usually arises from absence, but here presence itself satisfies what imagination could only approximate, so thought stops.

cards.front: Name the three naturalist strategies the lesson identifies as shaping Rocks's aesthetic.
cards.answer: Available light / Hand-held cinema verite camera / Ensemble group framing

cards.front: According to the lesson, what three things make Rocks atypical of the social-realist tradition?
cards.answer: Black British teenage girl as lead / Multicultural female friendship group as social world / Female-majority crew
items: Black British teenage girl as lead
Multicultural female friendship group as social world

cards.front: Why is holding the whole friendship group in one ensemble shot a departure from conventional drama technique?
cards.answer: Conventional drama cuts to individual close-ups at emotional peaks to guide identification with one character, but Rocks refuses to single anyone out.

cards.front: Why does the score's arrival in the closing reunion scene mark it as emotionally significant?
cards.answer: The score has been minimal throughout, so its gentle non-diegetic rise in this otherwise score-free sequence signals significance without overwriting the moment.

title: The Origin of the Universe and Stewardship
subject: religious-studies-eduqas

cards.front: Name the six things God creates in order in the Genesis 1 creation account.
cards.answer: Light / Sky / Land / Vegetation / Animals / Humanity

cards.front: What are the three stages of the universe's cycle in Hindu teaching?
cards.answer: Srishti (creation) / Sthiti (maintenance) / Pralaya (dissolution)

cards.front: Why do many religious thinkers argue that science and religion do not conflict over the universe's origin?
cards.answer: Because science answers the question 'how' the universe began while religion answers 'why', so both can be held together.

cards.front: Why does the Talmud's story of Honi teach Jewish environmental responsibility?
cards.answer: It shows a man planting a tree that takes seventy years to fruit, teaching that people should provide for future generations as others provided for them.

cards.front: The lesson names three ways Meena's identity crisis changed her behaviour after Sam's speech. What are they?
cards.answer: Becomes more reckless / More willing to follow Anita into danger / Less connected to her family
items: More willing to follow Anita into danger

cards.front: What three qualities did Meena once admire in Anita, according to the lesson?
cards.answer: Toughness / Defiance / Freedom

cards.front: Why do immigrant families become scapegoats for Tollington's economic decline?
cards.answer: They are visible and different, so blaming them is easier than confronting the real economic causes of decline.

cards.front: How does Sam Lowbridge work as both a character and a symbol in the novel?
cards.answer: As a character he is shaped by poverty and lack of education, while as a symbol he represents wider racist forces threatening Meena's belonging.

cards.front: Name the three reasons the lesson gives for why reported rates of mental health problems have increased over recent decades.
cards.answer: Increased challenges of modern living / Increased recognition of mental health problems / Lessening of social stigma
items: Increased recognition of mental health problems

cards.front: Name the three things the lesson says cultural variations affect regarding mental health.
cards.answer: Help-seeking behaviour / Willingness to disclose symptoms / Type of treatment preferred

cards.front: Why can significant mental health problems damage a person's relationships?
cards.answer: Withdrawal, irritability or changes in behaviour make it hard to maintain friendships, romantic partnerships or family bonds.

cards.front: Why might untreated mental health conditions be linked to increased crime rates?
cards.answer: Individuals experiencing a mental health crisis may act in ways they otherwise would not.

cards.front: Name the five key offerings the lesson gives for puja.
cards.answer: Water (purification) / Flowers (beauty) / Incense (sweet fragrance rising to God) / Food/prasad (shared as blessing) / Light (arati lamp)

cards.front: What are the three core religious duties in Hinduism named in the lesson, alongside yajna (sacrifice)?
cards.answer: Yajna (sacrifice) / Dana (giving) / Tapas (austerity)

cards.front: How does the fire in havan purify participants and the space around them?
cards.answer: The fire burns away impurity while the smoke is believed to carry prayers upward to the deities.

cards.front: Why does puja focus on worshipping a murti rather than meditating directly on formless Brahman?
cards.answer: The Bhagavad Gita says meditating on unmanifest Brahman is difficult, so a murti gives an accessible route for devotees who relate to God in personal form.

cards.front: Name the three things Dolly Winthrop teaches Silas as his guide to parenthood.
cards.answer: How to care for a child / How to discipline gently / How to participate in community traditions like christening
items: How to care for a child
How to participate in community traditions like christening

cards.front: Name the three ways Silas learns to engage with village life after raising Eppie.
cards.answer: Attending church / Visiting neighbours / Celebrating festivals

cards.front: Why does Eliot contrast Dolly Winthrop's faith with the Lantern Yard congregation's?
cards.answer: Dolly uses religion to welcome and support, while Lantern Yard used it to judge and exclude, showing genuine faith is kindness not doctrine.

cards.front: Why does Godfrey's secret about Eppie eat at him for sixteen years after marrying Nancy?
cards.answer: His marriage to Nancy is childless, and Godfrey knows this is punishment for hiding that Eppie is his daughter.

cards.front: Name the six life stages in Pearson's model of human lifespan development.
cards.answer: Infancy / Early childhood / Adolescence / Early adulthood / Middle adulthood / Later adulthood

cards.front: Name the seven categories of factors that can affect growth and development given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Physical factors / Lifestyle factors / Emotional factors / Social factors / Cultural factors / Environmental factors / Economic factors

cards.front: Why is Component 3 described as a synoptic exam?
cards.answer: Because it draws on knowledge from Components 1 and 2 as well as the Component 3 content itself.

cards.front: How does social development typically change as someone moves through the life stages?
cards.answer: It moves from dependence on family, towards wider relationships, and in later life sometimes back to a smaller social circle.

cards.front: Name the three categories that props divide into in film analysis.
cards.answer: Functional (serve a practical purpose) / Symbolic (carry meaning beyond their literal use) / Signature (linked to one character's identity)
items: Symbolic (carry meaning beyond their literal use)

cards.front: Name the five elements the lesson says mise-en-scene encompasses.
cards.answer: Setting (sets and locations) / Props / Costume and wardrobe / Make-up / Performance and blocking of actors

cards.front: Why does a protagonist's costume shifting from dull, neutral tones to richer, saturated colours communicate character change?
cards.answer: The spectator absorbs the shift as signalling growing confidence or power even without consciously noticing it.

cards.front: Why might a production designer deliberately break period accuracy, such as putting modern trainers on a historical figure?
cards.answer: To make a statement about the universality or relevance of the story's themes to a modern audience.

cards.front: Name the four jobs the lesson says promotion does.
cards.answer: Inform / Persuade / Remind / Build brand image

cards.front: Besides point of sale and advertising, name the four other promotional methods on the specification.
cards.answer: Price reductions / Loss leaders / Competitions / Free samples

cards.front: Why does point-of-sale promotion work well at boosting sales?
cards.answer: It reaches the customer at the exact moment they are deciding what to buy, lifting impulse purchases.

cards.front: Why is Greggs' distribution almost entirely physical rather than digital?
cards.answer: Because a sausage roll needs to be eaten hot, so it must be sold and eaten in person.

cards.front: Name the three things the Computer Misuse Act 1990 makes illegal.
cards.answer: Gaining unauthorised access to a computer system / Gaining access with intent to commit a further crime / Making unauthorised changes to data
items: Gaining unauthorised access to a computer system
Gaining access with intent to commit a further crime

cards.front: Under the Data Protection Act 2018, name the four things an organisation must do with personal data.
cards.answer: Keep it secure and accurate / Use it only for the reason it was collected / Keep it no longer than needed / Let people see the data held about them
items: Use it only for the reason it was collected
Keep it no longer than needed
Let people see the data held about them

cards.front: Why can being on the wrong side of the digital divide cause problems for someone?
cards.answer: They can miss out on jobs, education and services that are increasingly only available online.

cards.front: Why might a school with little money but skilled staff choose open source software?
cards.answer: To save on licence fees and to customise the software for their lessons.

title: Rock and Pop: The Features That Give the Style Away
subject: music-aqa

cards.front: Name the six individual features the lesson says you should listen for one at a time to identify rock or pop in an unfamiliar extract.
cards.answer: Line-up / Structure / Riff / Backbeat / Feel / Production

cards.front: Name the sections that can appear in a rock/pop verse-chorus form, as given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Intro / Verse / Chorus / Bridge / Middle eight

cards.front: How does layering build up the sound of a modern pop track?
cards.answer: Producers stack drums, bass, synth chords and vocal harmonies on top of each other, building the sound gradually across the track.

cards.front: Why is a middle eight often placed after the second chorus in a song?
cards.answer: It is a contrasting passage that takes the listener somewhere new, such as a different chord pattern, key change or texture drop, before the final chorus returns.

cards.front: Name the three functions Pinnock's code-switching serves in Leave Taking.
cards.answer: Characterisation (reveals cultural position) / Thematic (mirrors heritage vs assimilation tension) / Dramatic (exposes Enid's contradiction)

cards.front: Name the two theatre productions the lesson cites as key to Leave Taking's critical reception.
cards.answer: 1994 National Theatre production / 2018 Bush Theatre revival

cards.front: Why should analysis of Leave Taking connect specific details to social and historical context?
cards.answer: Because top-band responses must explain not just what Pinnock shows but why she chose to show it, linking to Windrush-era experience.

cards.front: Why is Winsome Pinnock's own background significant to the context of Leave Taking?
cards.answer: She writes from within a community whose stories had been largely absent from mainstream British theatre.

title: Identifying Substances: Flame Tests and Gas Tests
subject: separate-sciences-ocr

cards.front: Name the four gases the lesson gives specific chemical tests for.
cards.answer: Hydrogen / Oxygen / Carbon dioxide / Chlorine

cards.front: In the silver nitrate test for halide ions, what precipitate colour does each halide give?
cards.answer: Chloride - white precipitate / Bromide - cream precipitate / Iodide - yellow precipitate

cards.front: Why must the nichrome wire loop be cleaned in concentrated hydrochloric acid before a flame test?
cards.answer: To remove residues from previous tests, which could contaminate the sample and give a misleading colour result.

cards.front: Why can flame emission spectroscopy identify potassium in a mixture where a simple flame test cannot?
cards.answer: It produces a spectrum with separate lines for each metal, so sodium's intense colour can't mask potassium's lines.

title: Engineering Calculations: Area, Volume, Density and Pressure
subject: engineering-aqa

cards.front: Name the three area formulas given in the lesson (for rectangle, triangle and circle).
cards.answer: Rectangle: A = length × width / Triangle: A = ½ × base × height / Circle: A = πr²

cards.front: Name the five SI prefixes given in the lesson, with their multipliers.
cards.answer: milli = ×10⁻³ / centi = ×10⁻² / kilo = ×10³ / mega = ×10⁶ / giga = ×10⁹

cards.front: Why does a stiletto heel damage a wooden floor more than a flat shoe, for the same person's weight?
cards.answer: The same force is applied over a much smaller area, which concentrates it into a much higher pressure.

cards.front: Why do students often lose marks on calculation questions even when their arithmetic is correct?
cards.answer: They leave the answer in the wrong unit instead of converting to the required unit as the final step.

title: Popular entertainment and fashion: from teddy boys to punk
subject: history-eduqas

cards.front: Name the four youth subcultures the lesson lists appearing in Britain from the 1950s to the 1970s.
cards.answer: Teddy boys / Mods and Rockers / Hippies / Punks

cards.front: Name the four fashion features of teddy boys described in the lesson.
cards.answer: Drape jackets / Drainpipe trousers / Brothel creeper (crepe-soled) shoes / Quiff hairstyles

cards.front: Why did a distinct teenage consumer culture emerge in Britain in the 1950s?
cards.answer: Rising wages gave young workers disposable income for the first time, creating a new commercial culture of music, fashion and cinema aimed at them.

cards.front: Why did punk reject the hippie movement and progressive rock?
cards.answer: Punk was a violent reaction against hippie idealism's 'peace and love' message and against the pomposity and commercial success of progressive stadium rock.

title: Development in a Developing or Emerging Country
subject: geography-edexcel-a

cards.front: Name the four reasons the lesson gives for why India's coastal and southern states form the economic core.
cards.answer: Access to ports for trade / Longer history of education investment / Better infrastructure / Stronger state governance

cards.front: Name the three government schemes the lesson gives as responses to the negative impacts of India's rapid development.
cards.answer: National Clean Air Programme / Swachh Bharat sanitation drive / Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana housing scheme
items: Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana housing scheme

cards.front: Why is female labour force participation in India so low, at around 27%?
cards.answer: It is held back by social expectations, safety concerns and limited childcare.

cards.front: How does the lesson say India's government makes megaprojects and welfare schemes work together most effectively?
cards.answer: By using tax revenue from megaprojects to fund welfare schemes, combining the scale of top-down projects with the fairness of bottom-up schemes.

cards.front: Name the four demands the Levellers made, as stated in the lesson.
cards.answer: a widened male franchise / equality before the law / freedom of conscience in religion / an end to arbitrary imprisonment

cards.front: Name the three other radical religious groups the lesson mentions besides the Quakers.
cards.answer: Ranters (denied sin and conventional morality) / Fifth Monarchists (believed Second Coming was imminent) / Muggletonians
items: Fifth Monarchists (believed Second Coming was imminent)

cards.front: Why did the New Model Army become a political as well as military force after 1645?
cards.answer: Its soldiers debated theology and read pamphlets, and religious ferment combined with grievances over pay and disbandment to politicise them.

cards.front: Why did Ireton want the vote restricted to property owners at the Putney Debates?
cards.answer: He feared that if all men could vote, the propertyless majority would use it to abolish property rights.

cards.front: Why do professional programmers split large programs into many small subroutines instead of one long block of code?
cards.answer: Each subroutine can be tested independently (unit testing), so if a bug appears later, only that subroutine needs checking.

cards.front: Why can using too many global variables make a program harder to debug?
cards.answer: Because any part of the program can read or change a global variable unexpectedly, making unwanted changes hard to trace.

cards.front: Name the four functions of the family identified by Murdock in his 1949 study.
cards.answer: Sexual / Reproductive / Economic / Educational

cards.front: Name the three sociological perspectives that compete over what functions the family performs.
cards.answer: Functionalists (Murdock, Parsons) / Feminists (Oakley, Delphy and Leonard) / Marxists (Zaretsky, Engels)

cards.front: Why did Murdock conclude that the nuclear family is universal?
cards.answer: His study of 250 societies found the nuclear family present in every one, performing four essential functions.

cards.front: Why do Marxists argue the family acts as a unit of consumption under capitalism?
cards.answer: Because family members purchase goods and services that generate profit for the bourgeoisie.

cards.front: Name the four members of the Birling family analysed in the lesson.
cards.answer: Arthur Birling / Sybil Birling / Sheila Birling / Eric Birling

cards.front: What three things does Arthur Birling's concern in the play focus on throughout?
cards.answer: His potential knighthood / his family's social standing / avoiding a public scandal

cards.front: Why did Eric turn to alcohol and theft instead of asking his parents for help?
cards.answer: The family's obsession with appearances meant Eric felt he couldn't confide in his parents, so he drank and stole money secretly instead.

cards.front: How do Sheila's and Eric's reactions to the Inspector's message differ?
cards.answer: Sheila's awakening is intellectual and moral, understanding the systemic problem, while Eric's is emotional and instinctive, driven by guilt and anger.

cards.front: Name the four forms the 'beast' takes as it evolves through the novel.
cards.answer: Beastie or snake-thing (littluns' nightmare) / Beast from water / Beast from air (the dead parachutist) / The Lord of the Flies itself
items: The Lord of the Flies itself

cards.front: What four locations does Golding map onto his philosophical argument, and what does each represent?
cards.answer: Beach and platform - democratic, open governance / Castle Rock - tyranny / Mountain - truth and knowledge / Jungle - the unknown and darkness within
items: Beach and platform - democratic, open governance
Jungle - the unknown and darkness within

cards.front: Why does Golding make Piggy's death happen at the same moment as the conch's destruction?
cards.answer: He binds the symbol and its champion together, showing that democracy and rational thought rise and fall as one.

cards.front: How does Golding use face paint to invert colonial assumptions about 'savages'?
cards.answer: Victorian literature linked face paint to primitive non-European 'savages', so by having British schoolboys wear it, Golding shows the 'civilised' become the savages.

cards.front: Name the five roles religious houses played in local communities before 1535.
cards.answer: Landlords renting out farms / Employers of servants and labourers / Hosts for travellers / Schools for gentry's sons / Almoners giving food to the poor
items: Almoners giving food to the poor

cards.front: Name the three historians' explanations the lesson gives for the dissolutions.
cards.answer: Bernard: Henry's personal greed and suspicion of independent institutions / MacCulloch: Cromwell's genuine evangelical reforming conviction / National Archives: long fiscal afterlife creating a gentry landowning class
items: Bernard: Henry's personal greed and suspicion of independent institutions
MacCulloch: Cromwell's genuine evangelical reforming conviction
National Archives: long fiscal afterlife creating a gentry landowning class

cards.front: Why did the crown sell off most monastic land instead of keeping it?
cards.answer: Selling raised cash for war and bound gentry, lawyers and merchants to the Reformation, as they'd lose land if Catholicism returned.

cards.front: How did the Pilgrimage of Grace lead to the fall of the larger monasteries?
cards.answer: After it was crushed in 1537 and abbots were implicated, larger houses lost political protection and were pressured into surrendering with pensions.

cards.front: Name the three ways electronic systems can be represented.
cards.answer: System block diagram / Circuit schematic / PCB layout

cards.front: What four steps should you follow to complete a partially drawn block diagram in an exam?
cards.answer: Identify blocks already drawn and their stage / Identify what is missing / Work out each empty block's function / Draw signal arrows between every block
items: Identify blocks already drawn and their stage
Work out each empty block's function
Draw signal arrows between every block

cards.front: Why is the freezer temperature alarm system classed as closed loop?
cards.answer: The microcontroller continuously reads the thermistor's output, checking and re-checking temperature rather than acting once, creating a feedback loop.

cards.front: How do you tell if a missing block in a diagram is an input block?
cards.answer: It is an input block if it converts an environmental signal, like temperature, into an electrical signal.

cards.front: Name the five stages of Rostow's model.
cards.answer: Traditional society / Preconditions for take-off / Take-off / Drive to maturity / High mass consumption

cards.front: Name the four organisations that partnered to fund Nigeria's polio vaccination teams.
cards.answer: World Health Organization / UNICEF / Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation / Rotary International

cards.front: Why did falling oil prices in 2014 and 2020 cause Nigeria to fall into recession?
cards.answer: Because oil supplies most government income, so falling prices weakened the naira and pushed the economy into recession.

cards.front: Why do most geographers place Nigeria at stage 3, 'take-off', of Rostow's model?
cards.answer: Because a few sectors like oil, telecoms and fintech are growing fast, infrastructure is improving, and a small middle class has appeared.

cards.front: Name the three things Orwell's use of allegory achieves, according to the lesson.
cards.answer: Makes complex politics accessible through familiar characters / Creates emotional engagement with the story / Achieves universality beyond Russia
items: Makes complex politics accessible through familiar characters
Creates emotional engagement with the story

cards.front: Name the three specific luxury items in the farmhouse that symbolise privileges the revolution was meant to abolish.
cards.answer: Beds / China / Whisky

cards.front: Why is the farm itself described as a microcosm in Animal Farm?
cards.answer: Its closed boundaries let Orwell trace the full arc of a society from rebellion to tyranny in one contained world.

cards.front: How does Minimus's replacement anthem show that cultural control serves political power?
cards.answer: It replaces 'Beasts of England' with a bland song about the farm, hiding the gap between promises and reality.

cards.front: Name the four activities included in Hector's general studies lessons.
cards.answer: Reciting poetry / Re-enacting scenes from films / Singing songs / Debating ideas

cards.front: What three things does Hector's 'passing the parcel' metaphor reveal about his teaching?
cards.answer: He is part of a chain from his own teachers / Knowledge is not for anything, just passed on / He hands it on to people he'll never meet
items: He is part of a chain from his own teachers
Knowledge is not for anything, just passed on
He hands it on to people he'll never meet

cards.front: Why is the Headmaster so eager to sack Hector once the abuse is revealed?
cards.answer: He resents that Hector's teaching produces results he cannot measure, so the abuse gives him a convenient excuse to remove him.

cards.front: Why does Irwin tell the boys to argue that the dissolution of the monasteries was a good thing?
cards.answer: To demonstrate contrarian thinking — arguing against the obvious, even the indefensible, to stand out to Oxbridge examiners.

cards.front: Name the four sampling methods the lesson identifies.
cards.answer: Random sampling / Stratified sampling / Volunteer sampling / Opportunity sampling

cards.front: Name the three research designs the lesson identifies for organising participants across conditions.
cards.answer: Independent measures / Repeated measures / Matched pairs

cards.front: Why does using different participants in each condition (independent measures) avoid order effects?
cards.answer: Because each participant only takes part once, so there is no practice or fatigue across conditions.

cards.front: Why is stratified sampling likely to produce a highly representative sample?
cards.answer: Because it divides the population into subgroups and selects participants from each in proportion to their size.

cards.front: What three themes does the lesson identify in 'Love After Love'?
cards.answer: Self-love as recovery / Neglect and return / Ritual

cards.front: Name the four anthology poems given as comparison partners for 'Love After Love'.
cards.answer: Poem for My Love / The Perseverance / Flirtation / Lullaby

cards.front: Why does Walcott use second-person address ('you') throughout 'Love After Love'?
cards.answer: It makes the poem feel like direct advice or a personal promise, collapsing the 'you' addressed and the welcomed self into one person.

cards.front: How does the poem's free verse form suit its theme of breaking old patterns?
cards.answer: Free verse refuses the tight, repeating shapes that might suggest an unchanging relationship, keeping movement forward before tightening into short commands.

title: How Citizens Bring About Political Change
subject: citizenship-aqa

cards.front: Name the three levels at which political campaigns can take place, according to the lesson.
cards.answer: Local / National / International

cards.front: Name the five methods campaigners use, as given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Social media / Press releases / Rallies / Door-knocking / Producing written materials

cards.front: Why does digital exclusion concern critics of digital democracy?
cards.answer: Older citizens, disabled people, or those without internet access may find digital channels harder to use, so some voices are heard less.

cards.front: Why is standing for election seen as one of the most direct forms of democratic participation?
cards.answer: It places an individual in a position to make decisions, scrutinise legislation, and represent a constituency.

cards.front: Name the five other anthology poems the lesson pairs with Boat Stealing for comparison.
cards.answer: Songs for the People / Colonization in Reverse / Papa-T / We Lived Happily during the War / Thirteen
items: We Lived Happily during the War

cards.front: Which three short quotable phrases does the lesson recommend memorising for exam use?
cards.answer: troubled pleasure / like a living thing / unknown modes of being

cards.front: Why does Wordsworth tell Boat Stealing through an adult narrator looking back on a boyhood memory?
cards.answer: The retrospective narration lets him frame a simple childhood incident as the origin of the idea that nature shapes a person's growth of mind and conscience.

cards.front: Why does the calm, graceful imagery at the start of the poem matter for the cliff's appearance?
cards.answer: The calm imagery of the boat moving like a swan makes the sudden, shocking appearance of the huge cliff feel far more dramatic.

cards.front: Name the five pricing methods covered in this lesson.
cards.answer: Price skimming / Penetration pricing / Competitive pricing / Loss leader / Cost-plus

cards.front: Name the four factors that influence a business's pricing decisions.
cards.answer: Costs / Nature of the market / Degree of competition / Product life cycle stage

cards.front: Why does a strong brand image make it easier for a business to launch new products?
cards.answer: Customers already trust the established brand name, so they are willing to try its new products, as with Apple's move into phones and watches.

cards.front: Why do businesses carry out market research before launching a new product?
cards.answer: To reduce the risk of the new product failing before the business commits cash to it.

cards.front: Name the four creative concepts the lesson says shape how sounds are arranged for media.
cards.answer: Texture / Mood / Style / Impact

cards.front: Name the five export formats the lesson explains for finished audio/video.
cards.answer: MP4 / MOV / MP3 / WAV / AIF (AIFF)

cards.front: Why do sound designers create contrast between high-impact and low-impact sounds in a scene?
cards.answer: Contrasting a loud, attention-grabbing sound with a quiet background one creates drama.

cards.front: How is the final audio combined with the video file for delivery?
cards.answer: The DAW or video editor bounces the finished audio mix and embeds it into the video container, such as MP4 or MOV.

title: Consumerism, coffee houses and political activism
subject: history-ocr

cards.front: Name the three things London's coffee houses were centres of, according to the lesson.
cards.answer: Political debate / Commerce (e.g. Lloyd's marine insurance) / Press culture (newspapers read aloud)

cards.front: Name the six types of workers/industries the lesson says participated indirectly in the slave trade in Britain's slave ports.
cards.answer: Shipbuilders / Rope-makers / Ironmongers / Textile merchants / Insurance brokers / Dock workers

cards.front: Why did ideas of racial hierarchy become more systematised in British thought from the late seventeenth century?
cards.answer: Because the slave trade required ideological justification, so ideas classifying people by skin colour with different capacities and rights developed.

cards.front: How did journals like The Spectator reach a wide readership in the 1710s and 1720s?
cards.answer: Through coffee houses, where copies were passed from reader to reader.

cards.front: Name the four ways given in the lesson to increase the rate of a reaction.
cards.answer: Raising temperature / Increasing concentration (or pressure for gases) / Increasing surface area of solid reactants / Using a catalyst
items: Increasing surface area of solid reactants

cards.front: Name the three common methods the lesson gives for measuring reaction rate.
cards.answer: Gas collection / Mass loss / Colour/turbidity change

cards.front: Why does raising the temperature increase the rate of reaction, according to collision theory?
cards.answer: Particles gain more kinetic energy, move faster and collide more often, with a greater proportion exceeding the activation energy.

cards.front: Why does increasing concentration increase the rate of reaction?
cards.answer: More particles in a given volume means collisions between reactant particles happen more frequently.

title: Sit-Ins, Freedom Riders and James Meredith, 1960-62
subject: history-edexcel

cards.front: Name the three types of abuse sit-in students were trained to absorb without responding.
cards.answer: Verbal abuse / lit cigarettes pushed into their hair / food poured over them
items: Lit cigarettes pushed into their hair

cards.front: Name the three campaigns of 1960-62 that forced the federal government to enforce a Supreme Court ruling Southern states were ignoring.
cards.answer: The Greensboro sit-ins / the Freedom Riders / the Meredith/Ole Miss case

cards.front: Why did press photographs of the Greensboro sit-ins help persuade public opinion?
cards.answer: They showed well-dressed students sitting calmly while white teenagers screamed abuse at them.

cards.front: Why was Robert Kennedy forced to send federal marshals to protect the Freedom Riders after Anniston?
cards.answer: Photographs of the firebombed bus and Birmingham beatings were broadcast worldwide, forcing federal action despite his reluctance.

title: The Buddha and the Four Noble Truths
subject: religious-studies-aqa

cards.front: What are the three forms of craving (tanha) the Buddha identified?
cards.answer: Craving for sense pleasures / Craving for existence (wanting things to continue) / Craving for non-existence (wanting things to stop)
items: Craving for existence (wanting things to continue)
Craving for non-existence (wanting things to stop)

cards.front: What are the three parts of the Threefold Way that structure the Eightfold Path?
cards.answer: Ethics / Meditation / Wisdom

cards.front: Why is ignorance (moha) considered the deepest of the Three Poisons?
cards.answer: Because it produces the false belief in a fixed, permanent self, from which greed and hatred then arise.

cards.front: Why did Siddhartha abandon the path of extreme asceticism after nearly dying from it?
cards.answer: He recognised that extreme self-mortification, like extreme luxury, would not lead to liberation, so he sought a balanced Middle Way.

cards.front: Name the four levels of Regency society's social hierarchy, from top to bottom.
cards.answer: Aristocracy / Landed gentry / Professionals / Servants and labourers

cards.front: Why is Mrs Bennet's frantic matchmaking not simply comic?
cards.answer: Because entailment means she and her daughters will lose their home and income when Mr Bennet dies, so marriage is a survival strategy.

cards.front: Why does Mr Collins propose to Elizabeth?
cards.answer: Partly to 'make amends' for inheriting the Bennet estate that would otherwise have gone to the daughters.

cards.front: Name the three reasons Mr Collins gives for proposing to Elizabeth (without ever mentioning love).
cards.answer: Lady Catherine's approval / his duty as a clergyman / the entail

cards.front: How does Austen use Wickham as a foil to Darcy?
cards.answer: Wickham is charming but morally bankrupt while Darcy seems proud but is genuinely honourable, reversing first impressions.

cards.front: Why is Darcy's letter the novel's structural turning point?
cards.answer: It reveals Wickham's true character and forces Elizabeth to recognise her own prejudice, splitting the novel into before and after.

title: The Solar System: Planets, Dwarf Planets and Small Bodies
subject: astronomy-edexcel

cards.front: Name the five recognised dwarf planets in the Solar System.
cards.answer: Pluto / Ceres / Eris / Haumea / Makemake

cards.front: Name the three distance units used in astronomy.
cards.answer: Astronomical unit (AU) / Light year (ly) / Parsec (pc)

cards.front: Why does Venus have the highest surface temperature of any planet, despite not being closest to the Sun?
cards.answer: Venus has an extreme greenhouse effect, which raises its surface temperature to about 460°C regardless of its distance from the Sun.

cards.front: Why did the rocky material in the asteroid belt never accrete into a planet?
cards.answer: Jupiter's strong gravitational influence constantly stirred the region, preventing the remnant planetesimals from accreting into a planet.

cards.front: What three tones does the lesson give for Hood's, Clare's and Wordsworth's poems about childhood belonging?
cards.answer: Hood: elegiac and mournful / Clare: celebratory and communal / Wordsworth: urgent and optimistic

cards.front: What structural technique does the lesson say each poet uses — Hood, Clare and Wordsworth?
cards.answer: Hood: regular stanzas with a past-to-present turning point / Clare: rhyming couplets running on smoothly / Wordsworth: short punchy stanzas with imperative verbs
items: Hood: regular stanzas with a past-to-present turning point
Clare: rhyming couplets running on smoothly
Wordsworth: short punchy stanzas with imperative verbs

cards.front: Why is Clare's celebration of childhood freedom in nature described as especially poignant?
cards.answer: Because his later life was marked by mental illness and institutional confinement, contrasting with his memories of open countryside freedom.

cards.front: How does Hood's stanza structure reinforce the theme that belonging is easier in childhood than adulthood?
cards.answer: Each stanza contrasts bright, elevated childhood memories with a present-day adult perspective heavy with loss.

cards.front: Name the four factors the lesson gives for choosing the right production process.
cards.answer: Volume of output needed / Degree of customisation required by customers / Target cost per unit / Level of flexibility the market demands
items: Degree of customisation required by customers
Level of flexibility the market demands

cards.front: Name the four variables the lesson says are traded off when a business invests in production technology.
cards.answer: Cost / Productivity / Quality / Flexibility

cards.front: Why can 3D printing help small businesses compete with traditional job production?
cards.answer: It lets them produce customised items at a lower cost than traditional job production methods.

cards.front: Why do businesses in competitive markets tend to move from job to batch to flow production as they grow?
cards.answer: Lower costs per unit enable lower prices, which help the business win greater market share.

cards.front: Name the four different ways the lesson says the same logic circuit can be described.
cards.answer: A written description in plain English / A Boolean expression / A logic diagram of gates / A completed truth table
items: A written description in plain English

cards.front: In a Boolean expression, what symbol is used for each of the three basic operations: AND, OR and NOT?
cards.answer: A dot for AND / A plus sign for OR / A bar over a letter for NOT
items: A bar over a letter for NOT

cards.front: For the circuit Q = (A AND B) OR C, how do you work out the value of Q for each row of the truth table?
cards.answer: Work out A AND B first as a helper column, then apply OR between that helper column and C.

cards.front: Why is a bubble drawn on the tip of a NOT gate's symbol?
cards.answer: The bubble shows the signal is being inverted, telling you the gate flips its input from 0 to 1 or 1 to 0.

cards.front: The lesson groups Lagos's growth-related challenges into four big areas. Name them.
cards.answer: Housing / Services / Jobs and crime / Environment

cards.front: Name the three types of environmental pressure the lesson describes in Lagos.
cards.answer: Waste piling up in dumps and the lagoon / Water pollution from sewage, industrial waste and oil / Air pollution from generators, traffic and burning rubbish
items: Waste piling up in dumps and the lagoon
Water pollution from sewage, industrial waste and oil
Air pollution from generators, traffic and burning rubbish

cards.front: Why were Makoko residents left with no protection when the government demolished parts of the slum in 2012?
cards.answer: Houses were built without planning permission and residents had no formal land title, so they had no legal protection from demolition.

cards.front: Why does Lagos's traffic 'go-slow' hit informal workers hardest financially?
cards.answer: Workers in the informal economy are paid by the day, so hours lost sitting in gridlock directly cut their earnings.

title: Describing Systems: Block Diagrams, Schematics and Flowcharts
subject: engineering-aqa

cards.front: Name the three main tools engineers use to describe systems, from the lesson.
cards.answer: Block diagrams / Schematic drawings / Flowcharts

cards.front: Name the six sub-systems of a car given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Engine management / Braking / Steering / Lighting / Infotainment / Climate control

cards.front: Why are most industrial control systems, like cruise-control or furnace controllers, closed-loop?
cards.answer: Because small disturbances, such as draughts or varying load, would cause the output to drift without feedback correction.

cards.front: Why would a circuit diagram not be accepted in place of a block diagram?
cards.answer: Because it shows how components are wired, not the system stages the block diagram question asks for.

cards.front: Name the four inner (rocky) planets of the solar system.
cards.answer: Mercury / Venus / Earth / Mars

cards.front: What three challenges of space exploration does the lesson give?
cards.answer: Extreme distances involved / Hostile environment (radiation, vacuum, microgravity) / Enormous cost

cards.front: Why do the inner planets orbit the Sun faster than the outer planets?
cards.answer: They are closer to the Sun, so they experience stronger gravitational attraction, making them orbit faster.

cards.front: What happens to a satellite if its speed is too low or too high for its orbit?
cards.answer: Too low a speed makes it spiral inward; too high a speed makes it move to a higher orbit or escape entirely.

title: Woven, Non-Woven and Knitted Textile Construction
subject: design-technology-eduqas

cards.front: What are the three fundamental weave structures described in the lesson?
cards.answer: Plain weave / Twill weave / Satin weave

cards.front: What are the three methods used to bond fibres into non-woven fabrics?
cards.answer: Mechanical entanglement (needle-punching or hydroentangling) / Thermal bonding (melting synthetic fibres to fuse the web) / Chemical bonding (applying an adhesive binder)
items: Thermal bonding (melting synthetic fibres to fuse the web)

cards.front: Why does twill weave drape better than plain weave?
cards.answer: Twill has fewer interlacement points than plain weave, allowing the yarns to move more freely.

cards.front: Why is warp knit fabric more dimensionally stable than weft knit?
cards.answer: Multiple yarns run lengthways and interlock sideways on each course, so it does not ladder or distort easily.

cards.front: Name the four historical events between 1912 and 1945 that the 1945 audience already knew had shattered the Birlings' world.
cards.answer: First World War (1914–1918) / General Strike (1926) / Great Depression (1929–1939) / Second World War (1939–1945)

cards.front: Name the three post-war creations Priestley's campaigning helped bring about after the 1945 Labour landslide.
cards.answer: The NHS / Free education / Social security

cards.front: Why did Birling sack Eva Smith?
cards.answer: She took part in a strike demanding a pay rise from 22s6d to 25s a week, and Birling saw no moral problem in firing strikers.

cards.front: Why did An Inspector Calls premiere in Moscow before London?
cards.answer: Partly because Soviet socialist values aligned with Priestley's message, and partly because London theatres were fully booked.

cards.front: Name the three major Catholic plots against Elizabeth between 1571 and 1586.
cards.answer: Ridolfi Plot (1571) / Throckmorton Plot (1583) / Babington Plot (1586)

cards.front: What multiple causes does the lesson give for Mary's execution in 1587?
cards.answer: Babington letter gave written proof / 1585 Act for Queen's Surety allowed it / Parliament and Privy Council pushed for years / Spanish invasion fleet preparations were visible
items: 1585 Act for Queen's Surety allowed it
Parliament and Privy Council pushed for years
