Spanish invasion fleet preparations were visible

cards.front: Why did Walsingham let Mary's letters keep flowing through the beer barrel channel at Chartley?
cards.answer: So Mary would commit herself in writing approving Elizabeth's assassination, giving legal proof to convict her.

cards.front: How did Phelippes use the Babington letter to expose the other plotters?
cards.answer: He forged a postscript asking Babington to name his fellow conspirators, resealed it, and let it through.

cards.front: Name the three factors the lesson gives for variation in UK climate across the country.
cards.answer: Latitude / Altitude / Distance from the sea

cards.front: Name the three factors the lesson gives as producing the UK's mild, wet climate.
cards.answer: Latitude in the mid 50s °N / The Gulf Stream warming Atlantic air / Prevailing south-westerly winds bringing moisture
items: The Gulf Stream warming Atlantic air

cards.front: Why does the equator receive roughly twice as much solar energy per square metre as the poles?
cards.answer: The Sun's rays strike the equator almost vertically but hit the poles at a glancing angle.

cards.front: How do depressions form along the polar front?
cards.answer: Warm subtropical air meets cold polar air, and the temperature and density contrast forces air upwards, creating cloud and rain.

cards.front: Name the six strategies in the 6Rs framework for metal sustainability.
cards.answer: Reduce / Reuse / Recycle / Refuse / Repair / Rethink

cards.front: Name the four applications of shape memory alloys given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Medical stents / Orthodontic arch wires / Actuators in engineering / Eyeglass frames

cards.front: Why can the aluminium drink can have such a thin wall despite holding a carbonated drink?
cards.answer: The internal pressure of the contents stiffens the can, so the thin wall is strong enough (the pressurised vessel effect).

cards.front: Why does declining copper ore grade increase the energy used in extraction?
cards.answer: Lower-concentration deposits mean more rock must be processed per tonne of copper recovered, raising energy use and waste rock volume.

title: The Romantic Concerto: The Age of the Virtuoso Soloist
subject: music-ocr

cards.front: Name the three virtuoso techniques the lesson says Paganini used to astonish audiences.
cards.answer: Rapid double-stopping / Harmonics / Left-hand pizzicato

cards.front: Name four extra instruments the lesson says were added to the Romantic orchestra beyond the Classical orchestra.
cards.answer: Piccolo / Cor anglais / Bass clarinet / Contrabassoon / Trombones / Tuba

cards.front: Why did composers write thicker orchestration and wider dynamic contrasts for Romantic concertos?
cards.answer: Because concerts moved to bigger purpose-built concert halls, and a bigger room demanded a bigger, louder sound.

cards.front: How did the role of the cadenza change from the Classical to the Romantic era?
cards.answer: It changed from being often improvised by the performer to being fully composed by the composer and integrated into the structure.

title: Rivonia Trial and the long silence
subject: history-ocr

cards.front: Why did Mandela argue that the ANC's use of sabotage was justified?
cards.answer: Because the apartheid government's violence against its own citizens had made peaceful protest impossible, leaving sabotage as a last resort.

cards.front: How did the Rivonia Trial backfire on the apartheid government?
cards.answer: Mandela's smuggled dock statement spread internationally, turning the accused into martyrs and boosting the ANC's reputation abroad, prompting UN resolutions for their release.

cards.front: Name the four advantages (Vorteile) of social media given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Stay in contact with friends/family far away / Useful for school - find info and work with classmates / Meet new people and discover different cultures / It's fun and entertaining
items: Stay in contact with friends/family far away
Useful for school - find info and work with classmates
Meet new people and discover different cultures

cards.front: Name the four disadvantages (Nachteile) of social media given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Cyberbullying is a big problem / Too much screen time causes sleep problems / Data protection problems - info not always safe / Social media can be addictive
items: Too much screen time causes sleep problems
Data protection problems - info not always safe

cards.front: Why is 'das Handy' called a false friend in German technology vocabulary?
cards.answer: It looks like the English word 'handy' but actually means 'mobile phone', not something useful.

cards.front: How does using 'einerseits ... andererseits' help you present a balanced opinion on social media?
cards.answer: It lets you state one advantage (staying in contact with friends) then contrast it with a disadvantage (too much screen time being unhealthy).

cards.front: Name the five areas of life the lesson says social class determines outcomes in, according to Russell's play.
cards.answer: Education / Employment / Health / Housing / Survival

cards.front: How does Russell use the Johnstones' move to Skelmersdale to show class cannot be escaped by relocation?
cards.answer: Moving to a new estate doesn't change the family's class; the same poverty, unemployment and lack of opportunity follow them.

cards.front: Why does Russell argue that education reinforces class division rather than breaking it down?
cards.answer: Eddie's private school encourages and supports him toward university, while Mickey's comprehensive has low expectations and scarce resources, leading him to unemployment.

cards.front: Why does the Moon appear to go through phases as seen from Earth?
cards.answer: The Sun always lights half the Moon, but as the Moon orbits Earth we see different fractions of that lit half.

cards.front: Why did the late nineteenth century see the world divided into time zones?
cards.answer: Because if every location kept its own Local Mean Time, clocks would differ town to town, making travel and communication chaotic.

cards.front: Name the six staging configurations the lesson identifies.
cards.answer: Proscenium arch / Thrust stage / Theatre in the round / Traverse / End-on staging / Promenade

cards.front: Why can a proscenium arch theatre support illusionistic staging with hidden machinery?
cards.answer: The audience sees only one face of the stage, so the wings to either side stay invisible, hiding backdrops and machinery.

cards.front: Why does traverse staging create a sense of surveillance or voyeurism?
cards.answer: The two audience banks face each other across the action, so each group can see the other watching the performance.

cards.front: Name the four separation techniques described in the lesson for different mixtures.
cards.answer: Filtration / Crystallisation / Simple distillation / Fractional distillation

cards.front: Name the three steps used in the UK to produce potable water from fresh water sources.
cards.answer: Sedimentation / Filtration / Chlorination

cards.front: Why is a pencil line (not pen) used for the baseline in paper chromatography?
cards.answer: Pencil is insoluble and will not dissolve in the solvent, unlike pen ink.

cards.front: Why must water used for chemical analysis not contain dissolved salts?
cards.answer: Dissolved ions could interfere with test results, giving false positives or inaccurate measurements.

cards.front: Name the four purposes of marketing set out in the specification.
cards.answer: Identifying customers / Understanding customers / Informing customers / Increasing sales

cards.front: Name the three businesses given as examples of identifying a specific target customer group, and their target group.
cards.answer: LEGO – children aged 4-11 and parents / Saga – over-50s / Aldi – price-conscious shoppers

cards.front: Why did Ben Francis spend time in gyms and on Instagram before advertising Gymshark?
cards.answer: To understand what young gym-goers actually wanted before informing them about the product.

cards.front: Why can a brilliant product still fail even with good marketing?
cards.answer: Because a brilliant product no customers know about will fail, so marketing must inform them for sales to happen.

title: Regulation, Digital Disruption and the BBFC, OFCOM, IPSO, ASA and PEGI
subject: media-studies-aqa

cards.front: Name the six UK media regulatory bodies given in the lesson.
cards.answer: OFCOM / IPSO / BBFC / ASA / PEGI / Video Standards Council (VSC)

cards.front: Name the five PEGI age rating categories for video games.
Why does digital disruption challenge the existing media regulation framework?
cards.answer: Social media lets billions publish unscreened content, anonymous speech enables harassment, and deepfakes/disinformation spread faster than regulators can respond.

cards.front: Why do critics see a risk in OFCOM's statutory status?
cards.answer: A government-backed regulator always risks political influence over the media it oversees.

title: The Four Aims of Life and Dharma
subject: religious-studies-aqa

cards.front: Name the four stages of life (ashramas) described in the lesson.
cards.answer: Student stage (brahmacharya) / Householder stage (grihastha) / Retirement stage (vanaprastha) / Renunciation stage (sannyasa)

cards.front: How does dharma act as a guardrail for the pursuit of artha and kama?
cards.answer: Wealth and pleasure are only wrong when pursued through greed, deception, lust or exploitation, which transgress dharma.

cards.front: Why do many Hindus prefer the term sanatana dharma over the word 'Hinduism'?
cards.answer: Because sanatana dharma stresses that its principles are universal and eternal, not tied to one culture, unlike the colonial-era term 'Hinduism'.

cards.front: Name the four types of work the lesson gives as examples of Lagos's informal economy.
cards.answer: Street selling / Motorbike taxis (okadas) / Small workshops repairing phones and TVs / Casual building work
items: Small workshops repairing phones and TVs

cards.front: Name the five formal services or resources the lesson says Lagos provides that rural villages cannot.
cards.answer: Specialist hospital care / University-level education / Piped water system / National grid electricity / Waste collection in planned districts

cards.front: Why would Lagos keep growing even if migration into the city stopped completely?
cards.answer: Migrants are mostly young adults who have children, birth rates stay high, and the death rate has fallen due to better healthcare and clean water.

cards.front: Why do sociologists describe Lagos's informal economy as the city's 'real economy'?
cards.answer: Because for most new arrivals it is the first, and often only, way to earn enough to put food on the table.

cards.front: Name the three dramatists of the Manchester School mentioned in the lesson.
cards.answer: Harold Brighouse / Stanley Houghton / Allan Monkhouse

cards.front: According to the lesson, what four things does AO3 context for Hobson's Choice require understanding of?
cards.answer: Victorian Salford / the rigid class system / attitudes to women / why Brighouse set the play in 1880 but wrote it decades later
items: why Brighouse set the play in 1880 but wrote it decades later

cards.front: Why does Willie Mossop work in the cellar while Maggie, Alice and Vickey work on the shop floor?
cards.answer: It creates a spatial hierarchy showing the most skilled worker has the lowest position, critiquing a system that rewards ownership over ability.

cards.front: Why did Hobson initially prefer Albert Prosser and Fred Beenstock over Willie Mossop as sons-in-law?
cards.answer: Because as a solicitor's son and a corn merchant's son they carried social status, which Hobson valued over Willie's practical skill.

cards.front: Name the four common metal stock forms described in the lesson.
cards.answer: Sheet and plate / Bar and rod / Tube / Angle section

cards.front: Name the four types of force that metals experience in service.
cards.answer: Tension / Compression / Shear / Torsion

cards.front: Why does quenching during hardening produce a hard but brittle steel structure?
cards.answer: Rapid cooling prevents carbon atoms migrating, locking a hard but brittle martensite crystal structure in place.

cards.front: Why is tube a more efficient stock form than solid rod for making a handrail?
cards.answer: Starting from tube eliminates the need to bore out the centre, saving time and material waste.

cards.front: Name the three colour worlds Deakins uses to structure Skyfall's visual journey.
cards.answer: Shanghai / Macau / Scottish Highlands

cards.front: Name the three named sequences given as micro-analysis worked examples in the lesson.
cards.answer: Macau-casino lizard-pit confrontation / Whitehall public-inquiry attack / Skyfall-house chapel finale

cards.front: Why does Deakins shift the palette from Shanghai's neon darkness to the Scottish Highlands' desaturated tones?
cards.answer: The shift strips Bond of his urban slickness, placing him in a bleaker, more exposed setting as narrative punctuation.

cards.front: Why does the colour change from gold to cold blue in the Macau lizard-pit confrontation matter?
cards.answer: It signals a sudden change in power dynamic, marking the transition from spectacle to threat.

cards.front: Name the three concessions Nicholas II made in the October Manifesto.
cards.answer: Civil rights (speech, assembly, conscience) / Legal political parties / An elected parliament (the Duma)

cards.front: Name the three things that saved the Tsarist regime after the 1905 Revolution.
cards.answer: The October Manifesto split the opposition / The war with Japan ended, freeing troops / The army stayed loyal
items: The October Manifesto split the opposition
The war with Japan ended, freeing troops

cards.front: Why did the October Manifesto split the opposition to the Tsar?
cards.answer: Liberals and Octobrists welcomed its concessions while revolutionaries dismissed them, so moderates now had something to lose by joining further uprisings.

cards.front: How did ending the Russo-Japanese War help the Tsar crush the Moscow Uprising?
cards.answer: The Treaty of Portsmouth brought the field army home from Manchuria, freeing reliable troops to crush the uprising with artillery.

cards.front: Name the three factors the lesson gives for why Viking raids on England began.
cards.answer: Population pressure in Scandinavia pushed younger sons abroad / Advances in longship technology allowed raids far inland / Anglo-Saxon England was divided and rich in monasteries
items: Population pressure in Scandinavia pushed younger sons abroad
Advances in longship technology allowed raids far inland
Anglo-Saxon England was divided and rich in monasteries

cards.front: Name the three military reforms Alfred introduced to defend Wessex after Edington.
cards.answer: Divided the fyrd into two rotating halves / Built or strengthened thirty burhs across Wessex / Invested in a small fleet for naval defence
items: Divided the fyrd into two rotating halves
Built or strengthened thirty burhs across Wessex
Invested in a small fleet for naval defence

cards.front: Why did dividing the fyrd into two halves help Alfred's defence of Wessex?
cards.answer: One half could always be on campaign while the other worked the fields, ending armies dispersing at harvest.

cards.front: Why did Æthelred's St Brice's Day massacre in 1002 lead to full-scale invasion?
cards.answer: The massacre of Danish settlers provoked the Danish king Sweyn Forkbeard to launch a full invasion of England.

cards.front: Name the three ways media ownership can change, according to the lesson.
cards.answer: Merger / Takeover / Demerger

cards.front: Name the three supply-chain stages a vertically integrated film conglomerate might own.
cards.answer: Production (studio creating content) / Distribution (gets content to retailers/broadcasters) / Exhibition (streaming service or cinema chain)

cards.front: How does diversification reduce financial risk for a media conglomerate?
cards.answer: If one division performs poorly in a given year, profits from another division can compensate.

cards.front: Why are independent (indie) producers not entirely free from conglomerate power structures?
cards.answer: They often rely on conglomerate-owned distributors to get their work to audiences.

cards.front: Name the four things the lesson says the kyria managed within the Athenian household.
cards.answer: Supervised domestic slaves / Managed food stores and finances / Organised weaving and cloth production / Raised and cared for children

cards.front: Name the four occasions the lesson gives when Athenian women could leave the house.
cards.answer: Attend religious festivals / Visit other women / Attend funerals / Collect water

cards.front: Why was the gynaikon usually placed at the back or upper floor of an Athenian house?
cards.answer: To stop women being seen by men arriving at or leaving the house, keeping them separate from male visitors.

cards.front: Why did weaving matter as a symbol of Athenian female virtue?
cards.answer: It was practically useful for producing household cloth, but also symbolically showed a woman's domestic virtue and loyalty, as with Penelope.

title: Investigating the Work of Designers and Companies
subject: design-technology-eduqas

cards.front: Name the five designers/companies you need to know for the exam.
cards.answer: Airbus / Apple / James Dyson / Philippe Starck / Matthew Williamson

cards.front: Name the three linked ideas to focus on when writing about Apple in an extended answer.
cards.answer: Minimalism / Material precision / Integration

cards.front: Why did Apple remove the headphone jack from the iPhone?
cards.answer: To reduce the number of components and waterproofing failure points, reflecting Apple's philosophy of simplification despite short-term controversy.

cards.front: Why does Airbus's design philosophy prioritise engineering precision over aesthetics?
cards.answer: Because decisions like using composite materials are driven by measurable performance data and safety regulations, not visual style.

title: The Babadook: Narrative and Grief as Monster
subject: film-studies-eduqas

cards.front: Name the four production companies/organisations that produced or backed The Babadook.
cards.answer: Causeway Films / Smoking Gun Productions / Screen Australia / South Australian Film Corporation

cards.front: Name the three diegetic domestic sounds mixed louder than naturalism requires in The Babadook.
cards.answer: Clocks / Creaking floorboards / Samuel's night-terrors

cards.front: How does the film's desaturated palette make the Babadook's appearance more disturbing?
cards.answer: Because the world is already drained of colour, the Babadook's high-contrast black-and-white shapes feel like a graphic intrusion rather than darkness entering a bright space.

cards.front: Why is sudden silence used in the police-station sequence?
cards.answer: The ambient domestic sound drops completely on the cut, and this contrast is more unsettling than a jump scare.

cards.front: Name the four areas the USSR expanded into after signing the Nazi-Soviet Pact.
cards.answer: Eastern Poland / The Baltic states / Finland / Romania

cards.front: Why did Stalin sign the Nazi-Soviet Pact in August 1939?
cards.answer: To buy time and keep the USSR out of the coming war while gaining territory in Eastern Europe.

cards.front: Why is the Battle of Stalingrad seen as the turning point of the war on the Eastern Front?
cards.answer: It was Germany's first major defeat there, shifting the strategic initiative to the Soviet Union for the rest of the war.

cards.front: The lesson names five common everyday sources of free sugars that people often overlook. What are they?
cards.answer: Ketchup / Low-fat yoghurt / Ready-made pasta sauces / Flavoured drinks / Breakfast cereals

cards.front: What are the three common scenarios given for using nutritional data to make targeted recipe changes?
cards.answer: Increasing dietary fibre (NSP) / Reducing saturated fat / Meeting free sugar recommendations

cards.front: Why does swapping 50 g butter for 50 g olive oil greatly reduce saturated fat even though total fat barely changes?
cards.answer: Butter is about 52% saturated fat while olive oil is only about 15% saturated, so total fat stays similar but saturated fat drops sharply.

cards.front: How can you check whether a recipe's stated kcal-per-serving figure is plausible?
cards.answer: Multiply the grams of fat, carbohydrate and protein by their energy yields (9, 3.75, 4 kcal/g) and add the results to compare with the stated figure.

cards.front: Name the four additions Leicester made to Kenilworth for Elizabeth's visits in the 1570s.
cards.answer: Leicester's Building (state apartments) / a grand new gatehouse / great windows cut into the Norman keep / a privy garden
items: great windows cut into the Norman keep

cards.front: Name the six entertainments the lesson describes at the 1575 visit.
cards.answer: fireworks / hunting / masques / bear-baiting / an Italian tumbler / a swimming pageant with Arion

cards.front: Why do historians think the 1575 visit was Leicester's last bid to marry Elizabeth?
cards.answer: The pageants staged masques of marriage and a lady freed from an enchanted lake, and a planned marriage-themed entertainment was never performed, likely because the queen declined it.

cards.front: How did Leicester turn the mere, an old medieval defence, into part of his entertainment for Elizabeth?
cards.answer: The mere, which had once made Kenilworth almost siege-proof, was used as a stage for water pageants, including the swimming performance of Arion on a mechanical dolphin.

title: The Trinity, the Incarnation and Jesus as Moral Authority
subject: religious-studies-eduqas

cards.front: In the Sermon on the Mount, what three examples does Jesus give showing that interior disposition matters, not just external acts?
cards.answer: Anger is the root of murder / Lust is the root of adultery / Generosity must be given freely without public display
items: Anger is the root of murder
Lust is the root of adultery
Generosity must be given freely without public display

cards.front: Why does the Incarnation give Catholic theology a deep respect for material and bodily existence?
cards.answer: Because if God became truly human, human nature — including bodily existence, suffering and death — has been taken into the life of God.

cards.front: Why is it significant that it is the incarnate Son of God, not just a human being, who suffers on the Cross?
cards.answer: Because Jesus is fully God and fully human, so his suffering shows God himself entering the darkest human experience.

cards.front: Name the six relational operators in Python.
cards.answer: == (equal to) / != (not equal to) / (greater than) / = (greater than or equal to)

cards.front: Name the three logical operators in Python.
cards.answer: and / or / not

cards.front: Why does adding a string and an integer together in Python cause a TypeError?
cards.answer: Because Python's + operator can only concatenate strings, so a number must first be converted to a string with str().

cards.front: Why is len(s) - 1 used to get the last character of a string instead of a negative index?
cards.answer: Because Python does not include negative indexes, so len() is used to calculate the position of the last character.

title: Rehabilitation & Reducing the Risk of Injury
subject: cambridge-nationals-sport-science

cards.front: Name the four group characteristics a risk assessment considers when deciding on supervision and precautions.
cards.answer: Age / Experience / Medical conditions / Group size

cards.front: Name the three methods used in medical screening before contact sport.
cards.answer: Health questionnaires / Physical examinations / Electrocardiograms (ECGs)

cards.front: How does electrotherapy help an injured performer during rehabilitation?
cards.answer: It uses electrical stimulation, such as TENS, to reduce pain and stimulate contractions in weakened muscles.

cards.front: Why is PNF stretching particularly useful in the later stages of rehabilitation?
cards.answer: Contracting then stretching the muscle in PNF stretching helps the athlete regain full flexibility at the injured joint.

title: From Page to Stage: The Rehearsal Process
subject: drama-aqa

cards.front: Name the seven main stages of a professional rehearsal process, in order.
cards.answer: Read-through / Blocking rehearsals / Character and scene work / Production meetings / Technical rehearsal / Dress rehearsal / Previews

cards.front: Name the three reasons the lesson gives for why a short scene might take an hour to tech.
cards.answer: A lighting state may need refocusing / A sound cue may arrive at the wrong moment / A scene change may need to be refined
items: A lighting state may need refocusing
A sound cue may arrive at the wrong moment
A scene change may need to be refined

cards.front: Why might a director ask a performer to try a scene both in stillness and with continuous movement during early rehearsals?
cards.answer: To find out which choice communicates more clearly to the audience at the back of the house, testing whether the director's concept works.

cards.front: How does a production meeting turn a director's technical request into a working solution?
cards.answer: The director states a specific need, the designer proposes a solution, and the stage manager records it in production notes.

cards.front: Name the three network topologies covered in the lesson.
cards.answer: Bus (single shared cable) / Star (central hub) / Ring (loop of devices)

cards.front: Name the six hardware devices the lesson describes as making a network function.
cards.answer: Router / Switch / Hub / Modem / Network interface card (NIC) / Wireless Access Point (WAP)

cards.front: Why does performance get worse in a bus topology as more devices are added?
cards.answer: Because all devices share the same single backbone cable to send and receive data.

cards.front: How does encryption protect data from packet sniffing?
cards.answer: It scrambles data using a key so intercepted packets appear as meaningless ciphertext without the decryption key.

cards.front: According to the lesson, what three qualities does Orwell use to build reader sympathy for Boxer before his death?
cards.answer: His loyalty / His gentleness / His simple decency

cards.front: How does Squealer explain away the horse slaughterer's writing on the side of the van?
cards.answer: He claims the van used to belong to a knacker but was now owned by a vet who hadn't repainted it.

cards.front: Why does Orwell suggest Benjamin is complicit in the pigs' crimes even though he never actively helps them?
cards.answer: He has the intelligence and literacy to prove the commandments are being changed but does nothing, letting the pigs act unchallenged.

cards.front: Why does Boxer's broken retirement promise represent Orwell's most damning criticism of the Soviet system?
cards.answer: It symbolises the social contract between workers and the state — work hard and you'll be looked after — which Napoleon betrays completely.

title: Lenses, Visible Light and Black Body Radiation
subject: science-aqa

cards.front: Name the three standard rays used to draw a ray diagram for a convex lens.
cards.answer: Ray parallel to the axis, refracts through the principal focus / Ray through the centre of the lens, passes straight through unbent / Ray through the near focus, refracts to become parallel to the axis
items: Ray parallel to the axis, refracts through the principal focus
Ray through the centre of the lens, passes straight through unbent
Ray through the near focus, refracts to become parallel to the axis

cards.front: Name the three secondary colours formed by mixing two primary colours of light.
cards.answer: Red + green = yellow / Red + blue = magenta / Green + blue = cyan

cards.front: How do a cyan filter and a yellow filter together produce only green light?
cards.answer: The cyan filter absorbs red and the yellow filter absorbs blue, so together they absorb both, transmitting only green.

cards.front: How does the greenhouse effect increase the Earth's surface temperature?
cards.answer: Greenhouse gases absorb outgoing infrared radiation and re-emit some of it back towards the Earth, raising the surface temperature.

cards.front: Name the four types of daily offerings made to the Lares.
cards.answer: Incense / Wine / Cakes / Garlands

cards.front: Name the three deities honoured in the Capitolium temple at Pompeii's forum.
cards.answer: Jupiter / Juno / Minerva

cards.front: Why was the Genius of the paterfamilias worshipped at the household shrine?
cards.answer: Worshipping his divine life-force reinforced the authority of the male head of household within the family's religious and social life.

cards.front: Why is it significant that Horace mentions Roman religious practice only in passing?
cards.answer: The incidental, unexplained nature of his references suggests religious practice was so ordinary it needed no explanation.

cards.front: Name the five types of love Shakespeare presents in Romeo and Juliet.
cards.answer: Petrarchan love / True romantic love / Physical love / Parental love / Friendship love

cards.front: Name the four moments the lesson uses to show violence escalating through the play.
cards.answer: The servants' brawl (Act 1, Scene 1) / Tybalt's fury at the ball / Mercutio's death and Tybalt's killing (Act 3, Scene 1) / The double suicide in the tomb (Act 5, Scene 3)
items: Mercutio's death and Tybalt's killing (Act 3, Scene 1)
The double suicide in the tomb (Act 5, Scene 3)

cards.front: Why does the lesson argue that love and violence are connected rather than opposites in Romeo and Juliet?
cards.answer: Romeo kills Tybalt out of love for Mercutio, Juliet kills herself for love of Romeo, and the feud only ends because the parents love their dead children enough to stop fighting.

cards.front: How does honour culture create an endless cycle of violence in the play?
cards.answer: Honour culture demands every insult be answered with a sword, so even Romeo, who tries to refuse fighting Tybalt, gets dragged back into the cycle.

title: Native Americans, Chicanos and other civil rights movements
subject: history-ocr

cards.front: Name the four problems the lesson says Native Americans faced before the civil rights movements.
cards.answer: Extreme poverty / High unemployment / Poor health outcomes / Broken treaty promises

cards.front: Name the four directions the Chicano movement developed in beyond the UFW.
cards.answer: Alianza Federal de Mercedes (Tijerina) / Crusade for Justice (Gonzales) / LA school walkouts (1968) / La Raza Unida Party (1970)

cards.front: Why were many charges against AIM leaders after Wounded Knee eventually dismissed?
cards.answer: They were dismissed due to government misconduct, later linked to FBI surveillance of AIM documented by the Church Committee.

cards.front: Why did Native American activists argue the Indian Civil Rights Act 1968 was a limited gain?
cards.answer: It gave legal rights but did not restore treaty lands, so conditions on reservations remained dire without an economic base.

cards.front: What four reforms did Dubcek's Action Programme introduce in April 1968?
cards.answer: Abolished censorship and let independent newspapers flourish / Released political prisoners / Began to decentralise economic planning / Allowed open debate of past Stalinist abuses
items: Abolished censorship and let independent newspapers flourish
Allowed open debate of past Stalinist abuses

cards.front: What three responses did younger reformers turn to after concluding change inside the system was impossible post-1968?
cards.answer: Silent emigration / Dissident protest / Simple cynicism

cards.front: Why was Brezhnev alarmed by the success of the Prague Spring reforms?
cards.answer: He feared that if the Czech experiment succeeded, reformers in Poland, East Germany and elsewhere would press for similar reforms.

cards.front: Why were East German troops held back at the border during the August 1968 invasion?
cards.answer: To avoid awakening memories of the German occupation of Czechoslovakia in 1938-39.

title: Closing the Gap: Aid, Trade & Tourism in The Gambia
subject: geography-aqa

cards.front: Name the seven main strategies geographers identify for reducing the global development gap.
cards.answer: Investment / Industrial development / Tourism / International aid / Intermediate technology / Fair trade / Microfinance loans / debt relief

cards.front: Give the three examples of intermediate technology used in the lesson, with their countries.
cards.answer: Hand-drilled wells in Malawi / Treadle pumps in Bangladesh / Clay pot fridges in Sudan

cards.front: How does the multiplier effect help a poorer country's economy through tourism?
cards.answer: Money tourists spend gets re-spent locally on food, building materials and education, circulating through the economy.

cards.front: Why do charities like Oxfam favour aid that builds local capacity rather than giving handouts?
cards.answer: Because aid can create dependency or be misused if governments are corrupt, so capacity-building aid avoids these problems.

title: Questionnaires, Pilot Studies and Cleaning Data
subject: statistics-aqa

cards.front: Name the five key features to consider when designing a good questionnaire.
cards.answer: Leading questions / Avoiding biased sources / Choice of open or closed questions / Interview technique / Time factors
items: Choice of open or closed questions

cards.front: What four purposes does a pilot study serve before the main data collection?
cards.answer: Identifying ambiguous or unclear questions / Checking response categories are exhaustive and mutually exclusive / Estimating how long the questionnaire takes / Revealing leading or loaded language
items: Checking response categories are exhaustive and mutually exclusive
Estimating how long the questionnaire takes

cards.front: Why might asking about sleep habits on a Monday give misleading results?
cards.answer: Answers on a Monday reflect weekend sleep patterns, so they differ from typical mid-week sleep, biasing the data.

cards.front: Why does excluding non-respondents from analysis risk biasing the results?
cards.answer: If the people who didn't respond share a characteristic, excluding them makes the remaining data unrepresentative.

cards.front: Name the four methods the lesson gives for preventing rusting.
cards.answer: Galvanising (zinc coating) / Painting / Oiling / Using a sacrificial metal

cards.front: Name the four common alloys the lesson describes and what metals each contains.
cards.answer: Steel: iron + carbon / Bronze: copper + tin / Brass: copper + zinc / Gold alloys: gold + silver or copper
items: Gold alloys: gold + silver or copper

cards.front: Why does the solution turn from blue to pale green when iron is added to copper sulfate solution?
cards.answer: Iron displaces copper, forming pale green iron(II) sulfate solution while copper metal is deposited on the iron.

cards.front: Why is limestone added to a blast furnace during iron extraction?
cards.answer: Limestone removes acidic silicon dioxide impurities by reacting with them to form calcium silicate slag, which is tapped off separately.

cards.front: Name the four rules the lesson gives about magnetic field lines.
cards.answer: Run from north to south outside the magnet / Closer lines mean a stronger field / Strongest at the poles, weakens with distance / Field lines never cross
items: Run from north to south outside the magnet
Closer lines mean a stronger field
Strongest at the poles, weakens with distance

cards.front: Name the five uses of electromagnets given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Scrapyard cranes / Electric bells / Relays / Loudspeakers / MRI scanners

cards.front: Why does the Earth have a magnetic field?
cards.answer: It is produced by convection currents in the Earth's liquid outer core.

cards.front: How does a loudspeaker use the motor effect to create sound? (Higher tier)
cards.answer: A varying current in a coil inside a magnetic field changes the motor-effect force, pushing the cone in and out to make sound waves.

cards.front: Name the three staging methods used to distinguish flashbacks from present-day scenes in Refugee Boy.
cards.answer: Different lighting (warm/harsh tones) / Changes in music / Physical positioning

cards.front: Why does Refugee Boy juxtapose a scene of Alem at school in England with a scene of violence in Ethiopia?
cards.answer: It forces the audience to hold two realities in mind at once, deepening their understanding of what Alem carries with him.

cards.front: Why is the structure of Refugee Boy non-chronological rather than linear?
cards.answer: It reflects Alem's own experience of trauma, which does not follow a neat timeline, so memories intrude on the present.

cards.front: Name the four sources of formal support the lesson identifies.
cards.answer: Professionals / Trained volunteers / Support groups / Charities

cards.front: Name the four sources of informal support the lesson identifies.
cards.answer: Friends / Family / Neighbours / Community and work colleagues

cards.front: How does regular cardiovascular exercise lower resting heart rate?
cards.answer: It strengthens the heart muscle, which lowers the resting heart rate over time.

cards.front: How does high blood pressure affect a person's health risk?
cards.answer: High blood pressure (140/90 mmHg or above) increases the risk of stroke and heart disease.

title: Book 1 Continued: The Fall of Civilisation
subject: english-literature-eduqas

cards.front: The lesson names four sounds that create the invasion's alien atmosphere — what are they?
cards.answer: Fighting machines howl 'Aloo! Aloo!' / Dying Martian wails 'Ulla, ulla, ulla, ulla' / The Heat-Ray hisses and crackles / The Black Smoke settles silently
items: Dying Martian wails 'Ulla, ulla, ulla, ulla'

cards.front: Name the three real-world events or ideas the lesson says Book 1 proved prophetic about.
cards.answer: WW1 poison gas attacks / WW2 evacuations of London / Modern disaster scenarios of infrastructure collapse
items: Modern disaster scenarios of infrastructure collapse

cards.front: Why does Wells focus so much on the sounds of the invasion?
cards.answer: To create an atmosphere of alien menace, using sounds recognisable enough to be terrifying but strange enough to feel inhuman.

cards.front: Why does the brother witness both kindness and savagery during the exodus?
cards.answer: Wells shows humanity without illusions, capable of both compassion and brutality when placed under extreme pressure.

title: Mao's death, the Gang of Four and the Democracy Wall
subject: history-ocr

cards.front: The lesson gives three purposes served by the Gang of Four trial. Name them.
cards.answer: Drew a line under the Cultural Revolution / Blamed the four defendants rather than Mao or the Party / Showed commitment to socialist legality
items: Drew a line under the Cultural Revolution
Blamed the four defendants rather than Mao or the Party

cards.front: Why did Deng Xiaoping initially tolerate the Democracy Wall?
cards.answer: Its criticisms of the Cultural Revolution undermined Hua Guofeng's legitimacy, since Hua was associated with Mao's legacy.

cards.front: Why is the Third Plenum of 1978 seen as the formal end of the Maoist era?
cards.answer: It shifted the Party's focus from class struggle, Maoist politics' defining feature, to economic modernisation.

title: Conquering Wales: The Wars of 1277 and 1282-83
subject: history-aqa

cards.front: Name the three acts of defiance by Llywelyn that Edward saw as breaking the Treaty of Montgomery, leading to the 1277 war.
cards.answer: Refused to perform homage five times / Sheltered his rebel brother Dafydd / Planned marriage to Eleanor de Montfort
items: Refused to perform homage five times
Planned marriage to Eleanor de Montfort

cards.front: Name the four castles in Edward's first ring, built to garrison the lands won in 1277.
cards.answer: Flint / Rhuddlan / Builth / Aberystwyth

cards.front: Why was Llywelyn forced to surrender by November 1277?
cards.answer: Edward's fleet occupied Anglesey, the 'granary of Snowdonia', cutting Llywelyn off from his harvest and starving him into submission.

cards.front: Why did Dafydd ap Gruffudd attack Hawarden Castle at Palm Sunday 1282?
cards.answer: Dafydd had switched sides to Edward in 1277 but felt the rewards he received were inadequate, so he rebelled.

title: Mechanical Calculations: Levers, Gears and Pulleys
subject: design-technology-eduqas

cards.front: Why does a long spanner undo a tight bolt more easily than a short one?
cards.answer: A longer effort arm from the pivot needs a smaller effort force to produce the same moment, balancing the load.

cards.front: Why must the belt not slip in a belt-and-pulley system for the velocity ratio calculation to work?
cards.answer: Friction between the belt and pulley is essential so the belt transmits speed correctly between the driver and driven pulleys.

cards.front: According to the lesson, what three things does Pip spend money on in London that he hasn't earned?
cards.answer: Clothes / Furniture / Entertainment

cards.front: Name the three features of Wemmick's miniature Walworth home mentioned in the lesson.
cards.answer: A miniature castle / A moat / A cannon

cards.front: Why does Pip assume Miss Havisham, rather than Magwitch, is his benefactor?
cards.answer: Because in Victorian society the idea of a convict funding a gentleman was unthinkable, so Pip assumes a wealthy patron instead.

cards.front: Why does Wemmick act completely differently at Jaggers's office compared with at home in Walworth?
cards.answer: The professional world forces him to suppress his humanity, so he creates a private world at home where genuine feeling can survive.

title: Types of School and Educational Provision
subject: sociology-eduqas

cards.front: Name the six main types of school in the UK given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Comprehensive schools / Grammar schools / Academies / Free schools / Private (independent) schools / Faith schools

cards.front: According to Ball, what four things do middle-class parents do to navigate school choice?
cards.answer: Read league tables / Visit multiple schools / Write effective appeals / Move into desirable catchment areas

cards.front: Why do critics argue that grammar schools entrench class inequality?
cards.answer: Middle-class families can afford private tuition to prepare children for the eleven-plus, while working-class families typically cannot.

cards.front: How does Ball argue marketisation reinforces the class gap in education?
cards.answer: Middle-class families use cultural capital and social networks to navigate school choice, while working-class families lack this, concentrating advantage.

title: Little Rock and the White Backlash, 1955-60
subject: history-edexcel

cards.front: Name the three forms of massive resistance to Brown that this lesson identifies.
cards.answer: KKK violence and terror / Dixiecrat political obstruction in Congress / White Citizens' Councils economic coercion

cards.front: Name the three groups the White Citizens' Councils pressured to punish Black activists economically.
cards.answer: Banks (to call in mortgages) / Employers (to dismiss activists) / Suppliers (to refuse goods)

cards.front: Why did Eisenhower send federal troops to Little Rock in September 1957?
cards.answer: Faubus had used state troops to defy a federal court order, creating a constitutional crisis threatening federal authority, not a civil rights issue Eisenhower chose to act on.

cards.front: Why did the 1957 Civil Rights Act end up being a weak law?
cards.answer: Lyndon Johnson stripped it of meaningful enforcement powers to persuade Southern senators to allow a vote on it.

cards.front: Name the three advantages of continuous training given in the lesson.
cards.answer: No specialist equipment needed (simplicity) / Low cost / Can be done almost anywhere

cards.front: Name the three advantages of fartlek training given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Variety, which reduces boredom / Flexibility, performer chooses when to sprint / Replicates unpredictable demands of team sports
items: Flexibility, performer chooses when to sprint
Replicates unpredictable demands of team sports

cards.front: Why do performers need a strength base before starting plyometric training?
cards.answer: Plyometric exercises involve high impact on the joints and muscles, so a solid strength base is needed first.

cards.front: Why is interval training seen as flexible for coaches?
cards.answer: Coaches can precisely control the intensity, duration and number of repetitions to match the specific demands of the sport.

cards.front: Name the three types of plate boundary described in the lesson.
cards.answer: Destructive (convergent) boundary / Constructive (divergent) boundary / Conservative (transform) boundary

cards.front: Name the three larger-scale volcanic landforms described in the lesson.
cards.answer: Shield volcanoes / Stratovolcanoes (composite volcanoes) / Calderas

cards.front: Why do mountains form instead of volcanoes where two continental plates collide?
cards.answer: Neither plate is denser than the other, so neither subducts; the rocks crumple upwards into mountains like the Himalayas.

cards.front: Why are shield volcanoes wide with gentle slopes rather than steep cones?
cards.answer: They are built from runny basaltic lava that flows fast and far across the surface before it cools.

cards.front: Name the five types of stress/force the lesson says a designer must consider when selecting a polymer.
cards.answer: Tension (pulling apart) / Compression (squeezing) / Torsion (twisting) / Bending / Shear (opposite forces across a cross-section)

cards.front: Name the four types of additive the lesson describes being added to polymers during compounding.
cards.answer: Plasticisers / Stabilisers / Pigments / Flame retardants

cards.front: Why are oxo-degradable plastics now banned in the EU?
cards.answer: Because they only fragment into microplastics rather than truly biodegrading.

cards.front: How does colouring a polymer with pigment differ from painting it?
cards.answer: Pigments disperse evenly through the melt giving consistent colour throughout the cross-section, whereas paint only coats the surface.

title: Pilgrimage, Festivals and the Church in the Community
subject: religious-studies-edexcel

cards.front: Name the three reasons the lesson gives for why pilgrimage is spiritually valuable.
cards.answer: Sacred places give a powerful encounter with the history of faith / The effort of the journey mirrors the spiritual life / Meeting other pilgrims builds community
items: Sacred places give a powerful encounter with the history of faith
The effort of the journey mirrors the spiritual life

cards.front: Name the three ways the lesson says Christians engage in mission.
cards.answer: Local outreach like food banks and street pastors / National programmes like Alpha courses and school chaplaincy / Global mission organisations
items: Local outreach like food banks and street pastors
National programmes like Alpha courses and school chaplaincy

cards.front: Why do many Protestant Christians argue that pilgrimage is not spiritually necessary?
cards.answer: They believe God is present everywhere, not concentrated in special places, following the Reformation's rejection of holy places as theologically significant.

cards.front: Why does Paul say the resurrection is essential to Christian belief in 1 Corinthians 15?
cards.answer: Because if Christ has not been raised, preaching is useless and faith is worthless, so resurrection is foundational not optional.

cards.front: Name the four key stages of the nitrogen cycle.
cards.answer: Nitrogen fixation / Nitrification / Denitrification / Decomposition

cards.front: Name the three human activities the lesson says disrupt the carbon, nitrogen and water cycles.
cards.answer: Burning fossil fuels / Fertiliser use and sewage release / Urbanisation and deforestation

cards.front: Why are waterlogged soils less fertile?
cards.answer: Denitrification removes available nitrogen (as N₂ gas) faster than nitrification can replace it.

cards.front: Why does urbanisation increase the risk of flash flooding?
cards.answer: Concrete and tarmac replace permeable soil, reducing infiltration and increasing surface run-off.

cards.front: What four techniques did the lesson describe as making up Roman siege warfare against Dacian hillforts?
cards.answer: Circumvallation (wall/ditch encircling the position) / Battering rams mounted in wheeled towers / Artillery firing stones and bolts / Approach ramps of earth built up to wall level
items: Battering rams mounted in wheeled towers
Approach ramps of earth built up to wall level

cards.front: Name the three ways the lesson says Rome commemorated military victories in permanent public form.
cards.answer: Triumphal arches at key road entry points / Victory columns in the forum / Coins struck to broadcast victory
items: Triumphal arches at key road entry points

cards.front: Why did Trajan launch the second, more brutal Dacian campaign?
cards.answer: Because Decebalus broke the terms he had agreed to after surrendering in the first war.

cards.front: How did the Roman army's standard tactic work in a set-piece battle?
cards.answer: Soldiers threw a pilum volley to disorder the enemy, closed to sword range, then overwhelmed them with disciplined pressure from the scutum-wall.

cards.front: What three documents do Utterson and Poole find on Jekyll's desk in Chapter 8?
cards.answer: A new will naming Utterson as beneficiary / A short note / A thick sealed packet containing Jekyll's confession
items: A new will naming Utterson as beneficiary
A thick sealed packet containing Jekyll's confession

cards.front: Name the three things Poole does that drive the action in Chapter 8's climax.
cards.answer: Goes to Utterson's house for help / Provides the axe / Identifies the changed voice
items: Goes to Utterson's house for help

cards.front: Why do Utterson and Enfield just walk away in silence after seeing Jekyll's terror at the window?
cards.answer: Faced with something terrible, they choose not to speak of it, reflecting Victorian repression.

cards.front: How does the breaking down of the cabinet door work symbolically in the novella?
cards.answer: It represents Utterson and Poole literally smashing through the wall of secrecy protecting Jekyll's hidden double life.

cards.front: Name the three ships Columbus sailed with on his 1492 voyage.
cards.answer: Santa María / Pinta / Niña

cards.front: According to the lesson, what five things did Columbus's voyages bring to the Americas?
cards.answer: Commerce / Christianity / Disease / Slavery / Destruction of entire cultures

cards.front: Why did Portugal reject Columbus's proposal for a westward route to Asia?
cards.answer: Portuguese experts correctly judged that his estimate of the distance to Asia was too short.

cards.front: Why did the gold tribute system on Hispaniola prove catastrophic for the Tainos?
cards.answer: The island's gold deposits were too shallow to meet the quota, so terror spread as failure led to punishment.

title: Staging and Design: A World on a Bare Stage
subject: drama-aqa

cards.front: Name the three objects the lesson gives as examples of physical transformation by performers (not visual trickery), and what each becomes.
cards.answer: Chairs become a railway carriage / Rope becomes ship rigging / Canes become multiple tools

cards.front: Name the three costume accessories the lesson gives that signal different locations in this production.
cards.answer: Pith helmet signals India / Captain's peaked cap signals the ship / Sheepskin hat signals the American West
items: Captain's peaked cap signals the ship
Sheepskin hat signals the American West

cards.front: Why does putting Fogg on a raised platform for the Reform Club give him visual authority?
cards.answer: He is literally above the world he is about to conquer, while Passepartout at floor level shows their contrasting status instantly.

cards.front: Why do lighting transitions replace scene changes in this production?
cards.answer: Because the set is minimal, changing the wash (e.g. amber to blue) instantly relocates the audience without moving any furniture.

cards.front: Name the four processes by which a river transports its load.
cards.answer: Traction / Saltation / Suspension / Solution

cards.front: Name the three human interventions that have reshaped the River Tees.
cards.answer: Reservoirs at Cow Green and Selset / Tees Barrage at Stockton / Floodplain reconnections at Saltholme
items: Reservoirs at Cow Green and Selset

cards.front: How does lateral erosion create a river cliff and a slip-off slope on a meander?
cards.answer: Fast water on the outside of the bend erodes a steep cliff, while slower water on the inside deposits sediment as a slip-off slope.

cards.front: Why does the upper Tees have very high peak discharges?
cards.answer: Rainfall often exceeds 2000mm combined with the impermeable Whin Sill rock, producing flashy upland flow.

cards.front: Name the three factors the lesson gives that affect enzyme activity.
cards.answer: Temperature / pH / Substrate concentration

cards.front: Name the three types of digestive enzyme described in the lesson.
cards.answer: Carbohydrases / Proteases / Lipases

cards.front: Why does enzyme activity increase as temperature rises towards the optimum?
cards.answer: Molecules move faster and collide more frequently with the active site, increasing the rate of reaction.

cards.front: Why does the rate of reaction level off at very high substrate concentrations?
cards.answer: All the active sites become occupied, so the enzyme is saturated and adding more substrate can't increase the rate.

cards.front: Name the four main types of infrastructure the construction sector delivers.
cards.answer: Roads and motorways / Railways / Bridges / Tunnels

cards.front: Name the five types of electrical services in building services engineering.
cards.answer: Energy supply / Lighting and low voltage systems / Communications / Fire detection and protection / Security and alarm systems

cards.front: Why do openings like doors and windows need lintels above them?
cards.answer: A lintel is a horizontal beam above the opening that carries the load of the wall above the gap.

cards.front: How does the fire detection system help stop fire spreading in a modern building?
cards.answer: It automatically shuts down ventilation ducts when smoke is detected, preventing fire from spreading through the ducts.

cards.front: Name the four interlocking themes Blackman develops through the novel's male characters.
cards.answer: Masculinity and emotional repression / Homophobia and its consequences / Fatherhood and responsibility / Family as a site of damage and recovery
items: Family as a site of damage and recovery

cards.front: What six key facts does the lesson say a student must get correct about the novel's plot?
cards.answer: Dante plans to study journalism / Emma is about ten months old, in a pushchair / The mother died of cancer, not left / Josh, Logan and Paul are the attackers / Adam is hospitalised, not taken home / Josh later turns himself in to police
items: Emma is about ten months old, in a pushchair
The mother died of cancer, not left
Josh, Logan and Paul are the attackers
Adam is hospitalised, not taken home
Josh later turns himself in to police

cards.front: Why does Josh respond to Logan's 'prove you're not gay' test with violence against Adam?
cards.answer: His unaddressed shame and concealed sexuality, tested under peer pressure, drives him to attack Adam to protect his public identity.

cards.front: Why does Blackman use Melanie as a structural counterpoint to Dante?
cards.answer: Her choice to leave, revealed by text message, sharpens the contrast with Dante's eventual choice to stay and be a father.

cards.front: Name the five pricing methods covered in this lesson.
cards.answer: Cost-plus pricing / Competitor pricing / Penetration pricing / Price skimming / Promotional pricing

cards.front: What four things shape a business's pricing decisions, according to this lesson?
cards.answer: Costs (the floor) / The product's USP / How crowded the market is / What the business is trying to achieve
items: What the business is trying to achieve

cards.front: Why can a business using competitor pricing never stand out on price alone?
cards.answer: Because it sets prices close to rivals, so it must differentiate through product, promotion or place instead.

cards.front: Why does price skimming fail for copy-cat products?
cards.answer: Without a genuine USP that early adopters want first, copy-cat products look overpriced and stick on the shelves.

cards.front: Name the four themes the lesson identifies in 'Korea'.
cards.answer: Betrayal / Coming of Age / Money / Irish History

cards.front: Besides the insurance money, what three things does the lesson say press on the father?
cards.answer: poverty / loss of the fishing licence / his own war memories

cards.front: How does the shared work of fishing function between father and son in 'Korea'?
cards.answer: It gives them a space to communicate without words, so the silence of the labour makes their spoken conversations feel more charged by contrast.

cards.front: Why does the narrator resist fully accepting his suspicion about his father?
cards.answer: Because accepting it fully would mean losing his father entirely, so he resists the conclusion his own evidence points to.

cards.front: Name the four models of marriage Austen presents in Pride and Prejudice.
cards.answer: Charlotte/Collins – pragmatic survival / Lydia/Wickham – reckless / Jane/Bingley – gentle affection / Elizabeth/Darcy – intellectual equality

cards.front: Why does Austen present money and marriage as a matter of survival rather than romance?
cards.answer: Because a woman's future depended almost entirely on the man she married, since Regency women could not own property, work or vote.

cards.front: Why does Austen suggest Elizabeth's idealism might be a 'luxury'?
cards.answer: Austen implies only a younger, prettier woman like Elizabeth can afford idealism, unlike Charlotte, who needs practical security.

cards.front: Name the three external consequences Adam faces at school for being openly gay.
cards.answer: Bullying / Hostility / Social isolation

cards.front: Name the three internal consequences Josh faces because he stays closeted.
cards.answer: Shame / Self-denial / Violence

cards.front: Why does Josh insist that his relationship with Adam must stay completely secret?
cards.answer: His internalised homophobia makes him ashamed of his attraction and unable to accept being gay, so he controls the relationship to hide it.

cards.front: How does Josh's internalised homophobia eventually lead to violence against Adam?
cards.answer: His unaddressed shame becomes an engine of violence, and Logan's test forces Josh to attack Adam to prove he isn't gay.

cards.front: Name the four key sequences the lesson identifies for micro/representation analysis in Tsotsi.
cards.answer: Township-arrival opening on the train platform / Childhood-flashback under the concrete pipes / Miriam apartment-feeding sequence / Closing house-return confrontation
items: Township-arrival opening on the train platform

cards.front: Name the three production companies that produced Tsotsi.
cards.answer: Industrial Development Corporation of South Africa / UK Film and TV Production Company / Tsotsi Films
items: Industrial Development Corporation of South Africa
UK Film and TV Production Company

cards.front: Why is the close-up on the protagonist's face held longer than conventional editing in the opening train-platform sequence?
cards.answer: It forces the spectator to read a face that gives little away, resisting a quick stereotyped judgement of him.

cards.front: Why does Hood use low-angle child-perspective shots in the childhood-flashback sequence?
cards.answer: They collapse the distance between adult and child, contextualising his gang identity as a learned response to trauma, not innate criminality.

cards.front: Name the four checks a risk assessment involves before training.
cards.answer: Facilities (safe surfaces, adequate space, no trip hazards) / Equipment (good repair, correctly adjusted, appropriate) / Participants (medical conditions, previous injuries, fitness concerns) / Rules or laws (health and safety and governing body compliance)
items: Facilities (safe surfaces, adequate space, no trip hazards)
Participants (medical conditions, previous injuries, fitness concerns)
Rules or laws (health and safety and governing body compliance)

cards.front: What five costs does 'cost of training' cover for a performer?
cards.answer: Gym membership fees / Equipment purchases / Travel / Specialist coaching / Competition entry fees

cards.front: Why must a coach carry out a risk assessment before a training session?
cards.answer: It checks facilities, equipment, participant numbers and the environment for hazards, protecting participants and showing duty of care.

cards.front: Why does a performer's gender need to be considered when designing a training programme?
cards.answer: Gender causes differences in average strength, hormonal profile and injury susceptibility, which should inform exercise selection and intensity.

title: Short and Long Term Effects of Exercise
subject: physical-education-aqa

cards.front: Name the three timescales into which the effects of exercise are categorised.
cards.answer: Immediate effects / Short-term effects / Long-term effects

cards.front: Name the four short-term effects of exercise that appear in the hours after training.
cards.answer: Tiredness and fatigue / Light-headedness / Nausea / Aching, cramp and DOMS

cards.front: Why does breathing become deeper and more frequent during exercise?
cards.answer: Rising CO2 levels are detected by chemoreceptors, which signal the respiratory centre to increase breathing rate and tidal volume.

cards.front: Why can light-headedness occur when exercise stops suddenly?
cards.answer: Blood pools in the lower limbs when exercise stops abruptly, before circulation fully readjusts, reducing blood flow to the brain.

cards.front: Name the four class contrasts Russell accumulates between Mickey and Eddie in the play.
cards.answer: Council estate vs private house / Dialect vs standard English / Factory job vs university degree / Prison sentence vs council seat

cards.front: Name the three life stages the lesson gives for the escalation of violence in the play.
cards.answer: Childhood: toy guns and war games / Adolescence: Sammy burning the school down / Adulthood: armed robbery, prison and the final shooting
items: Childhood: toy guns and war games
Adolescence: Sammy burning the school down
Adulthood: armed robbery, prison and the final shooting

cards.front: How does superstition work as a dramatic device in Blood Brothers?
cards.answer: It works as a plot mechanism keeping the secret, and as a thematic red herring distracting from class as the real cause.

cards.front: Why does Russell suggest motherhood is shaped by class through Mrs Johnstone and Mrs Lyons?
cards.answer: Mrs Johnstone's poverty forces her to give up a child, while Mrs Lyons' wealth allows her to take one.

cards.front: What four types of scholarship gave Dumenil a broader understanding of who was excluded from the 1920s boom?
cards.answer: Social history / African American history / Labour history / Women's history

cards.front: Why does the Sacco and Vanzetti case symbolise the 'nation of contrasts' interpretation of the 1920s?
cards.answer: It showed the US justice system could execute men based on their ethnicity and political beliefs, contradicting America's self-image as a land of freedom.

cards.front: Why did the Ku Klux Klan grow to 4-5 million members in the mid-1920s?
cards.answer: It drew its strength from rural communities that felt left behind by the urban economic boom.

title: Sanctity of Life and the Afterlife
subject: religious-studies-ocr

cards.front: Name three concrete ways Pikuach Nefesh affects Jewish life, according to the lesson.
cards.answer: A Jewish doctor must treat patients on Shabbat or festivals if life is at risk / A sick person may eat non-kosher food if medically necessary / Communities must fund emergency services
items: A Jewish doctor must treat patients on Shabbat or festivals if life is at risk
A sick person may eat non-kosher food if medically necessary

cards.front: Why do Orthodox Jewish authorities generally oppose active euthanasia?
cards.answer: Because Pikuach Nefesh is understood to protect and extend life, so deliberately shortening life, even to end suffering, goes against the principle.

cards.front: Why has classical Judaism generally resisted seeing the body as a prison for the soul?
cards.answer: Because a person is a unity of body and soul, the body is valued and respected, and G-d will ultimately restore the whole person, body and soul.

cards.front: Name the three 'forge virtues' the lesson says Pip must learn to value.
cards.answer: Honesty / Loyalty / Hard work

cards.front: What are the stages of Pip's story that mirror the Prodigal Son parable?
cards.answer: Receives a fortune / Leaves home / Wastes his money on idle living / Falls into poverty / Returns humbled
items: Wastes his money on idle living

cards.front: Why is Pip's decision to tell Magwitch his daughter is alive and beautiful, while hiding the painful truth, seen as his most selfless act?
cards.answer: He gains nothing from it and prioritises the dying man's comfort over honesty, showing genuine compassion beyond class prejudice.

cards.front: How does Pip's return to the forge differ from the son's return in the Prodigal Son parable?
cards.answer: The biblical son returns home physically, but Pip's return is moral, as he can never truly go back to the life he left.

cards.front: Name the four properties used to describe all waves.
cards.answer: Amplitude / Wavelength / Frequency / Wave speed

cards.front: What three things can happen when a wave meets a boundary between different materials?
cards.answer: Reflected / Refracted / Absorbed

cards.front: Why does a wave change direction when it undergoes refraction?
cards.answer: Because the wave changes speed as it passes into a different medium, causing it to bend towards or away from the normal.

cards.front: Why can you hear someone talking around a corner but not see them?
cards.answer: Sound has long wavelengths so it diffracts easily around obstacles, while light's very short wavelengths only diffract through extremely narrow slits.

cards.front: Name the four things geographers and the UN look at to measure gender equality.
cards.answer: Girls completing primary and secondary school / Women in paid work / Women in parliament / Maternal mortality
items: Girls completing primary and secondary school

cards.front: Name the other health measures the lesson says fill in the picture beyond life expectancy and infant mortality.
cards.answer: Doctors per 1,000 people / Access to vaccines / Rates of HIV / Rates of malaria / Rates of tuberculosis

cards.front: Why does Costa Rica show that a lower GDP doesn't mean a worse quality of life?
cards.answer: Despite much lower GDP per person than richer oil states, it has higher literacy, longer life expectancy and stronger gender equality.

cards.front: Why has the global social development gap narrowed for most of the 21st century?
cards.answer: Life expectancy has risen, child deaths have fallen and girls' school enrolment has climbed, helped by Millennium and Sustainable Development Goal funding.

title: Targeting Audiences: Marketing, Trailers and Viral Campaigns
subject: media-studies-aqa

cards.front: Name the three types of promotional preview material the lesson describes.
cards.answer: Trailer / Teaser / Taster

cards.front: Name the four types of research the lesson says organisations use to build audience profile assumptions.
cards.answer: Surveys / Focus groups / Ratings data / Behavioural data collected online

cards.front: Why can audience profiles sometimes reinforce existing inequalities?
cards.answer: Because the assumptions used to build audience profiles can be shaped by stereotypes of certain demographic groups.

cards.front: How do genre conventions shape the marketing of a horror film?
cards.answer: Producers base assumptions about who enjoys horror on prior audience data, which shapes the marketing approach, the certificate sought, and the promotion platforms.

title: The Hundred Years' War & English Identity
subject: history-aqa

cards.front: Name the three phases historians divide the Hundred Years' War into.
cards.answer: Edwardian (1337-1360) / Caroline (1369-1389) / Lancastrian (1415-1453)

cards.front: Name the three changes inside England that the Hundred Years' War accelerated.
cards.answer: English replaced French at court from 1362 / Parliament became indispensable for war taxation / A sharper sense of Englishness emerged
items: English replaced French at court from 1362
Parliament became indispensable for war taxation
A sharper sense of Englishness emerged

cards.front: Why did war with France make it politically awkward for English barons to keep speaking French at court?
cards.answer: Barons descended from Normans were now sent to fight in the name of an 'English' king against a 'French' enemy, hardening identity along language lines.

cards.front: Why did the loss of England's continental empire after 1450 help cause the Wars of the Roses?
cards.answer: With no continental wars to fight and no French territory to govern, military noble families turned on each other in civil war.

cards.front: Name the four characters who conspire together to humiliate Malvolio.
cards.answer: Sir Toby Belch / Maria / Sir Andrew Aguecheek / Fabian

cards.front: What four things does the forged letter instruct Malvolio to do?
cards.answer: Wear yellow stockings / Be cross-gartered / Smile constantly / Be rude to Sir Toby

cards.front: Why does Malvolio's soliloquy show his ambition is about power rather than love?
cards.answer: He fantasises about status, ordering officers, wearing a velvet gown, and controlling Sir Toby, not about loving Olivia.

cards.front: How does the trick on Malvolio turn from comedy into cruelty?
cards.answer: It exploits his genuine desire to be loved and respected, and escalates into his imprisonment in a dark room.

cards.front: Name the five typical characteristics the lesson gives for embedded systems.
cards.answer: Dedicated to one task / Small enough to fit inside another product / Low-powered so they run cool and cheaply / Low-cost due to mass production / Highly reliable
items: Small enough to fit inside another product
Low-powered so they run cool and cheaply

cards.front: Name the four areas of everyday life the lesson gives examples of embedded systems in.
cards.answer: Home appliances / Transport / Healthcare / Leisure and personal technology

cards.front: Why doesn't a microwave's controller need the processing power of a desktop PC?
cards.answer: It only needs enough power to do its single task, so a larger processor would just waste money and energy.

cards.front: What is the main trade-off of choosing an embedded system instead of a general-purpose computer?
cards.answer: It loses flexibility: it can't easily be upgraded or given new tasks, and firmware faults are hard to fix once sold.

cards.front: Name the three sources of carbon dioxide the lesson gives for human-caused emissions.
cards.answer: Burning fossil fuels / Deforestation / Cement production

cards.front: Name the three sources of methane the lesson gives.
cards.answer: Livestock digestive processes / Landfill sites (decomposing waste) / Rice paddy fields

cards.front: How did the formation of the ozone layer allow complex life to evolve on land?
cards.answer: Ozone absorbs harmful UV radiation from the Sun, protecting land organisms from UV damage.

cards.front: Why is methane described as more potent than CO2 in the short term but not overall?
cards.answer: Methane traps more heat than CO2 over a short timescale, but it breaks down in the atmosphere more quickly.

cards.front: The lesson gives six factors that shift the supply curve to the RIGHT (increase supply). What are they?
cards.answer: Costs fall / Technology improves / A subsidy is granted / More firms enter the market / Productivity rises / Weather is favourable (for agricultural goods)

cards.front: The lesson gives four factors that shift the supply curve to the LEFT (decrease supply). What are they?
cards.answer: Costs rise / A tax is imposed / Firms leave the market / Bad weather destroys a harvest

cards.front: Why does the supply curve shift right when new firms enter a market?
cards.answer: New producers add their output to the market, so total market supply increases at every price.

cards.front: How does higher productivity shift the supply curve to the right?
cards.answer: Each unit of output needs fewer inputs, lowering unit costs, so firms can supply more at every price.

cards.front: Name the three London locations at the centre of Pip's life there.
cards.answer: Jaggers's office (near Newgate and Smithfield) / Barnard's Inn / The Finches of the Grove

cards.front: Name the three settings the River Thames connects in the novel.
cards.answer: The Kent marshes / London / The open sea of potential escape
items: The open sea of potential escape

cards.front: How does Estella leading Pip through Satis House by candlelight foreshadow her role in his life?
cards.answer: A beautiful girl leading a boy through darkness symbolises how Estella will lead Pip through years of emotional darkness.

cards.front: How does the decay inside Satis House foreshadow Miss Havisham's death?
cards.answer: The darkness, cobwebs and rot foreshadow her death by fire, so the house only 'comes alive' through destruction.

title: Descriptive Statistics, Graphs, Reliability and Validity
subject: psychology-ocr

cards.front: Name the five types of chart or graph the lesson describes for displaying data.
cards.answer: Bar chart / Pie chart / Histogram / Line graph / Scatter diagram

cards.front: Name the three measures of central tendency covered in the lesson.
cards.answer: Mean / Median / Mode

cards.front: Why does the normal distribution matter to psychologists?
cards.answer: It gives a benchmark for whether a score is typical or unusual, and many statistical tests assume data is normally distributed.

cards.front: Why is the mode the only measure of central tendency that works with categorical data?
cards.answer: It simply identifies the most frequent value, which works even when data cannot be ordered or added, like favourite colours.

cards.front: Name the four levels of job role in a business hierarchy described in the lesson.
cards.answer: Directors / Senior managers / Supervisors or team leaders / Operational and support staff

cards.front: Name the four ways the lesson says a business can advertise a role externally.
cards.answer: Agencies / Job boards / University careers fairs / Social media

cards.front: Why is poor recruitment expensive for a business?
cards.answer: Advertising costs money, interviewing takes management time, and hiring the wrong person means retraining or restarting the process.

cards.front: Why does training increase employee retention?
cards.answer: Employees who feel they are developing their skills are more likely to stay because they see a future with the business.

title: The Schlieffen Plan and the Battle of the Marne
subject: history-aqa

cards.front: What three gambles did the Schlieffen Plan require Germany to take?
cards.answer: Violate Belgian and Dutch neutrality / Assume France would attack into the trap on the border / Bet Russia would not mobilise faster than expected
items: Assume France would attack into the trap on the border
Bet Russia would not mobilise faster than expected

cards.front: Name the three connected reasons the lesson gives for why the Schlieffen Plan failed.
cards.answer: Belgian resistance at Liège cost critical days / Russia mobilised faster than expected / Joffre's counter-attack at the Marne drove back the German right wing
items: Belgian resistance at Liège cost critical days
Joffre's counter-attack at the Marne drove back the German right wing

cards.front: Why did Schlieffen plan to put roughly seven-eighths of the German army on the right wing?
cards.answer: So it could sweep through Belgium and the Netherlands, pivot south, and encircle Paris from the west.

cards.front: Why was the German army exposed to Joffre's counter-attack by early September 1914?
cards.answer: The over-extended right wing was weakened, troops were exhausted from forced marches, and supply lines were stretched, leaving a gap between armies.

cards.front: Name the five things you must be able to do in a restaurant role-play, according to the lesson.
cards.answer: Make a reservation / Order food and drink / Ask questions / Make a complaint / Pay the bill

cards.front: Give the four forms of the partitive article in French and when each is used.
cards.answer: du - before masculine nouns / de la - before feminine nouns / de l' - before vowels/silent h / des - before plurals

cards.front: How does a partitive article change when the sentence is made negative, e.g. 'Je ne mange pas ___ fromage'?
cards.answer: After a negative, all partitive articles change to de (or d' before a vowel).

cards.front: In the restaurant role-play, why is it important to use structures like Est-ce que, Qu'est-ce que or Avez-vous?
cards.answer: One prompt requires asking a question, and forming it well earns full marks for that task.

title: Songs for the People — Frances E. W. Harper
subject: english-literature-ocr

cards.front: Name the four groups Harper's repeated stanza openings ask to make or sing songs for.
cards.answer: The people / The weary / Little children / The poor and aged

cards.front: Name the four anthology poems the lesson compares with 'Songs for the People'.
cards.answer: The Destruction of Sennacherib / Vergissmeinnicht / Thirteen / Flag

cards.front: How does varying the number of unstressed syllables in the ballad stanza help Harper's argument?
cards.answer: It lets lines quicken or slow, shifting the rhythm between urgent and calm to support her case for peace.

cards.front: How does the poem's own musicality support Harper's claim that peace is more powerful than conflict?
cards.answer: The poem sets the harshness and discord of battle against harmonious music, so its sound backs up her argument.

title: The Plains Indians' Way of Life
subject: history-aqa

cards.front: Name the six major Plains nations the lesson names.
cards.answer: Lakota Sioux / Cheyenne / Arapaho / Comanche / Crow / Pawnee

cards.front: What five uses did Plains nations make of the buffalo carcass?
cards.answer: Meat for food / Hide for clothes and tipi covers / Sinew for thread / Bones for tools / Dung for fuel
items: Hide for clothes and tipi covers

cards.front: Why did US officials often misunderstand Plains treaty negotiations?
