cards.front: Why does the lesson argue the 1905 Aliens Act was not a general immigration control?
cards.answer: It exempted wealthy migrants and, in principle, political refugees, showing it specifically targeted poor Eastern European Jewish migrants.

cards.front: Why did Jewish migrants form trade unions like the Hebrew Cabinet Makers' Association?
cards.answer: To organise against the sweated trades' 12-hour days and low piece-rate wages, demanding limits on hours and minimum rates.

cards.front: What are the four class groupings sociologists commonly identify in the UK?
cards.answer: Upper class / Middle class / Working class / Underclass

cards.front: Why did Marx argue the proletariat are exploited by the bourgeoisie?
cards.answer: Because the value workers create through their labour is greater than the wages they receive, and the bourgeoisie keep this surplus value as profit.

cards.front: Why do functionalists like Davis and Moore see class differences as necessary rather than a problem?
cards.answer: Because they reflect differential rewards attached to roles of varying functional importance, which helps society operate efficiently.

title: Schmitt Inverters and Interfacing Analogue to Digital
subject: electronics-eduqas

cards.front: Name the three circuit methods described for converting an analogue signal into a digital logic signal.
cards.answer: Transistor switch / Op-amp comparator / Schmitt inverter

cards.front: What are the three common errors to avoid when reading Schmitt trigger threshold graphs?
cards.answer: Confusing which threshold triggers which transition / Missing the ruler and estimating by eye / Swapping the hysteresis direction
items: Confusing which threshold triggers which transition
Missing the ruler and estimating by eye

cards.front: Why does a standard logic inverter's output flicker rapidly when noise is present near its switching voltage?
cards.answer: It has only one fixed threshold, so any noise crossing that single level repeatedly flips the output HIGH and LOW.

cards.front: Why do transistor switch and comparator interfaces need extra components to match the Schmitt inverter's noise immunity?
cards.answer: They only have a single threshold, so filtering must be added separately, whereas hysteresis gives the Schmitt inverter noise immunity with no extra parts.

title: Sources, Style and the Whole-Theme Answer
subject: latin-eduqas

cards.front: Name the six prescribed pictures set for this theme.
cards.answer: Fresco of meal preparation with carcass and silver vessel / Decorated bronze food warmer / Garum jar from Scaurus's workshop / Fresco of a fruit bowl from Julia Felix's estate / Banquet scene from the House of the Triclinium / Fresco of a politician distributing bread
items: Fresco of meal preparation with carcass and silver vessel
Fresco of a fruit bowl from Julia Felix's estate
Banquet scene from the House of the Triclinium
Fresco of a politician distributing bread

cards.front: Name the three big ideas an extended evaluative response on this theme should connect back to.
cards.answer: Food eaten in wealthy and poorer households / The importance of hospitality / Food as a display of wealth and power
items: Food eaten in wealthy and poorer households
Food as a display of wealth and power

cards.front: How does Petronius's chiasmus describing Trimalchio's gaming pieces reinforce his wealth?
cards.answer: The crossed word order pairs each colour with its precious replacement, showing Trimalchio turns an ordinary game into a display of wealth.

cards.front: How does Martial's line placing mushrooms and pig-fungus together create its effect?
cards.answer: Placing the two foods side by side in the same line makes the gap in status felt in the grammar itself, not just the meaning.

cards.front: What three types of work make up the 'triple shift' that feminist sociologists say women carry out?
cards.answer: Paid work / Domestic labour / Emotional management of family relationships

cards.front: According to Marxist feminists, what four unpaid tasks does women's domestic labour typically involve?
cards.answer: Cooking / Cleaning / Child rearing / Caring for sick and elderly family members
items: Caring for sick and elderly family members

cards.front: Why did Parsons see segregated conjugal roles as functionally efficient for modern industrial society?
cards.answer: Paid employment was geographically mobile, so one adult needed to be free to move while the other maintained the home.

cards.front: How does the principle of stratified diffusion explain the spread of the symmetrical family, according to Willmott and Young?
cards.answer: Lifestyle changes begin among middle-class families and gradually spread down to working-class families.

cards.front: What three predictions does Birling confidently make in Act 1 that history proves wrong?
cards.answer: The Titanic is unsinkable / There will be no war / The future holds nothing but prosperity
items: The future holds nothing but prosperity

cards.front: Name the three things Britain lacked in 1912 that left workers unprotected if they lost their job.
cards.answer: No welfare state / No NHS / No unemployment benefit

cards.front: How does the lighting change in the opening stage directions support Priestley's message?
cards.answer: The lighting shifts from pink and intimate to brighter and harder as the Inspector arrives, symbolising the exposure of the family's hidden secrets.

cards.front: How does the stage direction describing the Birlings' dining room reveal Priestley's criticism of the upper classes?
cards.answer: Details like good solid furniture, champagne and dessert plates show the family living in a comfortable bubble that deliberately shuts out others' suffering.

title: Engineering Maths I — Formulae, Ohm's Law & Mechanical Advantage
subject: engineering-eduqas

cards.front: Name the three elements every lever has, according to the lesson.
cards.answer: Load / Effort / Pivot (fulcrum)

cards.front: Name the three equivalent formulae the lesson gives for electrical power.
cards.answer: P = IV / P = I²R / P = V²/R

cards.front: How does the Ohm's law triangle help you find an unknown quantity?
cards.answer: Write V at the top and I and R at the bottom, then cover the quantity you want to find and read off the remaining operation.

cards.front: Why can a machine still be useful even if its mechanical advantage is less than 1?
cards.answer: It reduces the force needed but increases speed, which is useful for different applications.

cards.front: Name the four finishes given in the lesson for papers and boards.
cards.answer: Varnishing / Hot foil blocking / Embossing / Edge staining

cards.front: Name the three things the lesson says timber needs protecting from.
cards.answer: Moisture / Insects / UV light

cards.front: How does dip coating produce a coating on a metal component?
cards.answer: The heated component is dipped into a fluidised bed of polymer powder, which melts on contact to form a smooth, scratch-resistant coating.

cards.front: Why are polymer finishes mostly aesthetic rather than protective against corrosion?
cards.answer: Polymers do not rust or rot, so their finishes mainly add appearance or specific surface properties instead of protection.

cards.front: The lesson names three of Ambroise Paré's contributions to surgery. What were they?
cards.answer: A salve instead of boiling oil for wounds / Designing artificial limbs / Improved ligation (tying blood vessels) instead of cauterising
items: A salve instead of boiling oil for wounds
Improved ligation (tying blood vessels) instead of cauterising

cards.front: Name the three scanning technologies the lesson says transformed diagnosis without surgery.
cards.answer: X-rays / Ultrasound / MRI

cards.front: Why did Galen's theories go largely unchallenged in medicine for centuries?
cards.answer: The Church backed ancient authority and books were rare before printing, making it dangerous and difficult to challenge his ideas.

cards.front: Why is germ theory seen as a turning point for modern medicine?
cards.answer: It provided the scientific basis for vaccines, antiseptics, antibiotics and the modern understanding of infection.

cards.front: Name the three factors that affect CPU performance.
cards.answer: Clock speed / Number of cores / Cache size

cards.front: During the Execute stage of a Load instruction, what three steps happen in order?
cards.answer: Operand's address placed in the MAR / Data fetched from RAM into the MDR / Data copied from MDR into the ACC
items: Operand's address placed in the MAR
Data fetched from RAM into the MDR
Data copied from MDR into the ACC

cards.front: Why do laptops throttle (reduce) their clock speed when they overheat?
cards.answer: A higher clock speed generates more heat and uses more power, so reducing speed lowers heat output.

cards.front: According to Amdahl's Law, why can adding more cores fail to speed up a program much?
cards.answer: If part of the program must run sequentially, that portion limits the maximum possible speedup no matter how many cores are added.

cards.front: Name the three Reed children who bully Jane at Gateshead.
cards.answer: John / Eliza / Georgiana

cards.front: Name the three things Miss Temple does that show quiet integrity at Lowood.
cards.answer: Feeds hungry students from her own supplies / Clears Jane's name after Brocklehurst's accusation / Treats the girls with genuine kindness
items: Feeds hungry students from her own supplies
Clears Jane's name after Brocklehurst's accusation
Treats the girls with genuine kindness

cards.front: How does Brontë use Brocklehurst to satirise religious hypocrisy?
cards.answer: He preaches Christian austerity to the students while his own wife and daughters dress in silk and velvet.

cards.front: Why does Jane's confrontation with Mrs Reed feel liberating to her?
cards.answer: Speaking out makes her soul 'expand' and 'exult' with freedom, showing rebellion gives her a selfhood submission never could.

cards.front: Name the seven components of a balanced diet.
cards.answer: Carbohydrates / Proteins / Fats / Minerals / Vitamins / Fibre / Water

cards.front: Name the four factors that affect an individual's daily energy requirement.
cards.answer: Age / Gender / Body size / Energy expenditure (exercise levels)

cards.front: Why does the body switch back to carbohydrate as exercise intensity increases, even though fat provides more energy per gram?
cards.answer: Because fat metabolism is too slow to meet the energy demand at higher exercise intensities.

cards.front: Why are female endurance athletes particularly vulnerable to iron deficiency?
cards.answer: Because they lose iron through both menstruation and high training volume combined.

cards.front: Name the five key quotations for Shylock given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Hath not a Jew eyes? / The villainy you teach me I will execute / I would not have given it for a wilderness of monkeys / I will have my bond / I am not well
items: The villainy you teach me I will execute
I would not have given it for a wilderness of monkeys

cards.front: Name the three character foil pairs the lesson identifies.
cards.answer: Shylock (outsider) vs Portia (insider) / Antonio (Christian merchant) vs Shylock (Jewish victim) / Jessica (abandons father) vs Portia (honours father)

cards.front: Why does Jessica's silence for the rest of Act 5 matter?
cards.answer: Surrounded by lovers, she may sense her acceptance by the Christians is conditional and fragile.

cards.front: How does Shakespeare use character foils to affect the audience's judgement of characters?
cards.answer: Contrasts like Shylock and Portia stop the audience siding entirely with anyone, since every virtue is complicated by a flaw.

cards.front: Name the three main factors affecting educational achievement studied in GCSE Sociology.
cards.answer: Social class / Gender / Ethnicity

cards.front: Name the four examples of material deprivation the lesson gives for working-class pupils.
cards.answer: Overcrowded housing with no quiet study space / Inability to afford uniforms or equipment / Needing part-time jobs that reduce study time / Parents unable to pay for tuition or educational visits
items: Overcrowded housing with no quiet study space
Inability to afford uniforms or equipment
Needing part-time jobs that reduce study time
Parents unable to pay for tuition or educational visits

cards.front: How does cultural capital give middle-class children an advantage at school?
cards.answer: They already know how to speak to teachers, present work, and use cultural references schools value, unlike working-class children.

cards.front: Why has the gender gap in achievement reversed since the 1990s, with girls now outperforming boys?
cards.answer: Girls' rising aspirations, the decline of traditionally male industries, and curriculum changes away from male-dominated content improved girls' performance.

title: Crime Drama: Trigger Point and The Sweeney
subject: media-studies-eduqas

cards.front: Name the four contexts the set episode of Trigger Point reflects.
cards.answer: Changing gender roles / Evolving representations of masculinity / Greater multiculturalism than earlier crime dramas / The growing role of technology in society
items: Greater multiculturalism than earlier crime dramas
The growing role of technology in society

cards.front: Name the four characters the lesson identifies as reversing or reinforcing stereotypes in Trigger Point.
cards.answer: Lana, competent female lead / Hassan, British Asian Muslim officer fighting terrorism / Danny, trusted Black colleague / John Hudson, racist officer shown negatively
items: Hassan, British Asian Muslim officer fighting terrorism
John Hudson, racist officer shown negatively

cards.front: How does ITV, as a commercial broadcaster, fund Trigger Point?
cards.answer: Through advertising revenue from linear ITV and the free streaming service ITVX, plus sponsorship such as Domino's.

cards.front: Why was casting Vicky McClure a way of balancing the risk of hiring a new writer for Trigger Point?
cards.answer: She brought an existing fanbase from Line of Duty and This is England, offsetting the risk of using an unestablished writer.

title: Mindset and Praise: Dweck and Gunderson
subject: psychology-edexcel

cards.front: Why does process praise encourage a growth mindset, according to Dweck's theory?
cards.answer: It teaches the child that success comes from effort and strategy, not from a fixed inborn quality.

cards.front: Why does person praise encourage a fixed mindset, according to Dweck's theory?
cards.answer: It teaches the child that success comes from an inborn quality, which can just as easily be lost.

cards.front: Name the three examples of exothermic reactions given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Combustion reactions / Neutralisation reactions between acids and bases / Oxidation reactions
items: Neutralisation reactions between acids and bases

cards.front: Name the three practical applications of exothermic reactions given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Heating systems / Self-heating food containers / Rocket fuels

cards.front: Why does an exothermic reaction release energy overall?
cards.answer: Because more energy is released when new bonds form than is needed to break the original bonds.

cards.front: Why does an endothermic reaction absorb energy overall?
cards.answer: Because more energy is needed to break the original bonds than is released when new bonds form.

title: Hitler's Aims and Early Foreign Policy 1933-1934
subject: history-aqa

cards.front: Name the four restrictions the Treaty of Versailles placed on Germany that Hitler wanted to tear up.
cards.answer: Lost about 13% of its territory / Army limited to 100,000 men / Tanks and submarines banned / Union with Austria forbidden

cards.front: Name the three reasons the lesson gives for why the Dollfuss Affair mattered.
cards.answer: Showed Hitler would interfere in a neighbour's politics / Showed he would back down against a great power / Set up the paradox that Mussolini later helped Anschluss
items: Showed Hitler would interfere in a neighbour's politics
Showed he would back down against a great power
Set up the paradox that Mussolini later helped Anschluss

cards.front: How did Hitler's three foreign-policy aims reinforce each other, according to the lesson?
cards.answer: Tearing up Versailles enabled pan-German union, which pushed borders eastward, making Lebensraum easier, while anti-communism justified action against the USSR.

cards.front: Why did Britain and France not challenge Hitler over leaving the League or over the German-Polish pact in 1933-34?
cards.answer: Both moves fitted their wider hope that a satisfied Germany would settle down peacefully.

cards.front: Name the six items that make up Jacob Marley's chain.
cards.answer: Cash-boxes / Keys / Padlocks / Ledgers / Deeds / Heavy purses

cards.front: Name the three Ghosts that visit Scrooge and what each represents.
cards.answer: Ghost of Christmas Past - ethereal, light-filled (truth/memory) / Ghost of Christmas Present - warm, abundant (generosity/community) / Ghost of Christmas Yet to Come - silent, dark (death/consequence)
items: Ghost of Christmas Past - ethereal, light-filled (truth/memory)
Ghost of Christmas Present - warm, abundant (generosity/community)
Ghost of Christmas Yet to Come - silent, dark (death/consequence)

cards.front: Why does Dickens have Belle use the word 'idol' when describing Scrooge's love of money?
cards.answer: It suggests Scrooge's worship of money is a form of blasphemy, replacing genuine human love with a false god.

cards.front: Why does Marley warn Scrooge 'I wear the chain I forged in life'?
cards.answer: It implies Scrooge is building an identical chain of selfish acts and will share Marley's fate unless he changes.

cards.front: Name three examples of signs of disease that a practitioner can observe or measure.
cards.answer: A rash / An elevated white blood cell count / A raised temperature
items: An elevated white blood cell count

cards.front: Name three examples of symptoms a patient might report with a disease.
cards.answer: Pain / Breathlessness / Nausea

cards.front: Why might a practitioner who only responds when disease is confirmed fail to support a patient?
cards.answer: A person may feel exhausted, anxious and unable to cope and deserves support even if blood tests come back clear.

cards.front: Why is the WHO's use of the word 'complete' in its health definition seen as a problem?
cards.answer: It sets a very high standard of total physical, mental and social well-being that some argue is rarely achievable in practice.

title: The Trinity, Creation and the Incarnation
subject: religious-studies-edexcel

cards.front: Name the three distinct roles Christians give to the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit in the Trinity.
cards.answer: Father: creator and sustainer of the universe / Son: took human form to reveal God and bring salvation / Holy Spirit: active presence guiding and empowering believers today
items: Father: creator and sustainer of the universe
Son: took human form to reveal God and bring salvation
Holy Spirit: active presence guiding and empowering believers today

cards.front: What three things does the lesson say the incarnation shows Christians today?
cards.answer: Reveals what God is like in human terms / Demonstrates God's love / Shows Jesus can identify with human suffering and weakness
items: Reveals what God is like in human terms
Shows Jesus can identify with human suffering and weakness

cards.front: How did the Filioque clause contribute to the Great Schism of 1054?
cards.answer: Western churches added 'and the Son' to the Spirit's procession, which Eastern Orthodox churches rejected as an unauthorised addition to the Creed.

cards.front: Why do Islam and Judaism reject the Christian doctrine of the Trinity?
cards.answer: They affirm strict monotheism and see the Trinity as incompatible with the belief that God is one.

cards.front: Name the four sub-cellular structures found in animal cells.
cards.answer: Nucleus / Cell membrane / Mitochondria / Ribosomes

cards.front: Name the three additional structures found in plant cells that animal cells don't have.
cards.answer: Cell wall / Chloroplasts / Vacuole

cards.front: Why does the egg cell's membrane change structure after fertilisation?
cards.answer: To prevent more than one sperm entering, keeping the correct chromosome number.

cards.front: Why do sperm cells contain many mitochondria in their middle section?
cards.answer: To provide the energy needed for the tail to swim towards the egg.

cards.front: Name the three things a stress–strain curve from a tensile test shows.
cards.answer: Elastic limit / Yield point / Ultimate tensile strength

cards.front: Name the three tests described for checking malleability, ductility and elasticity.
cards.answer: Malleability test (hammering/rolling) / Ductility test (bend test) / Elasticity test (load and release)

cards.front: How is tensile strength calculated from a tensile test?
cards.answer: The maximum force sustained before fracture is divided by the original cross-sectional area of the sample.

cards.front: Why is electrical conductivity testing classed as non-destructive?
cards.answer: Passing a known current through the sample and measuring voltage does not damage it, so it stays usable afterward.

title: Technology of warfare: medieval to industrial
subject: history-eduqas

cards.front: Name the three siege devices attackers used to breach medieval castles.
cards.answer: Trebuchets (hurled stones) / Battering rams / Siege towers

cards.front: Name the three castle defence features that emerged in response to siege technology.
cards.answer: Concentric castle walls / Towers for enfilading fire / Improved portcullises

cards.front: Why were early matchlock firearms less useful than artillery in the fifteenth century?
cards.answer: Early muskets were heavy, inaccurate and prone to misfiring in wet conditions, while cannon could immediately demolish medieval stone walls.

cards.front: Why did the rifled musket make traditional cavalry charges far more dangerous?
cards.answer: Its accurate range of over 400 metres, compared to 50-75 metres for smoothbore muskets, let infantry shoot cavalry from much further away.

cards.front: The lesson names four forms that gender discrimination can take. What are they?
cards.answer: Exclusion from religious leadership / Unequal pay / Restricted freedom of movement / Differential expectations in family life

cards.front: Which three historical movements does the lesson give as examples of religion's contribution to equality campaigns?
cards.answer: The abolitionist movement (Quakers and evangelicals) / The American civil rights movement (Black church traditions, MLK) / Archbishop Tutu's anti-apartheid work
items: The American civil rights movement (Black church traditions, MLK)

cards.front: Why did critics argue that the TRC's amnesty approach was unfair to victims?
cards.answer: Because granting amnesty instead of pursuing prosecution left victims without adequate redress for the crimes committed against them.

cards.front: How does the humanist 'argument from consistency' justify equality between men and women?
cards.answer: It says there is no morally relevant difference between men and women that would justify giving them different rights or opportunities.

cards.front: The lesson gives four reasons Puritans opposed the London theatres. What are they?
cards.answer: Crowds spread plague / Boys playing women's parts encouraged immorality / Pickpockets and prostitutes worked the audiences / Plays distracted apprentices from their work
items: Boys playing women's parts encouraged immorality
Pickpockets and prostitutes worked the audiences
Plays distracted apprentices from their work

cards.front: Name the five upper-class leisure pursuits the lesson lists.
cards.answer: Hunting / Hawking / Real tennis / Fencing / Bowls

cards.front: Why does the lesson argue that Elizabethan England was not a fully literate society despite the growth of grammar schools?
cards.answer: Schooling was concentrated on noble and gentry boys, so by 1588 only about 30% of men and far fewer women could sign their name.

cards.front: How did Elizabeth's own attitude help keep London's theatres open despite Puritan pressure?
cards.answer: She enjoyed plays at court, and her favour through the licensing system protected the theatres from Puritan attempts to close them.

cards.front: What are the three main groups of causes of uneven development?
cards.answer: Physical (climate, location, hazards) / Economic (trade and debt) / Historical (colonialism, conflict)

cards.front: What five push factors does the lesson give for international migration?
cards.answer: Unemployment / Low wages / Conflict / Drought / Poor public services

cards.front: How do trade rules lock poorer countries into low-value exports?
cards.answer: Rich countries charge low tariffs on raw materials like cocoa beans but high tariffs on processed goods like chocolate, discouraging processing at home.

cards.front: Why does colonial border-drawing still cause problems in Africa today?
cards.answer: Colonial powers drew borders without regard for ethnic groups, and this still fuels tension across much of Africa today.

title: Early Challenges: Versailles, Spartacists & the Kapp Putsch
subject: history-edexcel

cards.front: The lesson gives five reasons why the Treaty of Versailles was so unpopular in Germany. What were they?
cards.answer: Germany was not allowed to negotiate the terms / The War Guilt Clause was hated / Reparations threatened to cripple the economy / Military restrictions humiliated the nation / Loss of territory divided German-speaking people
items: Germany was not allowed to negotiate the terms
The War Guilt Clause was hated
Reparations threatened to cripple the economy
Loss of territory divided German-speaking people

cards.front: The lesson uses the mnemonic LAMB for the key terms of the Treaty of Versailles. What does each letter stand for?
cards.answer: Land - loss of territory / Army - military restrictions / Money - reparations / Blame - the War Guilt Clause

cards.front: Why did the 'stab in the back' myth damage the Weimar Republic?
cards.answer: It linked the new democratic government with betrayal and defeat, allowing right-wing groups to attack the Republic throughout the 1920s.

cards.front: Why did Ebert's government risk using the Freikorps to crush the Spartacist uprising?
cards.answer: The regular army was limited to 100,000 men by Versailles and was too small to deal with the uprising alone.

cards.front: Name the four traditional functions the lesson says have been transferred from the family to external institutions.
cards.answer: Economic production / Religious instruction / Health care / Education

cards.front: Name the four forms of harm the lesson says are more likely to occur within families than between strangers.
cards.answer: Domestic violence / Emotional abuse / Child neglect / Financial exploitation

cards.front: Why does the New Right argue that growing family diversity increases dysfunctional families?
cards.answer: They argue the growth of lone parent families and cohabitation has increased the prevalence of dysfunctional families and related social problems.

cards.front: Why do feminists reject the New Right's claim that lone-parent families are dysfunctional?
cards.answer: It pathologises lone parent families without recognising structural causes of their difficulties, such as poverty, lack of affordable childcare and the gender pay gap.

cards.front: Name the three things Silas loses at Lantern Yard, according to the lesson's key fact.
cards.answer: His faith in God / His trust in people / His fiancée Sarah

cards.front: Name the three reasons the villagers of Raveloe regard Silas with suspicion.
cards.answer: He is a stranger / He is a weaver, an unusual occupation / He is rumoured to have strange powers
items: He is a weaver, an unusual occupation
He is rumoured to have strange powers

cards.front: Why does Silas turn to gold after the events at Lantern Yard?
cards.answer: Having lost his faith, trust in people, and his fiancée simultaneously, he transfers all emotional energy onto gold as a substitute for human connection.

cards.front: How does Silas's loom relate to his hoarding of gold?
cards.answer: The loom's rhythmic, mindless weaving mirrors the repetitive counting of coins, both substituting for genuine human connection.

cards.front: Name the three main types of medical practitioner in medieval England.
cards.answer: Physicians / Apothecaries / Barber surgeons

cards.front: Name the four humours in the Theory of the Four Humours.
cards.answer: Blood / Yellow bile / Black bile / Phlegm

cards.front: Why were supernatural and religious beliefs about disease so widespread in medieval England?
cards.answer: The Church controlled education and hospitals, discouraged dissection, and taught illness was God's will, so no alternative explanations existed.

cards.front: How did miasma theory accidentally lead to public health improvements even though it was wrong?
cards.answer: Believing bad smells caused disease led towns to clean streets, remove waste and drain marshes, which improved sanitation and reduced infection.

cards.front: Name the five main data types described in the lesson.
cards.answer: Alphanumeric / Boolean / Date / Numeric / Text

cards.front: Name the four numeric sub-types given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Integer / Real or decimal / Currency / Percentage

cards.front: Why does a validation rule accept an age entered as 25 when the person is actually 30?
cards.answer: Validation only checks that data is a plausible, correctly formatted value, not whether it is factually true, so an incorrect but reasonable age passes.

cards.front: Why must raw numbers like 17, 19 and 22 be processed before they become information?
cards.answer: On their own the numbers have no context and mean nothing, so processing (calculating, labelling and adding context) is needed to give them meaning.

title: Communism in Asia: Mao's China and the Korean War
subject: history-aqa

cards.front: Name the three mutual defence treaties the US signed in 1951 as a result of the Korean War.
cards.answer: Treaty with Japan / Treaty with the Philippines / Treaty with the ANZUS countries

cards.front: Name the three UN Security Council resolutions passed in response to the North Korean invasion of 1950.
cards.answer: Resolution 82: condemning the invasion / Resolution 83: calling for armed assistance to South Korea / Resolution 84: authorising a unified UN command under US leadership
items: Resolution 83: calling for armed assistance to South Korea
Resolution 84: authorising a unified UN command under US leadership

cards.front: Why couldn't the Soviet Union veto the UN's response to the North Korean invasion?
cards.answer: The Soviet representative was boycotting the Security Council over its refusal to recognise Mao's government, so Moscow wasn't present to veto.

cards.front: Why did Stalin's death in March 1953 help end the Korean War?
cards.answer: It unblocked stalled negotiations between the two sides, leading to the armistice being signed at Panmunjom in July 1953.

cards.front: Name the four safety precautions the lesson gives for working at rock exposures.
cards.answer: Stay away from undercut cliff faces / Wear a hard hat where rockfall is possible / Don't hammer rock without eye protection / Never work at the base of an unstable face
items: Stay away from undercut cliff faces
Wear a hard hat where rockfall is possible
Don't hammer rock without eye protection
Never work at the base of an unstable face

cards.front: Name the four types of natural outcrop the lesson gives where geologists measure dip and strike.
cards.answer: Cliff faces / Stream banks / Road cuttings / Quarry walls

cards.front: Why do buried rocks bend into folds instead of breaking under tectonic stress?
cards.answer: Deep rocks behave differently from surface rocks, so under extreme tectonic stress they slowly bend rather than break.

cards.front: Why must a compass clinometer be held away from metal objects when taking a reading?
cards.answer: Metal objects such as belt buckles or steel toecap boots can deflect the magnetic needle, giving an inaccurate bearing.

cards.front: The lesson gives three key biographical facts about Dickens used to explain his purpose for writing A Christmas Carol. Name them.
cards.answer: His father was imprisoned for debt / He worked in a factory as a child / He wanted to change conditions for the poor, especially children
items: His father was imprisoned for debt
He worked in a factory as a child
He wanted to change conditions for the poor, especially children

cards.front: Name the three Gothic conventions the lesson says Dickens uses in A Christmas Carol.
cards.answer: Marley's ghost / dark foggy streets / supernatural visitations

cards.front: Why did Dickens decide to write a novella instead of a political pamphlet?
cards.answer: He believed a story could reach people's hearts in a way that statistics never could.

cards.front: How does Dickens contrast wealthy and poor society in his purpose for the novella?
cards.answer: He presented wealthy society as pleasant, ordered and extravagant, contrasted with poor society shown as disordered, barbaric and unhappy.

cards.front: Name the four things a genetic diagram should show.
cards.answer: Parental phenotypes and genotypes / Gametes / A Punnett square / Offspring ratios with probabilities

cards.front: Name the three things mapping the human genome has enabled scientists to do.
cards.answer: Identify genes linked to inherited disorders / Develop genetic tests / Research personalised medicine
items: Identify genes linked to inherited disorders

cards.front: How does meiosis create genetically unique gametes?
cards.answer: Chromosomes are randomly shuffled and sections of DNA are exchanged between chromosomes through crossing over.

cards.front: Why can two organisms with the same genotype have different phenotypes?
cards.answer: Phenotype depends on both the genotype and environmental factors, not genotype alone.

title: Act 2: Gerald and Mrs Birling Exposed
subject: english-literature-edexcel

cards.front: Name the four ways the lesson says Eva was judged and punished by both men and women in Act 2.
cards.answer: Sacked for asking for fair wages / Sacked again for being pretty / Used and abandoned by Gerald / Turned away by Mrs Birling's charity
items: Sacked for asking for fair wages
Turned away by Mrs Birling's charity

cards.front: Name the three things the lesson says Gerald gave Daisy during their affair.
cards.answer: Food / Shelter / Affection

cards.front: Why does Sheila return the engagement ring to Gerald in Act 2?
cards.answer: Because the ring represents a class-and-money alliance rather than genuine love, and she rejects those values, refusing to pretend nothing happened.

cards.front: Why does the Inspector interrogate the characters one at a time?
cards.answer: So they cannot coordinate their stories or deflect blame, gradually revealing secrets and building tension until the trap is sprung.

title: Selling Channels and the Product Lifecycle
subject: cambridge-nationals-enterprise-and-marketing

cards.front: Name the four digital selling channels the lesson describes for start-ups.
cards.answer: E-commerce/own website / Social media marketplaces / Online auction platforms / Downloads and digital products

cards.front: Name the five extension strategies the lesson gives for extending a product's life.
cards.answer: Increased advertising / Price reductions / Adding value / New packaging / Entering new markets

cards.front: Why is cash flow negative during the development stage of the product lifecycle?
cards.answer: The business spends money on research, design and testing but earns nothing yet, as the product isn't ready to sell.

cards.front: Why might an extension strategy fail to revive a product's sales?
cards.answer: If the product is genuinely obsolete and no longer wanted by any customer segment, even a large promotional budget won't work.

title: Market Research: Purpose, Methods and Sources
subject: cambridge-nationals-enterprise-and-marketing

cards.front: Name the six primary research methods a start-up might use.
cards.answer: Observations / Questionnaires / Interviews / Focus groups / Consumer trials / Test marketing

cards.front: Name the four main secondary research sources a start-up entrepreneur is expected to know.
cards.answer: Internal data (past sales) / Competitors' public data / Government publications / Commercial research providers e.g. Mintel

cards.front: Why does test marketing give more reliable data than simply asking customers if they would buy a product?
cards.answer: It generates real purchase data from an actual limited launch, rather than reported intent, which can differ from actual behaviour.

cards.front: Why can a focus group's results be misleading?
cards.answer: One or two dominant voices in the group discussion can skew the overall feedback and opinions gathered.

cards.front: Name the five types of formulations the lesson gives as examples.
cards.answer: Alloys / Paints / Medicines / Fuels / Foods such as sauces and dressings
items: Foods such as sauces and dressings

cards.front: Name the four steps in the crystallisation method to get pure salt crystals.
cards.answer: Heat gently to evaporate until crystals form / Remove from heat and cool slowly / Filter the crystals / Leave to dry
items: Heat gently to evaporate until crystals form
Remove from heat and cool slowly

cards.front: Why does slow cooling in crystallisation produce larger, purer crystals than rapid cooling?
cards.answer: As temperature drops slowly, more solute gradually comes out of solution and grows into larger, purer crystals.

cards.front: Why do different substances end up at different heights on a chromatogram?
cards.answer: They travel at different speeds because each is attracted differently to the mobile phase and the stationary phase.

cards.front: Name the three ways the lesson says Anita treats Meena within their friendship.
cards.answer: Humiliates Meena in front of others / Drops her when more popular friends appear / Uses her when convenient
items: Humiliates Meena in front of others
Drops her when more popular friends appear

cards.front: Name the three ways Meena imitates Anita in the early chapters.
cards.answer: Copies Anita's slang / Imitates her walk / Tries to adopt her attitude

cards.front: Why does Meena envy Anita's home life even though the Kumar house is warmer and more supportive?
cards.answer: Meena is blinded by her desire to belong to the English majority, so she cannot see the love and stability she already has.

cards.front: How does Syal use dramatic irony in Meena's fascination with Anita?
cards.answer: The reader sees Anita's 'freedom' is really the result of parental neglect, while Meena admires it in ignorance, creating humour and pathos.

cards.front: Name the four poems from the Youth and Age cluster that the lesson compares with 'Equilibrium'.
cards.answer: Baby Song by Thom Gunn / Prayer by Zaffar Kunial / Tea With Our Grandmothers by Warsan Shire / Happy Birthday Moon by Raymond Antrobus
items: Tea With Our Grandmothers by Warsan Shire
Happy Birthday Moon by Raymond Antrobus

cards.front: Why does Lola use a simile comparing her grandfather's silence after the naming ceremony to a post-mortem?
cards.answer: It treats the living man as already a corpse, unsettling the reader before the poem's elegiac tone settles.

cards.front: How does the stopwatch metaphor capture her grandfather's decline?
cards.answer: It pictures his life ticking down like time being measured and running out, making mortality feel mechanical and precise.

title: Disease, Pathogens and the Immune Response
subject: separate-sciences-edexcel

cards.front: Name the four main types of pathogen given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Bacteria / Viruses / Fungi / Protists

cards.front: Name the four key steps of aseptic technique described in the lesson.
cards.answer: Sterilising equipment in an autoclave / Working near a Bunsen flame / Flaming the necks of culture vessels / Using sterile pipettes and loops
items: Flaming the necks of culture vessels

cards.front: How does antibiotic resistance develop through natural selection?
cards.answer: Bacteria with random mutations giving resistance survive and reproduce, passing on resistance genes, especially when courses aren't completed.

cards.front: How does vaccination protect against future infection by the same pathogen?
cards.answer: It introduces antigens without causing disease, so the body makes antibodies and memory lymphocytes that respond rapidly if the real pathogen appears.

cards.front: Name the three key short-term effects of exercise described in the lesson.
cards.answer: Heart rate and cardiac output increase / Breathing rate and depth increase / Lactate accumulates if intensity exceeds the lactate threshold
items: Heart rate and cardiac output increase
Lactate accumulates if intensity exceeds the lactate threshold

cards.front: During EPOC, what four things does the extra oxygen consumed get used for?
cards.answer: Break down lactic acid / Restore muscle glycogen / Replenish oxygen stores in haemoglobin and myoglobin / Return body temperature and heart rate to resting values
items: Replenish oxygen stores in haemoglobin and myoglobin
Return body temperature and heart rate to resting values

cards.front: Why is it important that breathing depth increases as well as rate during exercise?
cards.answer: Increasing rate alone would move air only in the dead space (trachea/bronchi); increasing depth ensures air reaches the alveoli for gas exchange.

cards.front: How does increased venous return during exercise lead to a greater stroke volume?
cards.answer: The muscle pump squeezes blood back to the heart faster, stretching the ventricles so they contract more forcefully and eject more blood per beat.

cards.front: Name the four main UK exports the lesson gives.
cards.answer: Financial and professional services / Pharmaceuticals / Aerospace equipment / Motor vehicles

cards.front: Name the four main UK imports the lesson gives.
cards.answer: Manufactured goods / Fuels / Foodstuffs / Electronic components

cards.front: Why can a persistent trade deficit be a concern for a government?
cards.answer: It means the country spends more on foreign goods than it earns abroad, which may pressure the currency down and hurt domestic jobs.

cards.front: How does a rise in UK interest rates cause the pound to appreciate?
cards.answer: Higher interest rates attract foreign investors who must first buy pounds, raising demand for pounds and pushing the exchange rate up.

cards.front: Name the three factors the lesson gives that cause an outward shift of the PPF.
cards.answer: More resources (workforce, natural resources, capital stock) / Better technology / Improved education and training
items: More resources (workforce, natural resources, capital stock)

cards.front: Name the three causes the lesson gives for an inward shift of the PPF.
cards.answer: A natural disaster / A war / A major workforce illness

cards.front: Why is a point outside the PPF currently unachievable?
cards.answer: It would require more resources or better technology than the economy currently has.

cards.front: Why do developing economies face an acute dilemma between producing capital goods and consumer goods?
cards.answer: They need capital investment to grow, but their populations also have immediate consumption needs.

title: Traditional Music: The Four Styles You Must Recognise
subject: music-aqa

cards.front: Name the four traditional music styles you must be able to recognise from a short unheard extract.
cards.answer: Blues, 1920 to 1950 / Fusion with African and/or Caribbean music / Contemporary Latin music / Contemporary folk music of the British Isles
items: Fusion with African and/or Caribbean music
Contemporary folk music of the British Isles

cards.front: Besides the twelve-bar chord pattern, name the three other features that give away blues from 1920 to 1950.
cards.answer: Swung rhythm / Call and response / Blue notes

cards.front: Why do jigs and other folk dance tunes have their characteristic bounce?
cards.answer: Because they move in compound time, with the beat dividing into three rather than two.

cards.front: Why do reggae and ska have their characteristic lift?
cards.answer: Because in Caribbean-influenced styles the chords land on the offbeat.

title: Poverty, vagrancy and the Elizabethan Poor Laws
subject: history-aqa

cards.front: Name the four main drivers of Elizabethan poverty given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Population rise from 3 million to 4 million / Sharp inflation in food prices / Enclosure of common land for sheep farming / Bad harvests in crisis years
items: Population rise from 3 million to 4 million
Enclosure of common land for sheep farming

cards.front: Name the three separate London institutions set up to deal with different groups of poor.
cards.answer: Bridewell for idle vagrants / Bethlem for the mentally ill / Christ's Hospital for orphaned children

cards.front: Why did returning soldiers add to the poverty problem from the 1580s?
cards.answer: War with Spain sent thousands of soldiers home with no land, wages or health, and unpaid Armada veterans often turned to begging.

cards.front: Why did fear of disorder matter more than charity in driving government action against the poor?
cards.answer: Officials worried hunger could spark riots, like the Oxfordshire Rising of 1596, making public order a bigger concern than helping the poor.

cards.front: Name the three emotions the lesson says Dickens manipulated in readers to make his argument hit harder.
cards.answer: Fear / Pity / Joy

cards.front: Why did Dickens choose Christmas as the setting for the novella?
cards.answer: Because people were already thinking about generosity at Christmas, so the season amplifies his message rather than being decorative.

cards.front: Why did Dickens include Tiny Tim and the allegorical children Ignorance and Want?
cards.answer: To make wealthy readers see the human cost of their indifference to poverty.

cards.front: Name the four elements of the PEA+ method for analysing language in the extract task.
cards.answer: Point (what Syal does) / Evidence (quotation) / Analysis (how language works and its effect) / Plus (link to character, theme or context)
items: Analysis (how language works and its effect)
Plus (link to character, theme or context)

cards.front: Name the three levels at which racism operates in Anita and Me.
cards.answer: Overt racism / Casual racism / Structural racism

cards.front: How does the closing of Tollington's mines fuel racism against the Kumars?
cards.answer: Job losses created frustration and anger, feeding the false logic that immigrants must be taking scarce jobs.

cards.front: Why does Nanima's visit matter for Meena's sense of identity?
cards.answer: It shows Meena that her heritage's stories and traditions give her roots far deeper than Tollington, connecting her to something ancient.

title: Impact of the First World War on Germany
subject: history-aqa

cards.front: Name the three foreign food sources the lesson says the Allied blockade cut off from Germany.
cards.answer: Fertiliser from Chile / Grain from Russia / Dairy from Denmark

cards.front: According to the Key Fact, what three things exposed the gap between elite war aims and working-class suffering, breaking the Burgfrieden?
cards.answer: Stalemate / Hunger / Casualties

cards.front: Why did the Allied blockade cause mass starvation inside Germany?
cards.answer: It cut off the third of Germany's food imports while the army also requisitioned farm horses, men and machinery, collapsing rations to about 1,000 calories.

cards.front: How did Ludendorff's own actions in autumn 1918 help create the 'stab in the back' myth?
cards.answer: He privately told the Kaiser the war was lost, then insisted civilian politicians sign the armistice so the army's reputation stayed untouched and blame fell elsewhere.

cards.front: Name the four common addition polymers given in the lesson, each with one everyday use.
cards.answer: Poly(ethene) - plastic bags, bottles, packaging / Poly(propene) - ropes, carpets, food containers / PVC - window frames, pipes, flooring / PTFE - non-stick coatings on pans

cards.front: Name the four natural polymers the lesson gives as examples formed by condensation polymerisation.
cards.answer: Proteins / DNA / Starch / Cellulose

cards.front: How can you tell from a polymer's backbone structure whether it is an addition or condensation polymer?
cards.answer: A backbone with only C-C bonds is an addition polymer; one containing ester or amide links is a condensation polymer.

cards.front: Why are amino acids able to join together by condensation reactions to form proteins?
cards.answer: Each amino acid has both an amine group and a carboxyl group, letting them link via peptide bonds while releasing water.

cards.front: Name the three wires in a UK three-pin plug, with their colours.
cards.answer: Live (brown) / Neutral (blue) / Earth (green and yellow)

cards.front: Name the three biggest energy-consuming categories in a typical home, in order from biggest.
cards.answer: Heating and hot water / Cooking / Refrigeration and lighting

cards.front: Why is AC used for the UK mains supply rather than DC?
cards.answer: Because AC voltage can be easily changed using transformers, which is essential for the National Grid.

cards.front: How does a residual current device (RCD) protect against faults faster than a fuse?
cards.answer: It detects tiny imbalances between live and neutral currents and cuts the circuit within milliseconds.

cards.front: Name the four citizenship values the lesson says sit at the heart of migration debates.
cards.answer: Human rights / National sovereignty / Equality / Social cohesion

cards.front: Name the three groups the lesson gives as migrants to the UK in earlier centuries, before the Second World War.
cards.answer: Huguenot refugees from France / Jewish communities fleeing persecution in Eastern Europe / Irish workers seeking employment
items: Jewish communities fleeing persecution in Eastern Europe

cards.front: How does immigration help offset the effects of an ageing population?
cards.answer: It brings in younger workers who help support public pension and healthcare systems.

cards.front: Why might very rapid migration make integration harder, according to the lesson?
cards.answer: It can be harder for communities to build the shared understanding and civic ties needed for a diverse society to function well.

cards.front: After 24 weeks, name the three cases in which abortion is still allowed in England, Scotland and Wales.
cards.answer: Mother's life is at risk / Needed to prevent grave permanent injury to her physical or mental health / The foetus has a severe abnormality
items: Needed to prevent grave permanent injury to her physical or mental health
The foetus has a severe abnormality

cards.front: Name the three types of euthanasia described in the lesson.
cards.answer: Voluntary euthanasia / Non-voluntary euthanasia / Assisted suicide

cards.front: Why does belief in an afterlife make religious believers oppose euthanasia?
cards.answer: If life is preparation for eternity, cutting it short may have spiritual consequences and go against God's plan.

cards.front: Why does the Church of England sometimes accept abortion despite generally opposing it?
cards.answer: They allow it with compassion in cases like risk to the mother's life, severe foetal abnormality, or rape.

cards.front: Name the six changes of state given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Melting / Freezing / Evaporation / Boiling / Condensation / Sublimation

cards.front: Name the four insulation methods the lesson gives for reducing heat loss from a house.
cards.answer: Cavity wall insulation / Loft insulation / Double glazing / Draught excluders

cards.front: Why does temperature stay constant during a change of state even though energy is still being transferred in?
cards.answer: The energy goes into increasing potential energy by breaking bonds between particles, not into increasing kinetic energy, so temperature doesn't rise.

cards.front: Why is the Kelvin scale used instead of Celsius when relating temperature to particle kinetic energy?
cards.answer: Kelvin starts at absolute zero where particle motion stops, so it's directly proportional to kinetic energy, unlike Celsius.

cards.front: Name the four things the lesson says happen after a French wedding ceremony.
cards.answer: a meal (le repas) / speeches (les discours) / music / dancing

cards.front: Name the four time expressions the lesson gives for describing a French wedding.
cards.answer: avant la cérémonie / pendant le repas / après les discours / jusqu'à minuit

cards.front: Why has la bise become less common for some French people?
cards.answer: Since COVID-19, some French people have moved away from doing la bise, though it remains an important cultural tradition.

cards.front: How do you position a direct object pronoun when there is an infinitive in the sentence?
cards.answer: The pronoun goes before the infinitive instead of before the conjugated verb.

title: Shabbat, Home Worship and Sacred Texts
subject: religious-studies-aqa

cards.front: What are the five key elements of Shabbat home observance named in the lesson?
cards.answer: Candle lighting / Kiddush / Challah / Synagogue service / Havdalah

cards.front: Name the three daily prayers observant Jews say, in order.
cards.answer: Shacharit (morning) / Mincha (afternoon) / Ma'ariv (evening)

cards.front: Why does the woman of the household light at least two candles on Friday evening?
cards.answer: The two candles symbolise the two aspects of Shabbat: remembering (zachor) and keeping (shamor).

cards.front: Why is the Torah seen as the most authoritative section of the Tenakh?
cards.answer: It is believed to have been directly revealed by God to Moses at Sinai, and is the source of the 613 mitzvot.

cards.front: Name the three selfless actions that prove Darcy's transformation.
cards.answer: Welcoming the Gardiners at Pemberley / Paying Wickham's debts / Arranging Lydia's marriage without seeking credit
items: Arranging Lydia's marriage without seeking credit

cards.front: Name the four contrasting marriages compared in the novel's resolution.
cards.answer: Charlotte and Collins / Lydia and Wickham / Jane and Bingley / Elizabeth and Darcy

cards.front: Why is Mr Bennet's failure to control Lydia called his greatest parental failure?
cards.answer: His detached, ironic parenting style had real consequences, allowing Lydia's reckless elopement that threatened the whole family's reputation.

cards.front: How did Lady Catherine's intervention ironically help Darcy and Elizabeth?
cards.answer: Her report of Elizabeth's defiant refusal to yield encouraged Darcy to propose to Elizabeth again.

cards.front: Why does Napoleon cut off the hens' food rations during their rebellion?
cards.answer: To punish the hens for refusing to surrender their eggs and force them back into obedience, showing the regime starves its own citizens to control them.

cards.front: How does Napoleon respond to the destruction of the windmill in the Battle of the Windmill?
cards.answer: He declares it a 'great victory,' supported by Squealer's propaganda, showing how totalitarian leaders reframe catastrophic defeats as triumphs.

cards.front: Name the three main branches of the UK government.
cards.answer: Legislature / Executive / Judiciary

cards.front: What three ceremonial roles does the monarch play in government?
cards.answer: Formally opens Parliament / Gives royal assent to Bills / Invites the PM to form a government
items: Invites the PM to form a government

cards.front: Why is the British constitution described as flexible?
cards.answer: It mixes written laws, historical documents and unwritten conventions, so Parliament can change it simply by passing a new Act.

cards.front: Why can't courts strike down an Act of Parliament in the UK?
cards.answer: Because Parliament is sovereign, holding supreme power to make and unmake any law, which no other body can overrule.

title: Expansion in India: Company to Crown
subject: history-aqa

cards.front: Name the four deeper causes of the 1857 Rebellion given in the lesson, besides the greased cartridges trigger.
cards.answer: Anger at the Doctrine of Lapse / Resentment at evangelical Christian missions / New laws permitting widow remarriage / Annexation of Oudh in 1856
items: Anger at the Doctrine of Lapse

cards.front: Name the three Indian states annexed under Dalhousie's Doctrine of Lapse between 1848 and 1856.
cards.answer: Satara (1848) / Jhansi (1853) / Nagpur (1854)

cards.front: How did Clive's small army defeat the much larger Nawab's forces at Plassey in 1757?
cards.answer: Clive bribed the Nawab's commander Mir Jafar, who held back his forces, letting Clive's 3,000 men beat 50,000.

cards.front: Why was Warren Hastings impeached after returning to Britain in 1785?
cards.answer: He was accused of corruption for extracting huge sums from the Begums of Oudh and Raja of Benares to pay for war.

title: Smuggling and the Limits of British Authority
subject: history-edexcel

cards.front: Name the five types of goods the lesson says were smuggled into the colonies.
cards.answer: Molasses / Tea / Brandy / Wine / Luxury cloth

cards.front: Name the three reasons the lesson gives for why customs collection failed.
cards.answer: Officers were few and underpaid / Juries refused to convict smugglers / Walpole valued colonial markets over enforcement
items: Walpole valued colonial markets over enforcement

cards.front: How did a New England merchant typically evade duties on molasses, according to the lesson?
cards.answer: He bribed the local customs collector with a share of the cargo to falsely certify untaxed French molasses as a legal British import.

cards.front: Why did Walpole tolerate the customs service losing money?
cards.answer: British exports to the colonies grew sharply after 1720, so rising manufactured-goods sales mattered more than lost customs revenue.

cards.front: Name the five types of crime psychologists group criminal behaviour into.
cards.answer: Violent crime / Drug-related crime / Acquisitive crime / Sexual offences / Anti-social offences

cards.front: Why might a theory that explains violent crime fail to explain drug-related crime?
cards.answer: Violent crime may stem from a build-up of frustration, while drug-related crime is often linked to addiction or financial pressure instead.

cards.front: Why do psychologists often use official statistics and self-report studies together?
cards.answer: Official statistics give a large-scale reliable picture but miss unreported crime, while self-report studies reveal hidden offending, so combining both builds a fuller picture.

cards.front: Name the three main types of single-base mutation described in the lesson. (Higher tier)
cards.answer: Substitution / Insertion / Deletion

cards.front: What are the three possible effects a mutation can have on the protein produced by a gene? (Higher tier)
cards.answer: Harmful / Neutral / Beneficial

cards.front: Why does antibiotic resistance spread through a bacterial population once an antibiotic is introduced?
cards.answer: Random resistance mutations already exist; resistant bacteria survive and reproduce while non-resistant ones die, spreading the trait by natural selection.

cards.front: How can a mutation in a non-coding regulatory region contribute to cancer? (Higher tier)
cards.answer: It can silence a tumour-suppressor gene, reducing the amount of protein made so the cell no longer restrains cell division.

title: Context, User Needs and Design Briefs
subject: design-technology-eduqas

cards.front: Name the four primary research methods the lesson gives for designers gathering first-hand information.
cards.answer: Questionnaires and surveys / Interviews / Observation / Analysis of existing products (disassembly)

cards.front: Name the six areas the lesson says design criteria typically cover in a specification.
cards.answer: Function / User needs / Safety / Materials and manufacturing / Aesthetics / Sustainability

cards.front: Why does a design brief deliberately avoid saying what the solution should look like?
cards.answer: It identifies the user and problem but leaves the solution open for the design process to discover.

cards.front: Why might a portable speaker's design specification be updated after early user testing?
cards.answer: Testing can reveal issues, such as a grip depth too narrow for larger hands, so the specification is refined.

title: Staging and Design: The Flat, the Street and the Band
subject: drama-aqa

cards.front: Name the five objects the lesson says do symbolic work across A Taste of Honey.
cards.answer: Flower bulbs / Drink / Hands / Engagement ring / Baby doll

cards.front: What three things does the lesson say every strong design answer for A Taste of Honey must do?
cards.answer: Name a specific moment / Name a specific design element / State the effect on the audience
items: State the effect on the audience

cards.front: Why do sightlines matter when Helen uses direct address?
cards.answer: Every part of the audience needs a clear view of Helen's face during direct address, or the technique loses its force.

cards.front: How does staging configuration change what Helen's direct address can do?
cards.answer: On an end-on stage Helen can address the whole audience as one mass, but on a thrust stage she must turn to sections in turn, making it feel more individually implicated.

cards.front: Name the four limitations of the Florentine Codex as a source for the Nahua perspective, as given in the lesson.
cards.answer: Compiled fifty years after the events / in Spanish colonial conditions / translated and edited by a Spanish friar / informants may have shaped testimony to suit the post-conquest environment
items: Compiled fifty years after the events
Translated and edited by a Spanish friar
Informants may have shaped testimony to suit the post-conquest environment

cards.front: What three things did Cortés's letters to King Charles I emphasise?
cards.answer: Spanish bravery / the justice of the conquest / the need to bring Christianity to the Americas
items: The need to bring Christianity to the Americas

cards.front: Why is Bernal Díaz del Castillo often seen as more reliable than Cortés?
cards.answer: Because he had less to gain from distorting the record than Cortés, who wrote to justify his own expedition.

cards.front: Why do historians debate how far the Nahua voices in the Florentine Codex reflect their true views?
cards.answer: Because Sahagún's aim to convert indigenous people and the changed political context may have shaped what informants said.

cards.front: The lesson gives four reasons why the boarding-school setting works in Never Let Me Go. Name them.
cards.answer: It is enclosed, limiting what the children know / It has authority figures who control information / It is associated with privilege, creating cruel irony / Readers expect enclosed worlds, delaying the horror
items: It is enclosed, limiting what the children know
It has authority figures who control information
It is associated with privilege, creating cruel irony
Readers expect enclosed worlds, delaying the horror

cards.front: What reasons does the lesson give for why the clones in Never Let Me Go don't try to escape?
cards.answer: They have no money / They have no identity documents / They have no knowledge of the outside world / They have internalised their purpose
items: They have no knowledge of the outside world

cards.front: Why does Ishiguro keep the 'normal' humans who benefit from organ donations almost entirely absent from the novel?
cards.answer: By making the clones the most sympathetic characters, he forces readers to confront the ethical questions directly.

cards.front: How does the clones' failure to escape comment on human society more broadly, according to the lesson?
cards.answer: It shows how all humans accept constraining structures like class, work and mortality without questioning them.

title: Establishing Communist Rule and the Korean War, 1949-53
subject: history-edexcel

cards.front: Name the three parallel hierarchies through which power ran in the new People's Republic.
cards.answer: The CCP under Chairman Mao (set policy) / The State Council under Premier Zhou Enlai (ran government) / The People's Liberation Army (loyal to the party)
items: The CCP under Chairman Mao (set policy)
The State Council under Premier Zhou Enlai (ran government)
The People's Liberation Army (loyal to the party)

cards.front: What three things did the Korean War feed at home in China, according to the lesson?
cards.answer: Propaganda (Resist America, Aid Korea campaign) / Repression (campaign against counter-revolutionaries) / Debt (military costs owed to the USSR)
items: Debt (military costs owed to the USSR)

cards.front: How did Mao adapt Marxism-Leninism to fit Chinese conditions?
cards.answer: He made the peasantry the engine of revolution instead of the urban working class, since over 80% of the population worked the land.

cards.front: Why did the Korean War's costs help cause Mao's later break with Khrushchev?
cards.answer: Military costs to the USSR became loans Mao was still repaying in the late 1950s, fuelling resentment and the eventual split.

title: The power of the medieval papacy
subject: history-eduqas

cards.front: Name the four things the medieval Church did in people's daily lives, according to the lesson.
cards.answer: Baptised children at birth / Married couples / Heard confessions / Administered last rites at death

cards.front: What three spiritual benefits could a medieval pilgrimage bring?
cards.answer: Earn an indulgence / Demonstrate penance for sins / Strengthen a Christian's faith

cards.front: Why did bishops and abbots hold power beyond their spiritual roles?
cards.answer: They also held land, which made them feudal lords as well as spiritual figures.

cards.front: Why did reports from Jerusalem in the 1070s alarm Western Christians?
cards.answer: Reports said the Seljuk Turks mistreated pilgrims, desecrated churches, and restricted access to the Holy Sepulchre.

cards.front: Name the four steps in treating waste water (sewage treatment).
cards.answer: Screening / Sedimentation / Biological treatment / Final treatment

cards.front: Name the four stages of a product's life assessed in a life cycle assessment.
cards.answer: Extracting raw materials / Manufacturing and packaging / Use / Disposal

cards.front: How does biological treatment clean the effluent during waste water treatment?
cards.answer: Aerobic bacteria break down the organic matter present in the effluent.

cards.front: How does reverse osmosis produce potable water from sea water?
cards.answer: Sea water is forced through a membrane that blocks salt, letting fresh water through.

cards.front: Name the four precautions given in the lesson for handling radioactive sources.
cards.answer: Keep sources in lead-lined containers / Use tongs to handle sources / Wear protective clothing / Minimise exposure time

cards.front: Name the three practical uses of radiation given in the lesson, one for each type.
cards.answer: Gamma: medical tracers and sterilising equipment / Beta: thickness gauges / Alpha: smoke detectors
items: Gamma: medical tracers and sterilising equipment

cards.front: Why does the atomic number decrease by 2 and the mass number decrease by 4 when a nucleus emits an alpha particle?
cards.answer: Because an alpha particle is made of two protons and two neutrons, which are removed from the nucleus.

cards.front: Why does the atomic number increase by 1 when a nucleus emits a beta particle?
cards.answer: Because a neutron in the nucleus turns into a proton, increasing the atomic number by one while mass number stays the same.

cards.front: Besides Noël, Pâques, la fête nationale and Carnaval de Nice, name the four other notable celebrations the lesson mentions.
cards.answer: la fête des Rois (6th January) / la Chandeleur (2nd February) / la fête de la Musique (21st June) / la Toussaint (1st November)
items: la fête de la Musique (21st June)

cards.front: Name the four things families do on the morning of l'Aïd, according to the lesson's example text.
cards.answer: go to the mosque / pray / share a meal / exchange gifts

cards.front: How does the French Easter tradition explain where chocolate eggs come from?
cards.answer: Church bells are said to fly to Rome on Good Friday and return on Easter Sunday, dropping chocolate eggs in gardens for children.

cards.front: How do French people celebrate la fête nationale on 14th July?
cards.answer: There is a military parade on the Champs-Élysées in Paris, fireworks across the country, and people dance in the streets.

cards.front: Name the six key molecules the lesson gives for drawing dot-and-cross diagrams.
cards.answer: Hydrogen (H2) / Hydrogen chloride (HCl) / Water (H2O) / Methane (CH4) / Oxygen (O2) / Carbon dioxide (CO2)

cards.front: What are the four steps for drawing a dot-and-cross diagram?
cards.answer: Write electronic configuration of each atom / Identify electrons needed to fill outer shell / Draw overlapping outer shells with shared electrons / Check each atom has a full outer shell
items: Write electronic configuration of each atom
Identify electrons needed to fill outer shell
Draw overlapping outer shells with shared electrons
Check each atom has a full outer shell

cards.front: Why is graphite used as a lubricant?
cards.answer: Its layers are held together by weak intermolecular forces, so they can slide over each other easily.

cards.front: Why don't simple molecular substances conduct electricity?
cards.answer: They have no free electrons or ions to carry a charge.

cards.front: Name the four processes that drive coastal erosion.
cards.answer: Hydraulic action / Abrasion / Attrition / Solution

cards.front: Name the four factors that shape UK coastal landscapes.
cards.answer: Wave action / Geology / Climate / Human management

cards.front: Why do many UK spits curve at their end?
cards.answer: Secondary wind directions and tidal currents from the estuary mouth bend the growing end of the spit.

cards.front: Why do salt marshes form behind spits?
cards.answer: A spit shelters the water behind it, so waves lose energy and fine sediment settles, letting salt marsh develop.

title: Religious Experience, Prayer, Design and Cosmological Arguments
subject: religious-studies-edexcel

cards.front: What three explanations do Atheists and Humanists give for apparently answered prayers?
cards.answer: Coincidence / Confirmation bias (noticing hits, forgetting misses) / The natural course of events

cards.front: Name the four different Christian traditions and their approaches to prayer mentioned in the lesson.
cards.answer: Catholics/Anglicans use set, liturgical prayers / Protestants/evangelicals use informal personal prayer / Pentecostal/charismatic Christians report dramatic healings / Quakers practise silent waiting prayer

cards.front: Why did Hume challenge the cosmological argument's claim that 'every event has a cause'?
cards.answer: Because we only ever observe causation within the universe, not the universe as a whole, so the premise can't be proven by observation.

cards.front: Why do many Christians see fine-tuning as evidence for the design argument?
cards.answer: Because even small changes to the universe's physical constants would make life impossible, which seems to point to intentional design.

title: Indian Wars: Little Crow, Sand Creek and Red Cloud
subject: history-edexcel

cards.front: Name the three forts the US Army built along the Bozeman Trail in 1866.
cards.answer: Fort Reno / Fort Phil Kearny / Fort C.F. Smith

cards.front: Name the six Indigenous Plains nations the lesson lists as having distinct languages and separate political histories.
cards.answer: Lakota Sioux / Cheyenne / Arapaho / Comanche / Crow / Pawnee

cards.front: Why did the promises of the 1851 Fort Laramie Treaty collapse within a decade?
cards.answer: Settler pressure, gold rushes and broken supply lines undermined the promised annuities and safe passage.

cards.front: How did the Sand Creek Massacre push Red Cloud towards organised armed resistance?
cards.answer: It showed that peaceful treaty arrangements offered no real protection, pushing younger leaders like Red Cloud towards war.

cards.front: Name the four qualities the lesson gives that make Jekyll the embodiment of a Victorian gentleman.
cards.answer: Educated / Charitable / Sociable / Admired by his peers

cards.front: Name the six named characters analysed in this lesson on the novella.
cards.answer: Dr Henry Jekyll / Mr Edward Hyde / Mr Gabriel John Utterson / Dr Hastie Lanyon / Richard Enfield / Poole

cards.front: Why does witnessing Hyde's transformation into Jekyll destroy Lanyon?
cards.answer: Because it violates the boundaries of mainstream, empirical science he trusted, so the revelation itself effectively kills him.

cards.front: Why is Jekyll unable to get rid of Hyde, despite claiming he can whenever he chooses?
cards.answer: Because Hyde is not a separate person but a part of Jekyll himself, so removing Hyde would mean destroying Jekyll.

title: Context: The Russian Revolution & Orwell's Purpose
subject: english-literature-edexcel

cards.front: Name the three literary levels on which Animal Farm works.
cards.answer: Allegory / Fable / Satire

cards.front: What three causes led to the 1917 Russian revolutions, according to the lesson?
cards.answer: Anger over inequality / Food shortages / Russia's catastrophic losses in World War I
items: Russia's catastrophic losses in World War I

cards.front: Why did Stalin win the power struggle against Trotsky after Lenin's death?
cards.answer: Stalin was a cunning political operator who built alliances behind the scenes, while Trotsky was an intellectual focused on spreading world revolution.

cards.front: How did the withdrawal of Animal Farm by Jonathan Cape prove the point Orwell was making?
cards.answer: It showed that even in a democracy, the Ministry of Information could pressure a publisher to silence uncomfortable truths about a powerful ally.

cards.front: Name the three distinctive features that identified a Roman centurion.
cards.answer: Transverse crest on helmet (crista transversa) / Vine stick (vitis) for authority/punishment / Gladius worn on left hip

cards.front: Name the six types of building found in a typical Roman legionary fortress.
cards.answer: Headquarters building (principia) / Commanding officer's house (praetorium) / Barracks blocks / Granaries / Hospital / Bathhouse

cards.front: Why did a legionary's pay and rewards tie his loyalty directly to his general?
cards.answer: Legionaries received salary, campaign booty and land grants from their commanding general, linking their loyalty to him rather than the state.

cards.front: Why did Roman recruits train using weapons heavier than standard issue?
cards.answer: So that when they used their real, lighter weapons in battle, fighting would feel easier by comparison.

title: Tea With Our Grandmothers — Warsan Shire
subject: english-literature-ocr

cards.front: The lesson says to learn four things about the poem's 'shape' for the exam. Name them.
cards.answer: Two grandmothers / Three languages / A structure that moves between their stories / The phrase 'tally of surviving'
items: A structure that moves between their stories

cards.front: Name the five other poems in the cluster that the lesson compares Tea With Our Grandmothers to.
cards.answer: Holy Thursday / Baby Song / Prayer / Equilibrium / Theme for English B

cards.front: Why does Shire move between three different languages in Tea With Our Grandmothers?
cards.answer: Because diaspora identity means living inside more than one language and culture at once, which she builds directly into her vocabulary.

cards.front: Why does Shire structure the poem around two grandmothers from opposite ends of the world?
cards.answer: To suggest that survival, ageing and being remembered by the young are universal experiences, not limited to one culture or nationality.

cards.front: Name the four Conflict-cluster themes the lesson says 'Papa-T' explores.
cards.answer: Legacy of empire / Colonised family inheriting an imperial poem / Passing of memory between generations / Tension between obedience and disobedience
items: Colonised family inheriting an imperial poem

cards.front: Name the four poems the lesson compares 'Papa-T' with.
cards.answer: The Destruction of Sennacherib / Colonization in Reverse / Flag / Boat Stealing

cards.front: Why does the grandfather's threat of a 'good lickin' keep the poem's tone warm rather than frightening?
cards.answer: Because the discipline of empire is folded into the discipline of a loving grandfather, making the threat affectionate not menacing.

cards.front: How does D'Aguiar's poem 'talk back' to Tennyson's empire poem rather than simply rejecting it?
cards.answer: It absorbs Tennyson's poem and answers it, letting the grandfather's dialect voice remake the sound of the imperial poem from within.

cards.front: Name the four local (non-climate) factors that can affect biome distribution.
cards.answer: Altitude / Soil type / Drainage / Rock type

cards.front: Name the three climate factors that shape biome distribution.
cards.answer: Temperature / Precipitation / Sunshine hours

cards.front: Why do tundra plants manage to flower despite the short growing season?
cards.answer: Arctic summers have 24-hour daylight, giving long sunshine hours that let tundra plants flower briefly.

cards.front: Why does cutting down tropical rainforest slow down its own regrowth?
cards.answer: Fewer trees means less transpiration, which reduces local rainfall, which then slows regrowth of the forest.

cards.front: Why do close objects create greater retinal disparity than distant objects?
cards.answer: Because the eyes are set apart, nearby objects produce a larger difference between the two eye images than distant objects do.

cards.front: Why can artists create a convincing sense of depth on a flat painting using linear perspective, relative size and occlusion?
cards.answer: These monocular cues are properties of the light pattern in the scene itself, so they work without needing two eyes or a real 3D scene.

title: Atman, Samsara and the Purpose of Life
subject: religious-studies-edexcel

cards.front: Name the four stages of life (ashramas) in varnashrama dharma.
cards.answer: Student / Householder / Forest-dweller / Renunciant

cards.front: Name the four realms of rebirth that samsara can span, according to the lesson.
cards.answer: Human / Animal / Divine / Hellish

cards.front: Why does a person remain trapped in samsara according to Hindu teaching?
cards.answer: As long as they are driven by desires, attachments and ignorance, they keep generating karma and stay in the cycle of rebirth.

cards.front: How does the cycle of rebirth end and moksha occur?
